items.statement: North region market growth concern

items.quote: We are getting one incentive in the North, which is for Nimbahera Line 3 and that would only be available in this fiscal.

items.statement: Incentives for Ujjain and Panna

items.statement: IRR for putty expansion

items.statement: Debt to EBITDA target

items.statement: Saifco expansion potential

items.statement: Toshali expansion potential

items.statement: India Q2 CY25 sales grew 7% YoY to INR14.5bn, above weighted average market growth; tractors and trucks healthy, light vehicles and 2-wheelers sluggish below 5%
items.quote: In Q2 C '25, India business sales were at INR14.5 billion, which has grown at 7% year -on-year versus Q2 C '24 and marginally higher on a sequential basis. The growth is also higher than the weighted average market growth.

items.statement: Europe Q2 CY25 sales down 1% YoY to INR8.3bn; real volume drop 4% after 7% FX benefit and raw material price drop; improved vs double-digit declines in prior 3 quarters
items.quote: Sales were at INR8.3 billion, which are down year -on-year by 1%, but that includes a positive exchange rate effect of 7%. Without the effect of raw material prices drop also, the real drop in sales volume in Europe was 4% in Q2 C '25.

items.statement: India Q2 CY25 EBITDA margin 17.5%, marginally lower YoY and sequentially due to product mix; Q1 CY25 reported 18.6% included one-time government grant, underlying ~18%
items.quote: Now the EBITDA margin in India for the quarter was 17.5%, just marginally lower year -on-year and sequentially. This is largely due to product mix issues.

items.statement: Europe Q2 CY25 EBITDA margin 12.5% includes one-time Metalcastello restructuring cost; without it margin would be closer to 15%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in the European business for Q2 C '25 was 12.5%. Now, this includes a onetime restructuring cost at Metalcastello without which the margin would have been closer to 15%.

items.statement: Expect H2 CY25 better than H1 in India due to good monsoon and festive season; Europe H2 normally worse than H1 by ~15% due to seasonality
items.quote: Given the prospects of a good monsoon and the upcoming festive season, we expect H2 to be better than H1 in India.

items.statement: Europe market expected to remain at current weak level for next 1-2 quarters; customers indicate recovery by beginning next year but not certain
items.quote: So let's say that we are now in the valley of the sales, we can expect that the market will continue in this level during the next 1 or 2 quarters, but our customers are already saying us that they expect a certain recovery by beginning next year.

items.statement: New order book INR3.5bn in Q1 CY25, ~INR6bn in H1 CY25; trend continuing, order book healthy
items.quote: At this moment, we are around INR6 billion in the first half of the year. So we continue this trend. So the order book is quite healthy, and we continue getting new businesses from the customers.

items.statement: H1 CY25 growth capex INR0.7bn focused on India projects; expect full year capex close to 5% of revenue guidance as H2 ramps up with new projects
items.quote: We are controlling the capex because of the, let's say, weak situation of the market. But in the second half, we will -- we have a lot of, let's say, new projects, as I mentioned about the new order that we allocated and the capex will revamp. So we will be close to this 5% in the complete year.

items.statement: Europe recurrent EBITDA margin expected around 14-15% even in current market conditions; India margins expected to improve slightly with sales recovery
items.quote: We consider that we can be in a recurrent margins in Europe, around 14% to 15%. That's the -- what we see the future. And regarding -- in India, we expect also to improve slightly the margins in the next quarters, thanks to the growth that we expect.

items.statement: India exports ~12-13% of turnover; growth constrained by US tariff uncertainty; strategy is local-for-local, exports focused on iron castings and gears where capacity limited elsewhere
items.quote: Our export rate is not big. It's around 12%, 13%. That is the export rate that we have. In this moment, these export rates, let's say, that are under certain scrutiny because of the tariffs that are not yet clear.

items.statement: Expect important growth in casting exports to US from beginning of next year; China Plus One not a factor, benefit from technology not developed in US/Europe
items.quote: So we expect to grow importantly in the casting exports in the next, I would say, from the beginning next year, okay? So in that sense, we will have a good opportunity to grow and to grow our exports mainly to the US.

items.statement: INR590cr cash outflow from working capital variation in H1 CY25 due to not doing December discounting with Mahindra in June; will reverse if discounting done in December 2025
items.quote: We did in December discounting with Mahindra, the big customer. We did not do in June, and that's the impact there. It will reverse if we do it again in December '25.

items.statement: New product developments ramping up: 2-wheeler crankshafts for Royal Enfield, common rail, complex inner races, EV gears, aluminum/iron casting products; order book delayed last 1-2 years now getting sorted
items.quote: we were talking about 2 -wheeler crankshafts at CIE Hosur. We are talking about common rail. We are talking about inner races. So these were all new developments that we had done at CIE Hosur, so these we re completely new product developments that we had done

items.statement: Appointed new head of business development, refocusing on anchor customers; weekly reviews with CEOs and business development heads; CEO personally visiting purchasing directors; results expected in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We have started this activity. We have the new business development head working properly and also contacting all the customers. We have a scheduled and weekly review with all the COOs -- sorry, CEOs and the, let's say, business development heads.

items.statement: Completed liquidation of Bill Forge Precision; entity ceased to exist
items.quote: We would like to mention a change in this, where we have completed the formalities of liquidating Bill Forge Precision, and it has ceased to exist.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty and China rare-earth magnet restrictions are key watch-outs for market outlook
items.quote: We'll need to watch out for issues that may have negative impact like the potential tariffs from the US government or the impact of restriction on rare-earth magnets by China.

items.statement: Europe market remains difficult; not 100% sure of turnaround in CY26; continuing restructuring focus at Metalcastello
items.quote: So whether the market will turn or not, we are not 100% sure at this point of time. So we continue to assume that the market in Europe will be difficult, and we will continue to focus on restructuring profitability, etcetera.

items.statement: Metalcastello voluntary dismissal scheme: 30 of 200 workers left in June; temporary layoffs reduced; company better aligned to market conditions
items.quote: In June, 30 people left the company, okay? Now, the total amount of workers in this moment are about 170. We were 200, now 170.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 CY25 sales INR44.9bn (-1% YoY), EBITDA margin 16.3%, EBIT 12.4%, PAT 9.1%
items.quote: On Page 12, we have the H1 C '25 consolidated results of CIE India. Sales were INR44.9 billion, which is marginally lower by 1% versus H1 C '24. The EBITDA margin was 16.3%; EBIT, 12.4%; EBT, 12.1%; and PAT, 9.1%.

items.statement: Dividend payout INR7 per share in H1 CY25; cash outflow INR2.6bn
items.quote: Cash outflow on account of dividend was INR2.6 billion due to the dividend payout of INR7 per share.

items.statement: Europe Q2 sales drop includes 7% positive FX effect from rupee depreciation; raw material price drop also a factor
items.quote: The quarterly sales also improved on a sequential basis. Now, this is because there has been some improvement in the market situation with the Light Vehicles market being down by only 2% in Q2 C '25. The reduced base effect has also played a part in this improvement.

items.statement: Europe seeing consolidation opportunity as many competitors in bad financial shape; customers approaching CIE for sound suppliers; expect to be winners in consolidation
items.quote: The amount of bankruptcies that we are seeing is quite -- it's terrible. I mean, the companies are suffering a lot in this moment. So the customers are approaching us in order to consolidate the market and to be sure that they have the sound and solid suppliers.

items.statement: Engaging with Spanish government on defense opportunities; small series production planned but not significant for portfolio
items.quote: We are in contact with the Spanish government on this in Spain. You know that all these defense activities are driven by the governments. So we have had several meetings with the Spanish government on this subject and offering our capabilities.

items.statement: No access to rare-earth raw materials for magnets; all magnets are non-rare-earth; facing strong competition from China in magnet business
items.quote: We don't do Rare Earth Magnets. We don't have access to any raw materials. Of course, for doing Rare Earth, you'll have to make some process changes, like heat treatment, etcetera, which we can evaluate, but we have no access to Rare Earth raw material.

items.statement: Operating cash flow 76% of consolidated EBITDA in H1 CY25
items.quote: The company generated operating cash flows to the extent of 76% of consolidated EBITDA.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26
items.quote: So just to clarify here, we have been maintaining over the last quarter-on-quarter and over calls also that the range of margin that we expect in this business ranges from 14% to 16% of range, and we have been maintaining this for quite some time.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book size
items.quote: Our unexecuted order books remain robust at 3.15 GWp, which provides strong visibility of execution in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Order pipeline size
items.quote: So as of now, as far as our EPC company is concerned, we are chasing 25 GW worth of order pipeline, which we will try to convert them to the maximum possible into our confirm order.

items.statement: New orders won in Q1 FY26
items.quote: the order book -- order we have won during this quarter is 566 MW and worth of INR720 crores, which we have won during this quarter

items.statement: Execution in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During Q1, we successfully executed 699 MWp of EPC projects.

items.statement: Government-driven solar installation growth
items.value: 51.6% YoY growth (14.3 GW utility scale, 3.2 GW rooftop)
items.quote: In the first half of current year 2025 alone, solar installation rose by 51.6% year-on-year growth. Utility scale solar led the way with 14.3 GW added, while rooftop solar saw a 76% jump, adding 3.2 GW.

items.statement: Rooftop solar target under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
items.quote: Rooftop solar alone is expected to add around 27 to 29 GWh by 2030, creating significant opportunity for EPC players like us.

items.statement: Solar park capacity approved
items.value: 39.95 GW (18 projects fully developed, 6 partially developed)
items.quote: Under the Solar Parks Scheme, 55 solar parks with a cumulative capacity of 39.95 GW have been approved across 13 states. Of these, 18 solar projects totalling to 10.85 GW have been fully developed, and 6 parks with 4.77 GW are partially developed so far.

items.statement: Energy storage demand projection
items.value: 82.37 GWh (47.65 GWh pumped storage, 34.72 GWh battery)
items.quote: energy storage requirements are projected to rise sharply, reaching 82.37 GWh by FY 2027, comprising 47.65 GWh from pumped storage projects, and 34.72 GWh from battery energy storage systems.

items.statement: BESS order book size
items.quote: Currently, we have 40 MWh worth of order in our current order book.

items.statement: BESS cost per MW
items.quote: we have seen the rationalization of cost between $250 to $300 cost of a BESS system to today around $80 to $120 per MW kind of cost that we see.

items.statement: BESS price fluctuation risk mitigation
items.quote: we generally don't get into the business of commodity price risk, wherein either we do back-to-back hedging with our vendors on the day of taking an order or we go with a variable price component with our clients.

items.statement: Green hydrogen pilot project
items.quote: we have announced in the past that we have had 1 MW worth of green hydrogen development project as a piloted project.

items.statement: Data center EPC exploration
items.quote: There is a great amount of opportunity as far as the data center EPC work is concerned, because this AI, etc, consume more data. So, we'll have possibility of engaging EPC work of these data centers.

items.statement: Domestic bid pipeline exceeds 26 GW, total pipeline exceeds 30 GW

items.statement: First turnkey order in Q1: 290 MW Gujarat project worth INR813 crores from PSU
items.quote: We started this fiscal year by bagging our first turnkey orders when we were declared L1 for a 290-megawatt projects in Gujarat worth approximately INR813 crores from a leading PSU.

items.statement: FY26 setting up to be very good year for domestic solar EPC from strong bid pipeline
items.quote: FY '26 is setting up to be a very good year for the domestic solar EPC market from the strong bid pipeline that we are seeing buildup.

items.statement: Awarding activities from PSU and private IPPs expected to gain strong traction soon
items.quote: Awarding activities from both PSU and private IPPs is expected to begin to gain strong traction soon compared to the relatively quiet first quarter that we have seen for us and the market as a whole.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 gross margin 11.7% vs 10.1% in FY25, helped by softening input costs
items.quote: With respect to our gross margins, our consol Q1 gross margin was approximately 11.7%, while our FY '25 gross margin was 10.1%. So this has moved from 10.1% to now 11.7% first quarter.

items.quote: Looking at it segment-wise, our domestic EPC gross margin was 10.8%, and that's above our target range of 10%, while our international EPC gross margin was approximately 12.3% and more reflective of the steady-state margin profile of that segment.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin 7% in Q1, reported EBITDA margin 5.8%, expected to maintain same range
items.quote: Our operational EBITDA, which is operating revenue less recurring overheads, amounted to INR123 crores this quarter, that 7% operational EBITDA margin compared to approximately INR25 crores we have seen in quarter 1 FY '25.

items.statement: Module price softening due to tariff war and demand issues improved gross margins
items.quote: So because of the overall requirements -- demand issues, so the module prices have gone down. And some of the modules that -- the portions of modules that were supplied during this quarter that has given us advantage.

items.statement: Renegotiated module prices after order placement to take advantage of market price decline
items.quote: And going forward, then we renegotiated the price of the modules. And the price that was fixed, I mean, have gone under change to take advantage of the existing market price.

items.statement: BESS EPC cost estimated at INR2.5-4 crores per MW, BoS revenue INR30-40 lakhs per MWh
items.quote: So the battery price is constantly evolving, but the EPC cost on this, you should be expecting between INR2.5 crores to INR4 crores per megawatt.

items.statement: Commissioned over 1 GW projects in Q1 FY26, 93% YoY revenue growth to INR1,762 crores
items.quote: In terms of execution, our scale-up plans continue to remain on track and the improved top line of Q1, which has grown 93% year-on-year is reflective of the same.

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 9.3 GW as of June 2025, meaningful revenue pickup expected from H2 FY26
items.quote: Our current portfolio stands at 9.3 gigawatt as of June 2025. As we commission our large stream of EPC projects, which are nearing completion, it will feed our O&M portfolio and should aid a meaningful pickup in revenues in this segment from second half of FY '26.

items.statement: ALMM II cell deadline June 1, 2026; industry seeking timeline extension due to insufficient domestic manufacturing capacity
items.quote: Yes. So deadline for the ALMM II on the cell has been decided by ministries as 1st June 2026 right. And I mean, you see the total capacity in the country, I mean, not basically, as of now, the manufacturing capability and other things are not up to the scale to that level that can meet the requirement of the country's development plan.

items.statement: ISTS waiver extension not yet approved, impacting industry growth especially C&I sector
items.quote: Other is that the ISTS waivers, people are seeking approval for extension, which has not been given as of now. But then the industries, particularly in C&I sectors, they are expecting that this to come, right, so that they can get the -- I mean, the advantage on to the tariff that they have committed in terms of pricing and all.

items.statement: Government policy mandates 20% battery storage for new solar tenders under FDRE schemes
items.quote: So what I say the interesting point here is that under the new scheme of the Government of India, now for all the new tenders, 20% capacity of the solar plants have to be supported with the battery, right.

items.statement: International order target $250-300 million for FY26, split between Europe and Africa
items.quote: So in our business model, if you see for this year, financial year, our target is to get around $250 million to $300 million orders, primarily in European and the African markets, it is split between these 2.

items.statement: Gross borrowings declined due to IREDA loan repayment start; net debt increased INR205 crores due to Bank of Maharashtra disbursement utilization
items.quote: Our gross borrowings have declined during the quarter due to start of repayment of our IREDA loan. Our net debt has increased by around INR205 crores during the current quarter.

items.statement: Two-notch rating upgrade to BBB+ for working capital facilities and term loans
items.quote: A key development that I would like to highlight is a two-notch rating upgrade to BBB+ that we have received for our working capital facilities and term loan.

items.statement: New sanctions of INR900 crores from 3 new banks plus INR200 crores surety bonds; targeting additional INR1,500 crores credit lines this year
items.quote: We have also made progress on our banking limits front and have obtained fresh sanctions from 3 new banks for around INR900 crores, plus surety bonds of around INR200 crores we have got.

items.statement: Receivables >6 months: INR330 crores out of INR1,500 crores total, primarily retention amounts
items.quote: It's around INR330 crores, out of total receivables of around INR1,500 crore. And in terms of 7A and 7B note to the accounts, that claim is under 7A, which is not indemnifiable.

items.statement: India BESS pipeline: 3.3 GW lined up, 12.5 GW under tendering; target 74 GW by 2031-32
items.value: 3.3 GW lined up, 12.5 GW tendering, 74 GW target
items.quote: However, a significant pipeline is building up, 3.3 gigawatts of projects are already lined up and another 12.5 gigawatt is currently under various stages of tendering processes. The country has set an ambitious target of achieving 74 gigawatt of BESS capacities by 2031, '32.

items.statement: VGF scheme for 30 GWh BESS projects with INR5,400 crores budget; 25 GWh across 15 states, 5 GWh for NTPC
items.quote: Ministry of Power recently launched the second tranche of Viability Gap Funding scheme aimed at catalyzing the development of 30 gigawatt hour of BESS projects backed by a budgetary allocation of INR5,400 crores.

items.statement: Industry cement demand expected to grow 7%-10% in FY'26 post-monsoon driven by government capex
items.quote: Overall, if you see, post monsoon, we are confident that the industry should grow anywhere between 8%-10%. That's the optimistic number. Give or take, it could be 8%-10%, it could be 7%-9%. So, it's all in the ballpark of 7%-10% kind of a number is what I see the industry moving in this year.

items.statement: Nuvoco targets Rs. 50 per ton cost savings in FY'26 over FY'25 through allied slag, WHR de-bottlenecking, AFR increase, hybrid power and lead distance reduction
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting a cost saving of close to about Rs. 50-odd over and above FY'25 and FY'26 on a full year average.

items.statement: Vadraj plants at Kutch and Surat targeted for trial runs by H1 FY'27 and full functioning by Q3 FY'27
items.quote: Our current plan is to make the plants at Kutch and Surat and associated equipment including the jetty ready for trial runs by H1 FY'27 with full functioning targeted for Q3 FY'27.

items.statement: Freight cost targeted to reduce by Rs. 70-80 per ton in coming quarters through lead distance reduction of 10-13 km and increased direct dispatches
items.quote: And I guess the entire sales team has been instructed to sell more products, more markets and thereby reducing the lead distance as well as go away from STM movement and final sale into SO, increasing direct disptaches to the market. This is the agenda which we are driving very hard in this year, and we expect this number to come down by about Rs. 70 - Rs. 80 in the coming quarters.

items.statement: AFR usage targeted at 15% in H2 FY'26 post-monsoon, petcoke below 40% in H2 from current 42%
items.quote: Post-monsoon in H2 of this year, we are targeting 15% AFR. Petcoke should come less than 40% in H2, whereas currently it is about 42%.

items.statement: Depreciation ~Rs. 200 crore and interest ~Rs. 100-110 crore per quarter going forward
items.value: Rs. 200 crore depreciation, Rs. 100-110 crore interest
items.quote: In terms of depreciation and interest cost, we are looking at anywhere between, you take Rs. 5 crores here and there, about Rs. 200 crores of depreciation and close to about Rs. 100, Rs. 110 crores of interest. That's the kind of number you can keep quarter-on-quarter going forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY'26 capacity utilization at 82% with no clinker sales, only internal use and barter
items.quote: We don't do any clinker sale at all. We do clinker barter with a few companies which it helps them as well as helps us. But we don't do any clinker sale and it's all clinker for internal use.

items.statement: Q1 FY'26 highest ever first quarter EBITDA Rs. 533 crore, blended EBITDA/ton Rs. 1,052 (16-quarter high) driven by cost optimization and premiumization
items.quote: Demonstrating superior operational efficiency and profitability, the company delivered its highest ever 1st Quarter consolidated EBITDA of Rs. 533 crores in Q1 FY '26. items.statement: BRIDGE program delivered Rs. 86/ton cost savings over FY'24-FY'25 across power/fuel, material losses, damages/demurrages, direct dispatches

items.statement: Prices held stable in Q1 FY'26 vs Q4 FY'25 with small corrections; prices holding 3 weeks into Q2 FY'26
items.quote: Happy to report when we came to Q1 FY '26, the price continued to hold good in Q1 when compared to Q4 with small corrections as well happening in Q4 to Q1. items.statement: Premium product share improved to 41% and trade mix to 76% (13-quarter high) in Q1 FY'26 driven by Concreto Uno, Duraguard Microfiber rollout and Double Bull channel conversion
items.quote: The share of premium products and trade volume has further improved to 41%, while the trade mix reached 76% in Q1 FY'26. This notable improvement is a function of clear segment focus, a robust brand portfolio and a strong distribution network.

items.statement: Duraguard Microfiber sales up ~50% Q4 to Q1; Concreto Uno growing in Bihar, Bengal, Jharkhand; East premium share higher than national 41%

items.statement: Q1 demand moderate due to heat, geopolitics, early monsoon; post-monsoon optimism from central Rs. 11 lakh crore and state Rs. 9-10 lakh crore capex, SWAMIH fund, interest-free loans
items.quote: Cement demand during the quarter grew at a moderate pace impacted by intense heat, geopolitical situation and then early onset of the monsoon. However, looking ahead, we remain optimistic on demand post-monsoon driven by significant capital expenditure planned by both the central and state governments particularly in housing and infrastructure sectors.

items.statement: Carbon emission footprint improved to 454 kg CO2/ton cementitious in FY'25 from 457 in FY'24, industry lowest
items.quote: The carbon emission footprint has improved further reaching 454 kg CO2 per ton of cementitious material in FY '25 compared to a figure of 457 in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Orissa siding commissioning in 2 months; Q3 FY'26 100% clinker movement to Jajpur via siding

items.statement: Expect loan growth at system rate in FY26 and higher than system in FY27
items.quote: we expect our loan growth to continue to improve from here and remain confident of growing our advances at the system growth rate at FY26 and higher than the system in FY27

items.statement: Asset yield fell ~22 bps in Q1 FY26 due to EBLR repricing lag after rate cuts
