items.quote: The EEB portfolio declined by about 15% YoY, reaching INR52,812 crores. This decline was mainly driven by the strategic controls we have implemented in response to the elevated sectoral risks.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's non-EEB portfolio grew 27% YoY in Q1 FY26, driven by retail assets, wholesale banking, and housing
items.quote: the non-EEB portfolio, which now accounts for nearly 60% of total advances, up from 59% in the previous quarter and 51% a year back, registered a robust growth of 27% YoY.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's retail assets grew 78% YoY in Q1 FY26, supported by secured products like commercial vehicle, auto, and gold loans
items.quote: retail assets grew by 78% YoY. Wholesale Banking for an increase of 32% YoY and housing grew by 15% on a YoY basis. The growth in retail assets was mainly supported by secure products such as commercial vehicle and equipment loans, auto loans and gold loans.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's secured loan book grew 29% YoY in Q1 FY26, now constituting 52% of total advances
items.quote: The secured book grew by 29% YoY and now constitutes 52% of total advances, underscoring the shift towards a more secure and diversified asset base.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's NIM declined to 6.4% in Q1 FY26 from 6.7% in Q4 FY25 due to repo rate cuts and portfolio mix shift
items.quote: NIM for the quarter stood at 6.4%, a decline from 6.7% in Q4FY25. This moderation was primarily driven by an increased proportion of secured loans in the overall portfolio, reduction in the CD ratio, the impact of the recent repo rate cut and the continued stretch from the elevated slippages.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's cost of funds reduced by 19 bps sequentially in Q1 FY26 due to savings deposit rate cuts
items.quote: the cost of funds, which reduced by 19 basis points on a sequential basis in this quarter. This improvement was supported by rate reduction on savings deposit during the quarter.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank reduced savings and term deposit rates in Q1 FY26 to lower cost of deposits
items.quote: the first quarter of FY26, the Bank undertook strategic measures to reduce the cost of deposits by lowering interest rates on both savings and term deposit accounts

items.statement: Bandhan Bank expects EEB disbursals to improve in H2 FY26 due to festive season and monsoon season ending
items.quote: by quarter 2 end, I believe where the monsoon season gets over and the festive season kicks in, the momentum also shift towards more disbursal and sustainable disbursement.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's SMA-0 increased due to procedural change of raising installment demands on holidays, but remains recoverable
items.quote: this number has primarily happened because like what Rajeev was speaking about raising instalment demands on the holidays, which was a requirement to maintain the consistency amongst the products - demand on holiday was being raised from 31st of March.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's SMA-0 expected to rise further in Q2 FY26 due to festival holidays in Eastern states
items.quote: In the month of September holiday period of 4, 5 days together in Eastern part will have another spike up.

items.statement: Bandhan Bank's Bandhan Plus 3 portfolio expected to unwind to sub-2-3% within next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: You were speaking about Bandhan Plus 3, that is 5%. Now over the period of, I believe, next 2 quarters, these numbers will come down to sub 2 %-3% because now we have restricted the guardrails from April.

items.statement: Cement demand growth expected at 6-7% in FY26
items.quote: I believe that in financial year '26, the sector should be able to deliver a healthy cement demand growth of somewhere around 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Cement demand grew low to mid-single digits in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Based on current trends, we believe cement demand grew in the low to mid-single digits in Q1 of FY '26, but we expect it to pick up pace once the monsoon precedes.

items.statement: Capex spent INR612 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, we have incurred capex of INR612 crores, with a majority of it being spent on Umrangso clinker line and Belgaum -Pune project , b esides maintenance, land, and ROI projects

items.statement: Capex expected at INR4,000 crores in FY26
items.quote: For the full year FY '26, we expect our capex spending to be about INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected similar to FY26 (~INR4,000 crores)
items.quote: For next year basis, whatever the capex number should be something similar to a 4,000 again.

items.statement: 75-80% of FY26 capex allocated to growth projects
items.quote: Of the total capex, which Dharmender has said of INR 4,000 crores during the fiscal, approximately 75% to 80% will go into the announced growth projects.

items.statement: Sales volumes degrew 6% YoY to 7 million tons in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our sales volumes de-grew by 6% Y-o-Y to 7 million tons.

items.statement: Sales volumes from Dalmia plants flat YoY in Q1 FY26 (excluding tolling)
items.quote: if you look at the sales from Dalmia plant s, that is excluding the tolling volumes from JP plants last year, our volumes remained flattish in Q1 FY '26

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 24.3% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin during the quarter was 24.3% in Q1 FY '26, which is a good jump of almost 5.8% from the same quarter last year.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased 40% YoY to INR1,261 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA p er ton, thus works out to INR1,261 on a per ton basis, and this is a 40% increase on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Realization improvement higher than price increase in Q1 FY26
items.quote: I believe that our realization improvement in many markets has been higher than the price increase, which is visible in our 9% Q-o-Q NSR improvement.

items.statement: Cost reduction target: INR150-200 per ton over next 2 years
items.quote: We are committed to reduce Rs 150 to 200 per ton over the next two-year period and are working on the identified levers.

items.statement: Raw material cost per ton increased 8.5% YoY to INR791 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our raw material cost per ton of cement production increased by 8.5% Y-o-Y to INR791.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost per ton declined 2% YoY to INR981 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Power and fuel cost per ton of cement production declined by 2% Y-o-Y to INR981.

items.statement: Logistic cost per ton increased 2% YoY to INR1,135 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our logistic cost during the quarter increased marginally by 2% on Y-o-Y basis to INR1,135 per ton.

items.statement: Government capex spending INR2.2 lakh crores in April-May FY26 (20% of FY26 target)
items.quote: That's already 20% of the full year target of INR11.2 lakh crores, one of the highest spends in the first 2 months ever.

items.statement: Trade sales share improved to 68% in Q1 FY26 (from 64% YoY)
items.quote: Our share of trade sales improved to 68% from 64% last year.

items.statement: Premium product mix steady at 22% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Premium product mix also stood steady at 22% during the quarter.

items.statement: Direct dispatch percentage improved to 62% in Q1 FY26 (from ~55% previously)
items.quote: Direct dispatch percentage, which had been hovering around 55% over the last several years, has now reached 62% during the quarter.

items.statement: Legal risk from West Bengal government revoking incentive schemes
items.quote: The company has been legally advised that we have a Dalmia Bharat Limited. July 23, 2025 good case to challenge the vires and constitutional validity of the Revocation Act

items.statement: Income tax assessment for FY10-11 under legal challenge
items.quote: We have already filed special leave petition before the Honourable Supreme Court pursuant of which an interim stay has been granted by the court.

items.statement: Raised INR950 crores via NCDs in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, we had issued NCDs and raised INR950 crores of debt.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of Rs 1,200-1,600 crore through FY30 under Project Spring
items.quote: So again, within Project Spring, we have given a guidance of spending roughly ₹ 6,000 crores to ₹ 8,000 crores over the next 5 years. That is roughly ₹ 1,200 crores to ₹ 1,600 crores on an annual basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex was Rs 4.1 billion, primarily for Wires & Cables and backward integration
items.quote: Capital expenditure for the quarter was ₹ 4.1 billion, in -line with our Project Spring guidance of investing ₹ 12 billion to ₹ 16 billion annually through FY30.

items.statement: No plans for overseas manufacturing plants in near to mid-term; will expand capacity in India
items.quote: In the near to midterm, we don't have any plans of setting up manufacturing plants outside India. The benefit that we have when we are exporting our cables is because of the low -cost manufacturing, which is available in India.

items.statement: EPC open order book ~Rs 80 billion from BharatNet plus Rs 38-40 billion from RDSS, executable over 3-4 years
items.quote: So, in the EPC business, as at end of March, we had an open order book of roughly ₹ 70 billion. Post that, we won an order on the BharatNet project over there. So, both BharatNet projects put together, roughly, the capex part that we have to do and the overall outstanding is around ₹ 80 billion.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 210 bps YoY to 14.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter grew by 47% YoY, significantly outpacing revenue growth. This was on the back of a 210 basis point improvement in EBITDA margin, which stood at 14.5% for the quarter.

items.statement: Wires & Cables EBIT margin improved 190 bps YoY to 14.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On the profitability front, EBIT margins for the Wires and Cables segment stood at 14.7%, an improvement of 190 basis points YoY, supported by better operating leverage and strategic pricing actions.

items.statement: FMEG achieved second consecutive profitable quarter; margin expansion from premiumization and operating leverage
items.quote: The continued focus on premiumization helped the FMEG business achieve its second consecutive profitable quarter. Margin expansion was driven by a better product mix and operating leverage from scaling efficiencies.

items.statement: BharatNet EPC orders expected at 12-14% EBITDA margin; RDSS at high single digit
items.quote: As far as the profitability is concerned, we expect to accrue almost 12% to 14% of margins in that order book as well, which is pretty much in line with what we currently are making.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand for Wires & Cables driven by government capex, real estate, and commodity trends
items.quote: The Wires and Cable business continued to be our primary growth engine, driven by robust domestic demand and supportive commodity price trends.

items.statement: Government infrastructure spending at 19.7% of FY26 budget by May, highest in 7 years; expects Rs 1 trillion/month capex
items.quote: Looking at the annual target that the government has taken for this year and considering whatever they have spent so far, they still have to invest roughly around ₹ 1 trillion per month in terms of infrastructure growth.

items.statement: Cables ~73-74% of Wires & Cables revenue; wires remainder
items.quote: So, cables will be close to around 73% - 74% and remaining will be wires.

items.statement: FMEG: Solar became largest category (>2x YoY); premium fans ~25% of fan sales; premium lighting >35%; Levana switches ~20%
items.quote: The standout performance again this quarter was our solar product category, which recorded more than 2x growth over the same quarter previous year, now emerging as the largest contributor within the FMEG portfolio.

items.statement: Etira brand in high teens of retail wire sales; Maxima and Suprema ~20% each of wire sales
items.quote: Etira was specifically introduced for Tier 3 to 5 cities and the contribution from Etira would now be in high teens of the overall retail wire sales that we do. The other ranges that we introduced in wires on the premium side were Maxima and Suprema. Both of them, again, are in double digits, close to around 20% in terms of their contribution to the wires sales.

items.statement: Strategic pricing actions: passed on copper price moves due to unidirectional trend and low volatility
items.quote: For example, in the first 5 days of the quarter, while the copper was going down, but since then, we have seen it continuously moving in one direction. Now that is something wherein the pricing transfer for us becomes relatively much simple, and that is where we can maximize the benefit from any movement in commodity prices.

items.statement: Hedging policy unchanged: 90% distribution sales hedged; institutional back-to-back pricing
items.quote: We hedge our entire copper procurement that we do, and that is what is meant for selling to distributors. On the institutional part, it is back-to-back pricing. So, it doesn't really have any meaningful impact, the changes in prices.

items.statement: Broad-based demand across distribution and institutional channels; South region led growth
items.quote: Both our distribution and institutional channels registered healthy performance, indicating broad -based demand momentum. From a regional perspective, the South led the growth, followed by North, East and then West.

items.statement: Wires & Cables market share ~26-27% organized (FY25); cables ~30%, wires early 20s; gains from both organized and unorganized
items.quote: If you look at FY25, our market share in C&W put together was roughly about 26% to 27%. This is the organized market share. We would have it a bit higher as far as cables is concerned, more closer to 30%, whereas in wires, we will probably be in early 20s.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 43 days in Q1 FY26 (temporarily low due to higher payable days); expects normalization to 50-55 days
items.quote: Our working capital cycle stood at 43 days in Q1 FY26, positively impacted by a temporary increase in payable days. We expect this to normalize and revert to a long-term steady range of 50 days to 55 days in the coming quarters.

items.statement: BharatNet EPC has 10% upfront payment, favorable working capital cycle
items.quote: Overall, I think it should be a pretty good business as far as overall working capital cycle is concerned because of the fact that over here, there is an upfront payment of almost 10% of the order book.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 31 billion at end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet, closing the quarter with a net cash position of ₹ 31 billion.

items.statement: Wires & Cables volume growth >25% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The Wires and Cables business delivered a strong 31% YoY revenue growth, supported by over 25% volume growth during the quarter.

items.statement: US tariff situation evolving; renewable investment slowdown may not materially impact low/medium voltage cable exports
items.quote: The change in the outlook of investment towards renewable, I don't think it will have any material impact in that way in the kind of export that we were doing.

items.statement: EHV cable meaningful revenue only from FY28; plant commissioning then tender bidding required
items.quote: So extra high voltage, as you'll be aware, is a tender -based business. So once the plant is up and commissioned, you'll have to go and bid for the tender. And if you win, that is when you start executing and when you start accru ing revenues. So probably any form of meaningful revenue accrual will only happen in FY28.

items.statement: Management expects mid-double-digit 14-15% growth in both revenue and EBITDA on an annual basis
items.quote: I think as we had said on an annual basis, we expect to do a mid-double-digit, 14%-15% kind of growth, both on the top line as well as on the EBITDA front.

items.statement: Overseas formulation facility in Southeast Asia to start with Rs. 15-20 crore investment
items.quote: The CAPEX, which is coming up in , outside the formulation, it is a very small investment, between Rs. 15 crore - Rs. 20 crore.

items.statement: Capacity expansion projects across Rossari Biotech, Unitop Chemicals & Tristar Intermediates progressing with phased commissioning expected over coming quarters
items.quote: Our capacity expansion projects across Rossari Biotech , Unitop Chemicals & Tristar Intermediates are progressing well, with phased commissioning expected over the coming quarters.

items.statement: New capacities expected to deliver 3x-4x asset turnover at optimal utilization driving operating leverage and margin expansion particularly from FY2027 onwards
items.quote: Once fully commissioned and operating at optimal utilization levels, these facilities are expected to deliver 3 x-4x asset turnover, driving operating leverage and margin expansion, particularly from FY2027 onwards.

items.statement: Domestic business performed well supported by demand across key categories while export business faced headwinds due to global uncertainties impacting Agri and Textile segments
items.quote: While the operating environment remained dynamic, our domestic business performed well, supported by demand across key categories. Our export business, however, faced some headwinds due to prevailing global uncertainties, which also impacted the Agri and Textile segments.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 12.5% in Q1 FY26 vs 13.3% YoY; excluding institutional and B2C loss of Rs. 7 crore, adjusted EBITDA margin ~16%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 67.9 crore, up 4.6% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 12.5%, compared to 13.3% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Institutional and B2C business reported loss of ~Rs. 7 crore in Q1; management hopes to break even at EBITDA level in FY26 with minimal losses
items.quote: The institutional and B2C business reported a loss of approximately Rs. 7 crore in Q1, which impacted the consolidated margin.

items.statement: Export orders missed in Q1 due to plant shutdowns expected to be fulfilled in Q2; Q2 expected to be stronger quarter
items.quote: We lost about 7 -10 days of production and that impacted the overall exports where some of the planned orders we could not dispatch, and we are planning to make up for that in the 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Ethylene Oxide availability improved due to soft India consumption; Reliance expansion delayed but enhanced capacity expected by Q2-Q3 FY27
items.quote: The Reliance expansion is delayed, and it may take a few more quarters for them to start delivering higher EO. But considering the softness in all India consumption of EO, we are able to get more EO than we were getting normally.

items.statement: Q1 exports at Rs. 139 crore; annual exports expected at 27-28% of overall turnover with key markets in Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia and Middle East
items.quote: In Q1, the exports was about Rs. 139 crore and we expect on an annualized basis, exports to be around 27%-28% of the overall turnover.

items.statement: Non-EO chemistries include surfactants, esters, acrylic polymers, other polymers, methyl esters of vegetable oils targeting agro, home & personal care, oil & gas, pharma, paints & coatings
items.quote: On the non -EO side, we have mostly surfactants and these are surfactants, which include Esters, which include Acrylic Polymers, which include other Polymers based on different Monomers, which we do.

items.statement: Non-EO segment competes with global majors Dow, BASF, Lubrizol, INEOS, Nouryon, Sasol, Stepan, Clariant, Huntsman, Indorama and Chinese players
items.quote: The competition is all the global majors, who are the big global majors like Dow, BASF, Lubrizol, INEOS, Nouryon, Sasol, Stepan. So, these are the big ones who are global majors everywhere in the world.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning business has phased orders with Q3-Q4 stronger; Q1 softer but annual growth expected healthy
items.quote: Q1, if you see, generally, our Q1 in this business is not as strong as the subsequent quarters, especially Q3, Q4 are the stronger quarters for this business.

items.statement: Production lost 7-10 days in Q1 due to intermittent shutdowns for hot work and erection activities during CAPEX execution
items.quote: During Q1, as our CAPEX work was in full steam and following all safety protocols, we had to shut certain production operations for 10-12 days intermittently due to hot work, erection activities, etc.

items.statement: CAPEX funded through mix of internal accruals and debt; balance sheet remains healthy with strong liquidity and conservative leverage
items.quote: Funded through a mix of internal accruals and debt, these investments are expected to generate 3x-4x asset turns at optimal utilizations, driving stronger operating leverage over the medium term.

items.statement: Institutional business gross margins range 28-30%
items.quote: Gross margins are closer to, I think, 30%. They would range between 28% to 30%.

items.statement: Pricing remains a challenge; some raw material price declines may need to be passed on in coming quarters limiting EBITDA growth
items.quote: Yes, it should grow, but we are still being a little cautious because pricing is still a challenge for us. Some of the raw material prices have come down, and we expect that some of that we will have to give up in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Institutional business added ~100 people last year; manpower increase this year will be substantially lower
items.quote: Last year, if you remember, we have added almost 100 people in this business. This year will be substantially lower than that.

items.statement: Gross profit margin improved sequentially to 21.4% from 19.3% in previous quarter, marginally down 0.3% year-on-year
items.quote: Gross profit margin is 21.4%, which is sequentially higher than the 19.3% delivered in the previous quarter, but marginally down 0.3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 11% from 10.2% in previous quarter
items.quote: This all contributes to an adjusted EBITDA margin of 11%, which again is sequentially higher than the 10.2% seen in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Processed 39.3 billion billable transactions, similar to Q1 last year and marginally higher than previous quarter
items.quote: During the quarter, we processed 39.3 billion billable transactions, which is actually similar to the volumes we processed in the 1st Quarter last year, and marginally higher than w hat we saw last quarter

items.statement: Average realization per transaction was 27 paisa, influenced by higher share of domestic messaging in India
items.quote: The average realization per transaction was 27 pais a, and this was largely influenced by a shift in our traffic composition, particularly a higher share of domestic messaging in

items.statement: Next-generation product portfolio grew 11.4% year-on-year with several marquee enterprise onboardings
items.quote: We have witnessed growth of 11.4% year-on-year in this segment. We have onboarded several marquee enterprises with evolved customer engagement use cases that we support through the IP-based messaging solutions.

items.statement: Lost one large digital native enterprise customer moving directly to MNOs for bundled services including data and SMS
items.quote: One of them. And I think the reason they wanted to move to operators directly is beca use they have a new ecosystem within their company, which believes that having direct partnership with operators… They are not just talking about SMS as one option with operators. They are talking about data. They are talking about other services of operators to be used as a bundle deal with

items.statement: Firewall solution deployed with operator generates indirect margin when lost customer moves directly to that operator
items.quote: Yes. No, there is a benefit because our firewall is there with an operator. And that particular customer moves to the operator directly. Indirectly, we also make margin because of our firewall plays within that operator.

items.statement: WhatsApp pricing revision caused 12-13% pricing dilution, offsetting volume growth in new product revenue
items.quote: And WhatsApp, a lot of that business we do within India. Now, WhatsApp has revised their pricing for the market, which also results in us revising the selling price to remain competitive. So, on the volume front, we have definitely seen growth. But on the pricing front, there's been dilution of almost 12-13% on the pricing.

items.statement: Added 26 new employees and saw 63 exits during quarter, rationalizing teams from past acquisitions
items.quote: On the people front, we added 26 new employees during the quarter and saw 63 exits.

items.statement: Won large firewall deal in Latin America with one of largest MNOs, deploying AI-powered firewall and spam protection across multiple countries
items.quote: We recently onboarded one of the largest mobile network operators in Latin America, and we will be deploying our AI-powered firewall and spam protection solutions across various countries where this operator has presence.

items.statement: Completed RCS platform integration with one of largest global system integrators to reduce time-to-market
items.quote: For instance, we recently completed the integration of our RCS platform with one of the largest players across the globe.

items.statement: Cross-sell pipeline building with Proximus Global group companies, particularly in APAC markets
items.quote: We have also witnessed green shoots of cross-sell opportunities where the Proximus Global Group companies have started creating sales pipelines for Route Mobile omnichannel communication solutions. And this is currently more towards the APAC market, certain regions within the APAC market.

items.statement: Leveraging BICS reach to expand firewall and MAP solutions sales footprint with global telecom operators
items.quote: We are also leveraging the extensive reach of BICS , which is a part of the Proximus Global Group, to strengthen our relationship with tel ecom operators across the globe. We are approaching several global operators to expand the sales footprint of our firewall solutions and MAP solutions

items.statement: Normalized operating cash flow at around 120% of EBITDA in Q1
items.quote: On the operating cash flow, which is the easier one, on a normalized basis we would have done around 120% odd of CFO to EBITDA in the last quarter.

items.statement: Management not providing formal FY26 guidance but focusing on growth, cost optimization and Proximus synergies
items.quote: So, Nikhil, I think we are not sharing any guidance as you've seen even last quarter. But I think one thing I can assure you about me coming back as a CEO of Route Mobile, and I think there are three areas which I really want to focus now. One is growth, cost optimization, and synergies.

items.statement: Structural shift in A2P SMS market with enterprises evaluating messaging channels, pricing models and delivery quality differently
items.quote: There has been a structural shift in certain parts of the market, particularly around how enterprises evaluate messaging channels, pricing models and delivery quality.

items.statement: Consciously stepped back from low gross profit margin A2P SMS opportunities not aligning with long-term profitable growth view
items.quote: As part of our margin-focused approach, we have actually consciously stepped back from certain low-percentage gross profit margin opportunities. In the A2P SMS business, these opportunities were not essentially aligning with our long-term view of profitable growth.

items.statement: Integrated WhatsApp voice capabilities into platform to cater to expanded enterprise use cases
items.quote: For instance, we have integrated WhatsApp voice capabilities into our platform, which enables us to cater to an expanded set of use cases for our enterprise customers.

items.statement: Operating costs year-on-year, after adjusting for FX impact and non-core items, constrained to only 4% growth
items.quote: Operating costs year-on-year, after adjusting for FX impact and non-core items, is constrained to only 4% growth.

items.statement: 365squared firewall deal won in Latin America is combination of BICS relationship and 365squared technology
items.quote: So, this firewall d eal which we have won is a combination of BICS and 365squared. So, it is a relationship of BI CS which has helped us to win this contract and I think 365 is doing fantastically with the great pipeline they have right now

items.statement: Company is 100% GDPR compliant with no additional cost for regulatory compliance across geographies
items.quote: Route Mobile is GDPR compliant company and our server installation to every single aspect as far as the customers are concerned, I think we are 100% GDPR compliant company from the last so many years. So, I don't think there's any challenge and I don't think there's a cost involved anything on that.

items.statement: Rajdipkumar Gupta returned as CEO, replacing Gautam Badalia, focusing on growth, cost optimization and synergies
items.quote: I am honoured to be speaking with you once again as the CEO of Route Mobile Limited. It is a privilege to step back into the role at such a pivotal moment in our journey. I want to take a moment to thank our outgoing CEO – Gautam Badalia for his leadership and contribution.

items.statement: Platform play includes firewall, RCS, CPaaS-in-a-box solutions deployed at operators with 100% margin SaaS model
items.quote: So , when I talk about say f irewall solution Kaustav , firewall solution we deploy with operator and where we charge based on managed services along with per transaction where operator pays us per transaction basis plus managed services charges which is complete DM to us which is a complete SaaS

items.statement: Telecom API initiative for digital identity with Telesign in pilot testing phase in India with sandbox installations
items.quote: We are definitely in touc h with various customers. We are doing some pilot testing. There are some sand box installation is already being done in India with a few customers. Those testing are getting done, but it's a longer process because there are lots of security aspects we hav e to clear and close the customer

items.statement: Lost large financial services client in India due to competitive repricing through bid process
items.quote: Another one was one of the large financial services clients that we had in India where we had repricing. So, this is typically done through a bid process, and in terms of the competitive landscape, the pricing was revised, and accordingly, our revenues were impacted because of the revised pricing.

items.statement: Management expects absolute EBITDA/PAT growth of 15-20% and revenue growth of 10-15% for FY26
items.quote: That guidance number what we are saying is, in absolute terms we will grow between around 15% to 20%. That is what we are expecting it.

items.statement: Africa and Orgafeed expected to grow in higher teens; India standalone (ex-OSAM) in lower teens (10-15%); with OSAM, India growth moves to higher teens (~15%)
items.value: Africa/Orgafeed: higher teens; India ex-OSAM: 10-15%; India with OSAM: ~15%
items.quote: Africa will be on the higher teens. Orgafeed will also be in the higher teens of growth. And India will be in that 10% to 14% - 15% kind of a growth rate

items.statement: Early monsoon and unseasonal rains dampened summer demand for VAP (curd, flavored milk, ice cream); curd volumes degrew 3.2% YoY; lassi/buttermilk volumes dropped sharply
items.quote: We have not got any growth in curd, lassi. Lassi, we've lost a lot of volume. Even there's no curd growth, butter milk. So all that where we see VAP all wee -- we have maintained almost like last year numbers or 1% or 2% lesser than the last year numbers.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 8.2% in Q1 FY26 under pressure due to procurement prices rising faster than realizations and adverse VAP mix; expected to improve in Q2 as lower procurement prices reflect
items.quote: As a result of these multiple factors, the margin profile remained under pressure during Q1 FY '26. We expect this trend to improve in Q2 FY '26 as the full impact of lower procurement prices will be reflected in the current quarter.

items.statement: Orgafeed EBITDA margin jumped to 17.6% in Q1 FY26 (vs ~15% avg last year) driven by raw material prices falling 12% while sales realizations fell only 6%; margins expected to sustain within 1-2% range
items.quote: Overall, the selling price increased. 12% in the procurement cost of mix of all raw materials, the sales realization was reduced only by 6%. So ther e is a delta of 6%, whic h was in turn resulted into the overall margin improvement

items.statement: Africa EBITDA margin 13% in Q1 FY26 (lower YoY) due to new Kenya plant strategic pricing and higher procurement costs; expected to stabilize and improve as procurement prices stabilize
items.quote: In Africa, we saw a healthy growth in terms of revenue of 26.9% on a year-on-year basis and an EBITDA margin of 13%, which is lower as compared to Q1 of last year.

items.statement: India milk procurement price averaged INR37.38/L in Q1 FY26 (vs INR34.15/L YoY, INR37.36/L QoQ); July procurement price dropped to INR36.90/L; further reductions of INR0.30-0.90/L seen in April-May and INR0.58-0.60/L in July
items.quote: Running July, it's is INR36.90.

items.statement: Management not planning significant consumer price hikes despite earlier procurement cost increases; will maintain mass-premium positioning vs cooperatives; expect volume growth to recover to 7-8% and value growth 10-15% as procurement pric
items.quote: Regarding pricing, I don't think there will be an undercutting of pricing as much as to take on the market share. It will be that they are not trying to over premiumize our product versus the cooperatives. We are trying to maintain sort of a mass premium, not a super premium.

items.statement: SMP inventory reduced from INR144 cr (Jun'24) to INR17 cr (Jun'25); butter inventory from INR155 cr to INR9.7 cr; March inventories also sharply lower (SMP INR43 cr to INR17 cr; butter INR19 cr to INR9 cr)
items.value: SMP INR17 cr; Butter INR9.7 cr
items.quote: With regard to the inventory, sir, as of now, we are having butter only INR9.7 crores as against INR155 crores of last year June '24. So the substantial reduction. Even the skimmed milk power also, last year, we have around INR144 crores, but now we have only INR17 crores.

items.statement: Greenfield expansion of INR280 cr in Maharashtra (Solapur) on track; daily procurement in region already ~2.6 lakh LPD; building fully integrated facility of 10 lakh LPD capacity
items.quote: Further, our greenfield expansion of INR280 crores in Maharashtra aimed at tie-up in the potential Solapur market is on track with the daily procurement in the region already reaching around 2.6 lakh liters per day. We are developing a fully integrated facility with a capacity of 10 lakhs.

items.statement: Overall dairy capacity utilization at 70-75%; Kenya plant utilization low at 65-70k LPD vs peak capacity of 1.3-1.5 lakh LPD due to import permit restrictions from Uganda; Orgafeed plant utilization <45-50%
items.quote: Overall capacity utilization level of the dairy business is in the vicinity of 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of 100% stake in HR Food Processing (brand OSAM), strong in Bihar/Jharkhand; deal expected to close in next few days; part of predefined inorganic growth plan
items.quote: In line with this framework, our Board recently approved the acquisition of 100% stake in HR Food Processing Private Limited. The company operates on the premium brand OSAM and has established a strong presence in Bihar and Jharkand.

items.statement: VAP contribution 36.2% of sales in Q1 FY26; curd sales 452.3 MMT (-3.2% YoY); bulk sales (SMP/butter) INR57.7 cr vs INR35.5 cr YoY; liquid milk sales 11.9 lakh LPD (+4.9% YoY)
items.quote: Overall, our VAP sales contribution during this quarter stood at 36.2% of sales. Curd sales stood 452.3 million metric tons with a degrowth of 3.2% on a year-on-year basis. Bulk sales during FY - 1Q '26 stood INR57.7 crores, which was INR35.5 crores of the same period of the last year.

items.statement: Orgafeed currently serves 35-40% of own farmers; targeting to increase coverage; plant capacity utilization <50% leaves headroom for scaling
items.quote: Now, right now, we are catering only 35% to 40% of our own farmers. And month-on-month, year-on-year, we have keep on increasing. And still, we have a lot of scope because plant capacity utilization is less than 45%, less than 50% only.

items.statement: Working capital managed on cash-and-carry basis; sufficient cash balance to fund seasonal inventory buildup in Q2 (flush season) and OSAM acquisition
items.quote: Working capital, there is will not be any major work for the inventory, because data should be cash and carry. So we have a sufficient cash bala nce. If any inventory has to be built up that will be met from our cash balances

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; cash balances used for inventory buildup and OSAM acquisition; other income rose 144% to INR17 cr due to interest income and GST provision reversal
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, in Q2, we expect to utilize our cash balance towards inventory buildup during flush season and the OSAM acquisition, which is expected to complete in the next few days.

items.statement: India milk procurement hit record 18.7 lakh LPD avg in Q1 FY26 (+6.3% YoY); liquid milk sales 11.9 lakh LPD (+4.9% YoY); standalone milk revenue INR538 cr (+6% YoY); curd revenue INR204 cr (-3% YoY)
items.quote: During the quarter, our milk procurement was the highest ever level of around 18.7lakh liters per day on average. This is in line with our net seller strategy, where we continue to rise our procuremen t levels whenever there is a favorable procurement conditions available in the market

items.statement: Africa revenue grew 26.9% YoY; Kenya milk volume 1.6 lakh LPD (+19% YoY); Africa procurement 1.98 lakh LPD; Uganda yogurt volume ~40k LPD; consolidated realization INR62.78/L (India INR63.24, Africa INR59.25)
items.quote: Africa, milk volume is around 1.6 lakhs now as against 1.35 lakhs of last year. That is almost a 19% of growth in that volume. And with regard to the value, we said it is INR81 crores. Last ye ar, it is INR64 crores, that is 26% of growth in the Africa

items.statement: Africa competition stable; Uganda yogurt near #1 position; Kenya liquid milk has multiple players but brand established; India pricing maintained at mass-premium vs cooperatives, no undercutting for share
items.quote: We are living with the competition. There's no problem. Especially in Uganda, yogurt, there's no much players. There we have taken almost number 1 position in Uganda, yogurt is concerned.

items.statement: Kenya government restricts import permits for Ugandan milk (5-6 months near zero permits); only issues permits during shortages; forced local Kenya plant investment
items.quote: Kenyan government put a break, they stopped giving in a permits. So 1 year almost they have stopped giving a permit. That's why now in 2023, we acquired a plant in Kenya.

items.statement: Seasonal volatility (early/unseasonal rains) disrupts VAP demand (curd, lassi, buttermilk) and creates procurement-sales mismatch; managed via higher procurement buffer (8-10% above sales) and B2C focus
items.quote: Otherwise, we'll try to match mostly between our own requirement and our own sales. And we cannot match it precisely to start with by saying every day, it will be there or every quarter, it will be there. So now we are going with the view that we will have ample milk with us because a couple of years ago, we ran short of fat and we had to withdraw from ghee sale, for example.

items.statement: Plan to move most quick commerce inventory to 1P ownership within 2-3 quarters with margin accretion in same timeframe
items.quote: Yes. Manish, broadly that's the plan and your assessment is right. That's what we expect. In that timeframe, we should be able to move most of our business to inventory ownership and the margin accretion should also happen in that timeframe.

items.statement: Quick commerce margins expected to continue improving from -1.8% if competitive intensity remains same
items.quote: directionally, as you can see, the margins have improved from -2.4% to -1.8% in this quarter. What we are saying is we expect that projection to continue, subject to competitive intensity remaining the same.

items.statement: Food delivery margins to remain around current levels in near term as focus shifts to growth over margin expansion
items.quote: What we are saying is that while in the long term, margin expansion is possible, but in the near term, we are more focused on growth. And hence, therefore, the margins could remain around the mark they are today.

items.statement: Going-out losses expected to remain range-bound in near term, not meaningfully increase
items.quote: We don't want to provide any guidance on the short term at this point, but I don't expect the losses to meaningfully increase from where they are. They'll remain range-bound in the near term.

items.statement: Employee cost as percentage of revenue guidance maintained from previous quarters
items.quote: Rishi, in the past, we have given a guidance on our total employee cost as a percentage of revenue, which includes both the cash compensation and the ESOP charge, I think two quarters ago maybe and then before that also. So, we're still sticking to that guidance that we've given last time.

items.statement: Infrastructure build-out including warehousing expansion is lumpy with upfront investment and delayed utilization
items.quote: Apart from stores, some of the warehousing expansion is more lumpy where you invest upfront, but you start seeing utilization over a slightly longer period of time.

items.statement: Delhi city grew 70% year-on-year despite being geographically well covered
items.quote: a city like Delhi, which from a geographical coverage standpoint is fairly well covered, we've seen a growth of 70% year-on-year in this quarter.

items.statement: Quick commerce growth primarily from existing polygons, less than 5% from new expansion areas
items.quote: Even in this quarter when we opened a lot more cities, less than 5% of the overall growth came from the expansion areas that we were not serving earlier.

items.statement: Food delivery growth bottoming out with better app opens and resurrection rates in first three weeks of quarter
items.quote: basis what we have seen so far in the first three weeks of the quarter, the year-on-year growth has sort of bottomed out and we are seeing now better app opens from our consumers and better resurrection rates.

items.statement: Quick commerce industry growth rates expected to remain high for next two years as infrastructure builds out
items.quote: The growth momentum remains strong. And at least for the next two years, we feel that the growth rates will be high as we are still building out more infrastructure, and getting to 3,000 stores will take time.

items.statement: Quick commerce Adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -2.4% to -1.8% sequentially
items.quote: directionally, as you can see, the margins have improved from -2.4% to -1.8% in this quarter.

items.statement: Mature quick commerce stores already at 2.5% margin, rest catching up over time
items.quote: Parts of our business, as I mentioned, are already at 2.5% margin. So, the rest of the business catching up is a function of time.

items.statement: Food delivery MTC growth in sync with NOV growth year-on-year, expected to continue with AOV growth
items.quote: MTC growth is fairly in sync with the overall NOV growth, if you look at it on a year-on-year basis. Quarter-on-quarter, yes, it can appear to be lumpy but if you look at it from a more longer term, I don't think there is any divergent trend there, and we expect that MTC growth to continue along with AOV growth.

items.statement: Quick commerce growth secular across all categories, no category breakup disclosed
items.quote: The growth, for us, across all categories has been pretty secular. That's the only thing that we would like to share at this point.

items.statement: Non-grocery share will follow national consumption trends, grocery expected to remain disproportionate
items.quote: Manish, that will follow the consumption trend overall of the country. So, if the household share of buying groceries is always higher, then I don't think you will necessarily see the non-grocery segment being bigger than that.

items.statement: Will react to competitive circumstances to maintain leadership and best service, no fixed strategy
items.quote: We'll have to react to the circumstances. We've been fairly clear on this one, now and in the past, that we'll respond to what the market is, and we'll do the right thing.

items.statement: No interest in 30-40 minute delivery segment, focused only on 10-15 minute quick commerce
items.quote: Sachin, we don't see the opportunity there. So that's why we are not doing that.

items.statement: Quick commerce and food delivery user bases largely distinct with low overlap
items.quote: The overlap is not very high - is what I would say. There is a large user base on both sides, which is fairly distinct.

items.statement: Blinkit working capital at ~18 days, structurally better than traditional retailers due to replenishment frequency
items.quote: However, because of the way that we replenish and the frequency at which we are actually able to move products in our supply chain, we are structurally better off than most retailers that you would see across categories in the days of cover that we need to have.

items.statement: 1P inventory shift reduces administrative and licensing burden for company and brands
items.quote: Moving to 1P reduces the administrative burden, the licensing burden, all of that significantly for both us and the brands.

items.statement: Quick commerce GOV per day per store stable despite store count growing from 600+ to 1,500+, max throughput not yet reached
items.quote: So, to the first part, Rishi, we don't actually know. We still haven't reached the point of hitting max throughput capacity at any of our stores.

items.statement: Food delivery partner log-in hours and utilization improving, idle time decreasing enabling more orders with same fleet
items.quote: Secondly, utilization, or rather the idle time of delivery partners on the platform, continues to come down. And as that happens, we're able to do more Orders with the same number of log-in hours that we have on the platform.

items.statement: GLP-1 drug impact on food delivery too early to assess, theoretically could go either way
items.quote: No comment on it. It is still a new paradigm. And so far, I don't think we have seen GLP-1 impact in food delivery in many other countries. But as I said, it's fairly nascent. Theoretically, it can go either way, but too early for us to have a point of view or share that with you.

items.statement: Revenue will become similar to NOV under 1P model, Contribution margin definition unchanged, interim gross margin disclosure TBD
items.quote: Revenue will now become very similar to NOV because we own the inventory and Contribution margins, of course, in terms of definition and calculation, will not change. There is an now an interim gross margin of the business, that we'll take a call whether we want to disclose that or not in the next quarter.

items.statement: Annual wage revision cycle unchanged, expected in September quarter
items.quote: Appraisal cycle remains the same, Vijit.

items.statement: Record quarterly order intake of INR 515 crores in Q1 FY26, highest in 10 quarters; 50% executable in current year
items.quote: we had an order intake of INR 515 crores during the quarter. This is the highest quarterly order intake in the last 10 quarters. And the good news is the nearly 50% of this new order intake is actually executable in the current year itself.

items.statement: Order backlog at INR 2,132 crores, up INR 225.7 crores quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: from an order backlog perspective, we are at INR 2,132 crores which is a growth quarter-on-quarter of INR 225.7 crores or INR 2,257 million.

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio close to 2 in Q1; confident of sustaining above 1 for full year FY26
items.quote: we are confident and suggest in sustaining this trajectory and achieving and continuing to achieve a book-to-bill ratio significantly above 1 going forward.

items.statement: Gross contribution margin around 40% in Q1; similar mix expected in coming quarters
items.quote: If you look at the current quarter, whatever you are seeing as the mix of direct material cost to the total revenue is the same mix we can expect in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Seeing spike in RFQs from existing and new US prospects for dual sourcing from China; China Plus One driving opportunities
items.quote: we are seeing a spike in RFQs, coming from our existing customers and also some of the new prospects in U.S. where we are seeing some of the inquiries which are coming there, currently, they are making it in China. So, they are doing for a dual sourcing.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook in Aerospace, Defense, Medical and Industrial sectors; US tariff situation stabilizing and China Plus One playing to advantage
items.quote: With the U.S. tariff situation stabilizing, China Plus One playing to our advantage, with the increase in semiconductors and the use of electronics in various systems, etc., we expect demand to accelerate, especially in Aerospace and Defense, Medical and Industrial sectors.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 55-60% on full-year basis running 2 shifts; can double revenue by running 3 shifts without significant CAPEX
items.quote: our current capacity utilization is quite low. On a full-year basis, we will be close to 55%, 60% of capacity utilization. And this is running at 2 shifts, right? So, if we actually run 3 shifts, we can potentially double the current revenue without having to add any new factory or new SMT line.

items.statement: Free cash flow of INR 80 crores in Q1, third consecutive positive quarter; DIO high at 185 days due to denominator effect, inventory not grown much in absolute terms
items.quote: The consolidated free cash flow for the quarter is about INR 80 crores or INR 802 million. Now this is the third quarter in a row where we have generated positive cash.

items.statement: INR 60 crores of IPO proceeds used for working capital in Q1; another INR 60 crores earmarked for working capital in rest of FY26
items.quote: we have used up about INR 60 crores towards working capital in the current quarter. We have about another INR 100 crores left to be used for the rest of the year, out of which INR 60 crores is towards working capital.

items.statement: Build-to-spec (B2S) focus with product roadmap; B2S expected to contribute ~5% of revenue in FY26, with 100+ million revenue potential over years
items.quote: On the B2S, as I said, in the FY 26 immediately, we won't be seeing much revenue coming over on this one, so it will be probably 5% of the revenue in FY 26. Otherwise, we will be seeing as I said, some of the things which are right now in the pipeline, where we will be working on this, so probably both things will be having maybe 100-plus million of revenue which we will be seeing over the years.

items.statement: Added one new logo (Deutsche Aircraft) in Q1; two major BPS orders in finalization stage; two new accounts from last year visible to become multi-million dollar accounts in 1 year
items.quote: we had one new logo in Q1, which is Deutsche Aircraft, so this is basically BTS projects, which we are working out right now. And we also have 2 major BPS orders in the finalization stage, which probably we will be closing in this quarter.

items.statement: Order intake equally distributed across Aerospace & Defense, Industrial and Medical; executable backlog similar mix
items.quote: it is an equal distribution between all the 3 segments currently.

items.statement: Global EMS industry projected to grow at 6.9% CAGR to $1 trillion in 7 years; India EMS market growing driven by PLI schemes and Industry 4.0
items.quote: if you look at on the global EMS industry, it is projected to grow at a 6.9% CAGR. So, taking it to $1 trillion in the next 7 years, that's what the market size right now where we are going ahead.

items.statement: Middle East conflict disrupted supply chains: airspace restrictions and sea lane disruptions increased air freight costs and flight times
items.quote: the conflict in the Middle East between Israel and Iran. This has created a disruption in the supply chain. The Iranian and Gulf airspace restrictions have forced number of airlines like Emirates and Lufthansa, which carry a lot of the material that we supply to our customers to reroute, increasing flight times and costs.

items.statement: Delay in repeat order from major customer (BEL/Indian Navy) with no clear visibility on timing; Q1 deliveries impacted by Middle East conflict
items.quote: we don't have any clear indication of the repeat order, when it is going to happen. So, basically BEL has to get it from their end customer, basically from the Indian Defense side, Navy. So, we still don't have that visibility.

items.statement: Rajendra Velagapudi appointed CEO in addition to MD role earlier this quarter; sales team strengthened domestically and internationally
items.quote: the Board of Directors appointed Mr. Rajendra Velagapudi in the role of CEO, in addition to his role of the Managing Director of the company, and as such, will now be responsible for the overall operations of the company.

items.statement: Revenue of INR 2,784 million in Q1 FY26, up 8% YoY; growth muted due to large customer order ending and Middle East conflict shifting revenue to later quarters
items.quote: in terms of revenue, we delivered INR 2,784 million, which is a growth of 8% year-on-year. As indicated in the earlier commentary, the growth for this quarter has been muted for a couple of reasons. One, if you see last year, I think we had a large customer orde r that has come to an end completely

items.statement: No pressure to raise funds; in a healthy cash position; IPO proceeds usage compliant with RHP
items.quote: there is no pressure to sort of raise funds because they are in a heady cash position as of this quarter, right?

items.statement: Refraining from full-year FY26 revenue guidance; long-term 5-year 30% CAGR target maintained but with year-to-year volatility
items.quote: we are refraining from giving a full-year guidance. I think what we have said that in the past is over a long-term period of 5 years, I think we can confidently say that we will grow at 30% CAGR, right? But there will be odd years where it w ill be down , another year where revenue will be higher than that

items.statement: Altek Electronics margin profile similar to Cyient DLM at acquisition; synergy benefits flowing into India books; operating as one integrated entity
items.quote: when the acquisition happened, we had mentioned that the margin profile of the acquired company is similar to margin profile that we have. Now as we integrate, I think about the business, there is a lot of synergy benefits flowing into the India books as well.

items.statement: Shift to regional manufacturing due to tariff uncertainty; nearshoring and China Plus One driving dual sourcing opportunities
items.quote: we are seeing a shift to regional manufacturing due to tari ff uncertainty. So, we are still working on some of those areas. So, we are seeing a nearshoring is one of the areas to

items.statement: FY26 RAC market expected to grow 10-15% YoY despite Q1 degrowth
items.quote: So definitely, FY '26, we will still see growth and a strong demand is what most of the brands and customers are still expecting with this story -- with the tailwind still being strong on a long-term basis. So the market is definitely destined to grow overall for FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target of 7.5%+
items.quote: So, in terms of EBITDA margin, we are still targeting an EBITDA margin of 7.5% plus in FY '26 with a medium-term ambition of achieving 8

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance of INR450-500 crores (including subsidiaries)
items.quote: So, like we shared in the annual call, our outlook for the current year or next 12 to 18 months is overall capex of INR450 crores, plus/minus INR50 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: RAC 65%, SDA 10-15%, components 20-25%, LDA 10%
items.quote: So for current financial year FY '25, '26, based on present trends and ongoing ramp-up of AC, we foresee AC contributing close to 60%, 65% kind of revenue. Small domestic appliances contributing 10% to 15% kind of revenue and components, a healthy 20%, 25% kind of revenue.

items.statement: FY26 Hisense revenue to ramp up in calendar year 2026
items.quote: So the revenue -- I mean, the numbers would scale up the current calendar year or it can be -- largely, it would be the calendar year '26, wherein we will see ramping up of capacities and utilization.

items.statement: Hisense AC capacity of 0.5 million units in Phase 1
items.quote: So for Hisense, we are putting up a capacity of almost 0.5 million air conditions in Phase 1 for assembling of air conditions and making heat exchangers.

items.statement: Washing machine capacity of 1 million units by CY27
items.quote: So for the next calendar year, we can foresee a capacity of -- an available capacity of almost 1 million washing machines.

items.statement: Air fryer capacity of 1 million units in Phase 1
items.quote: And the kind of capacities we have set up for this product is almost 1 million air fryers is the capacity we have set up in Phase 1.

items.statement: EPAVO BLDC motor capacity of 3 million units (10% of India market)
items.quote: So, with this kind of capacity, we look forward to strong margins and revenue growth both in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Strong RFQs for Q3/Q4 FY26 due to BEE revision and new season prep
items.quote: So we see an early -- I mean, we believe that there will be an early start of season and Q3, Q4 should definitely see most of the production for the next year being done in advance.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 used for RFQs for next season (Q3/Q4 FY26)
items.quote: So generally, the industry works on a system wherein 2Q is used largely to create RFQs and the outlook for the next season.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion to 8% medium-term
items.quote: So alongside this margin expansion, our margin improvement strategy is built on the 3 levers like to continue to diversify and grow our portfolio of air conditioning alongside definitely growing the small domestic appliances as well as the large domestic appliances and the component business.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin of 8.24% (up 156 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA was around INR55 crores which increased by around 6% on a year-on-year basis with EBITDA margin reported at 8.24%, which expanded by 156 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Margin improvement from product mix shift (components/SDA/LDA higher margins)
items.quote: So margin improvement will definitely set in FY '27 onwards. So currently, with suboptimal utilization of capacities at Sri City, we believe that Q4 onwards, the capacity utilization would definitely be much better, and that would help us to further improve the overall margins from FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 RAC market degrowth of 30-35% due to unseasonal rains
items.quote: So the June numbers in terms of secondary sale is still not available. Basis the number available for April and May, it seems the market degrew largely up to almost to the extent of 30%, 35%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue mix: RAC 23% (down 34% YoY), SDA 16% (up 16% YoY), components 5-6% (up 556% YoY), LDA 29% (up 29% YoY)
items.quote: Our Components segment delivered standout growth of 5% to 6% year-on-year, supported by a solid order pipeline for PCBs, copper parts, plastic molded components. Our large domestic appliances segment reported a 29% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: New customers added: 8 in SDA, 4 in LDA, 3 in components
items.quote: Out of the 14 customers, 8 of them were for the small domestic appliances and 4 of them for the -- especially for the washing machine business and then 3 of them for the components.

items.statement: Customs issue on copper tube imports unresolved (industry-wide)
items.quote: So the customs issue is linked to imports of copper tube, which the industry does from the ASEAN country and a show -cause notice has been sent to, as per some news articles, to more than 2,000 importers. So that's an industry -wide issue, whic h is jointly taken up by all the industry associations, both with the Ministry and the Government

items.statement: Targeting 30% volume growth in FY26 and 10% EBITDA growth
items.quote: We are targeting a 30% increase in volume this year, and we are on track for that. Along with this, we will continuously be adding new capabilities to fuel growth for coming years.

items.statement: Expect 20% margin decline in FY26-27, recovery from FY28 with backward integration
items.quote: In order to achieve this, we might take a small decline in our margins until FY '27, but this should normalize or, in fact, increase further from FY '28 once the backward integration and specialty wire initiatives kick in.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR700-750 crores for FY26, spent over 2 years including Sanand project
items.quote: Sir, our major capex has been the Sanand project, which is about INR 600 crores and maybe another INR100 crores, INR150 crores on our regular maintenance and upgradation capex and how we will keep on adding volumes capacities to meet the growing demand. So I think it's safe to say about INR700 crores, INR750 crores of capex that we're looking at this year.

items.statement: Adding 60,000 tons capacity in Q2 FY26, another 60,000 tons by Q3 FY26 at Dadri
items.quote: About 60,000 tons is scheduled to be added within the second quarter. And now on volume front, as I said, our guidance has been 30% for this year, and we are on track to achieving this.

items.statement: Sanand project capex increased by INR60 crores to add 60,000 tons wire facility and enable debottlenecking to 2.5 lakh tons
items.quote: Sanand, sir, first thing is that, we've increased our capex by about INR60 crores for 2 reasons. One is that we are putting about 60,000 tons of wire facility, which was not the plan earlier. This is for stainless steel and low carbon wire. And second is, even in the equipment selection, we have tried to select such equipments that after some debottlenecking, we can increas e our capacity from 1.8

items.statement: Specialty wire products (hose wire, IHT, steel cord) receiving overwhelming customer response, import substitution opportunity
items.quote: We are especially focusing on growing a specialty wire segment today, products like hose wire, IHT and steel cord. These import substitute products have received an overwhelming positive response from the customer further setting tone for the future growth trajectory.

items.statement: Hose wire at 20% capacity utilization, steel cord samples sent with positive feedback, targeting commercial production by Q3-Q4 FY27
items.quote: So hose wire, we've already done about 20% kind of a capacity utilization. Apart from that, steel cord, we have already sent samples in the first quarter, and we've already received some positive feedback from customers on sampling bec ause of which why we are now confident of operationalizing this capacity within FY '27, of course, as and when the customer's approval

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA per ton at INR7.2/kg, guiding for 10% absolute EBITDA growth but blended EBITDA per ton may decline to INR6.5/kg
items.quote: EBITDA per ton, as I said, we are looking at a 10% increase in absolute EBITDA. So maybe INR6.5 a kg is the EBITDA per ton that we are looking at. We are at about INR7.2 a kg already in quarter 1.

items.statement: Sanand backward integration to add INR7,000-8,000 EBITDA per ton for steel and stainless steel
items.quote: Sir, for the steel and stainless steel project alone, we are looking at maybe INR7,000 to INR8,000 of EBITDA per ton, that will be added. On a consolidated basis also, if you look at it, we are reducing our EBITDA as per our guidance by 20% in '26 and '27. But this 20% will come back again from the Sanand project alone.

items.statement: Generated INR100 crores free cash flow in Q1 FY26, driven by inventory tightening and debtor days reduction
items.quote: We delivered over INR100 crores in free cash flow from operating activities, driven by tighter management, better working capital discipline an d improved operational efficiency. This performance marks a turning point, and we expect it to only strengthens in the coming quarters

items.statement: Using channel financing (non-recourse) and vendor financing to reduce debtor days, 75-person sales team working on collections
items.quote: First, majority has been in inventory, but we've also started utilizing a lot of other instruments, especially channel financing, which is one way we will be able to reduce our debtor days in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Comfortable taking debt for Sanand project as balance sheet has low leverage, will fund majority of capex through internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, sir. It would be. W e would fund some of it through debt as well because we do not have much leverage on our balance sheet today. items.statement: Cost-plus model passes raw material changes to realization, raw material cost <50% of pricing for export products reducing China disadvantage
