items.quote: 17% to 18%, usually around 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Yarn demand stable, no improvement or deterioration; yarn prices stable in +/-5% band for last 6 months
items.quote: On the demand side, there is not any improvement, but at the same time, not any deterioration also, so it's almost stable. On the prices also last almost 6 months, the price band has been going up plus/minus 5 from either on the demand side or on the yarn pricing side.

items.statement: Power cost benefits: rooftop solar operational but miniscule; third-party STV power starting in 1-2 months; energy conservation initiatives in 6 months; biomass boilers in ~1 year
items.quote: the major benefit is not coming, though th e investment has started happening. But the major benefit, I think will start during the next 3 , 4 months, and it will take us about a year or so to start taking the full benefit of that

items.statement: Cotton inventory longer than usual (beyond Oct/Nov season); roughly equal Indian and imported cotton; imported from US, Australia, Brazil
items.quote: our season starts in the month of October or November. And generally, we have the cott on up to that period. But this time, definitely, we have a little longer cotton compared to that, both Indian and imported

items.statement: Imported cotton share rose from typical 3-4% to ~20% of consumption; may continue buying more imported cotton unless Indian prices fall
items.quote: Normally, we used to import about 3% to 4% of our total consumption of cotton from outside India, which this year, I think we have already done close to about 20% or so. And unless the Indian prices comes down, we may continue to buy more imported cotton.

items.statement: Landed cost: US cotton 1,200-1,400 bps over NY Futures; Brazilian cotton ~800 bps over NY Futures; Vardhman imports from US, Australia, Brazil
items.quote: So the landed cost normally U.S. cotton is available on a basis of 1,200 to 1,300 -- 1,200 to 1,400 basis points over New York Futures. But India is importing vegan cotton, which is spread at about 800 to 900 basis points over New York Futures.

items.statement: Global cotton stocks projected to increase 0.5-1M tons next season per USDA and other agencies; limited upside for global cotton prices
items.quote: So the overall area in the world, there's not really much of change. And we are likely to look at addition of stock in the next financial year -- in the next cotton season also by 0.5 million tons to about 1 million tons.

items.statement: ~9.5-10M spindles permanently stopped in India in last 2-3 years; effective capacity down from 54-55M to 44-45M spindles per industry estimates
items.quote: We understand as of now that the total last 2, 2.5 years, almost 9 million, 9.5 million spindles have been stopped permanently, especially the smaller ones. So, the effective spindle available in India today is estimated -- it was earlier about 54 million, 55 million spindles, which now is estimated close to about 44 million, 45 million spindles.

items.statement: Two key uncertainties: US tariff structure finalization and Indian cotton price trajectory; spinning margins likely to come down unless duty-free import allowed or CCI sells at international parity
items.quote: So, we have 2 uncertainties as of now in our hands. One is the trade barriers or the trade tariffs, which we are not sure of what's likely to happen. And then the -- so we'll have to wait till the time the U.S. decides finally which countries has what -- which kind of a tariff and then accordingly, the margins could be differentiated.

items.statement: Tariff sharing requests: few on spinning side but declined due to margins; fabric side minor one-time adjustments for specific customers, insignificant to overall margins
items.quote: So on the spinning side, we've got a couple of requests, but co nsidering our margins, we could be -- we could explain to the partners that it's really not possible for us to share in the spinning. Fabric side, some specific customers, we have done some small adjustme nts. But that's really very, very insignificant compared to the overall size of the organization

items.statement: Advanced license for cotton import allows ~4.5% effective duty but only for export yarn (1/3 of production); domestic consumption (2/3) cannot use this route
items.quote: So practically, b est case scenario for us to import cotton with a concessional duty of 4%, 4.5% would be about 25%, 30% is the best-case scenario

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of CPP Investments' 49% stake in Island Star Mall Developers (ISMDPL) for Rs 5,449 crore payable over 36 months in four tranches, subject to shareholder and CCI approvals.
items.quote: The agreed consideration for the proposed transaction is Rs. 5,449 crores payable to CPP Investments over a 36-month period in four tranches, subject to applicable laws, and any adjustments including those related to prepayment of tranches.

items.statement: Group capex guidance of Rs 1,200-1,300 crore over the next 12 months.
items.quote: I think about Rs. 1,200 crores to Rs. 1,300 crores over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Residual capex for ISMDPL Phase 2 expansion is roughly Rs 1,000 crore between now and 2027; Phase 3 capex to be shared after approvals.
items.quote: Phase2, which is ongoing at ISML will roughly require about Rs. 1,000 crores between now and 2027 to take it to completion.

items.statement: Capex for next five years (excluding Thane, Coimbatore, Chandigarh) estimated at Rs 5,000-6,000 crore with higher cash flow generation.
items.quote: the CAPEX for next five years would be in the range of around Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 6,000 crores, and against that the cash flow generation will be much higher.

items.statement: Office leasing target of 90% occupancy by 2026 for ~2.2 msf completed offices currently at ~6% leased; strong pipeline in place.
items.quote: Our internal target is to achieve a 90% leasing in 2026, and we have a strong leasing pipeline in place.

items.statement: Leased over 430,000 sq ft of office space in Q1 FY26; expect strong demand for quality office spaces to continue.
items.quote: Overall for the quarter, we have leased an area in excess of 4,30,000 square feet and we expect demand to remain strong especially for these quality well-located office spaces.

items.statement: Retail consumption grew 12% YoY in Q1 FY26 with strong growth at Palladium, Palassio, Ahmedabad, Indore, Pune, and Bengaluru malls.
items.quote: Retail consumption at our malls was strong during Quarter 1, coming in at 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Retail rental income Rs 506 crore, up 4% YoY despite 5-6% impact from planned churn and Courtyard block demolition; expect stronger growth as occupancy stabilizes.
items.quote: For the quarter, retail rental income stood at approximately Rs. 506 crores, up 4% despite an impact from the planned churn at Phoenix Market City malls and also the loss of rentals from the planned convergence (Courtyard) block redevelopment at Phoenix Palladium.

items.statement: Hotel revenue up 11% to Rs 130 crore, EBITDA up 19% to Rs 58 crore in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Our hotel portfolio had a strong performance for the quarter with revenue coming in 11% higher at Rs. 130 crores, and EBITDA showing very strong growth of 19% reaching Rs. 58 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Group EBITDA Rs 544 crore, up 6% YoY in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: overall, if we look at our group leve ls, our EBITDA across the portfolio came in at about Rs. 544 crores, registering a 6% growth

items.statement: ISMDPL platform asset EBITDA Rs 617 crore in FY25 (purely retail); offices not yet EBITDA contributing.
items.quote: In FY25, while the retail EBITDA contribution came in mainly from retail, which was about Rs. 617 crores across four malls.

items.statement: ISMDPL platform operating free cash flow ~Rs 510 crore in FY25 (after interest and tax).
items.quote: The Rs. 617 crores of EBITDA generated by the platform also converted into an operating free cash flow of about Rs. 510 crores for FY25 if you take out interest and tax expense just for the platform.

items.statement: PML standalone operational free cash flow ~Rs 1,225 crore in FY25 excluding ISMDPL; similar run rate could yield over Rs 6,000 crore over five years.
items.quote: If we look at our FY 25 operational free cash flows, they were about Rs. 1,225 crores at the PML level excluding the ISM DPL and its subsidiaries. Now just assume a similar run rate over the next five years without anything else that itself could potentially translate to over Rs. 6,000 crores of operating free cash flows.

items.statement: Group debt Rs 4,435 crore; net debt/EBITDA reduced moderately; cost of debt 7.92% in Q1 FY26, expected to decline with RBI rate cuts.
items.quote: Our Group debt stood at about Rs. 4,435 crores and our net debt to EBITDA reduced moderately from the March ending quarter. We have also seen a significant reduction in our cost of debt. Cost of debt came at about 7.92% for quarter ending June 2025

items.statement: ISMDPL gross debt ~Rs 960 crore, cash Rs 360 crore, net debt ~Rs 600 crore at end FY25; net debt/EBITDA 1x.
items.quote: if I just see the FY25 balance sheet, our gross consolidated debt on the ISM DPL platform was Rs. 960 crores, and our cash on books at the end of FY25 was Rs. 360 crores. So, our net debt is a shade under Rs. 600 crores at this point in time.

items.statement: Acquisition funding via ISMDPL cash flows, dividends, buybacks, capital reduction; minimal secondary purchase by PML until last tranche; PML free cash flows and leverage headroom to fund growth.
items.quote: We have multiple modes of paying this consideration. These include buybacks, payment of dividends, capital reduction and secondary by PML or any of its affiliates. So, this is a combination that we are going to be looking at, and in each year, depending on the cash flows at the ISM DPL level we are going to be affecting dividend payouts or buybacks or capital reduction.

items.statement: Strategic repositioning of Phoenix MarketCity malls (Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Bengaluru) replacing low-efficiency formats with premium brands, flagship inline stores, watches, electronics, beauty; temporary occupancy dip to ~84% in Bengaluru
items.quote: We are actively reshaping the brand mix across these key centers and the broad goal here is to replace low efficiency formats with stronger, better trading brands while also creating more room for high performing flagship in -line stores and other key

items.statement: Phoenix Mall of Asia upper ground 8% vacancy held for luxury/star brands; recent watch brand deals at minimum guaranteed rental ~Rs 550/sq ft/month.
items.quote: Some of the watch brand deals recently concluded are currently at a minimum guaranteed rental of approximately Rs. 550 a square foot (per month).

items.statement: New mall completions: Kolkata (Grand Victoria) and Surat in 2027; Thane Phase 1, Coimbatore in 2029; Chandigarh Phase 1 2029-30; Palladium Mumbai expansion (retail & office) by end 2026/mid 2027.
items.quote: we expect the (Phoenix) Grand Victoria Mall, Kolkata to be completed in 2027. Surat is also expected to be completed in 2027. Thane Phase1 retail is expected to be completed in 2029. Coimbatore retail in the same year, and Chandigarh Phase1 retail between 2029 and 2030.

items.statement: ISMDPL Phase 2: Gourmet Village (19 F&B options) and 400-key Grand Hyatt launching 2026; ~400,000 sq ft offices. Phase 3 by 2030: second hotel ~300 keys, ~1.2 msf offices, ~600,000 sq ft retail.
items.quote: We will be launching the Gourmet Village in 2026, a brand new floor of F&B and entertainment spanning 19 new experiential dining options set in a beautiful theme. With a 400 key Grand Hyatt focused on events, we plan to establish ourselves as one of the most renowned hotels in Bengaluru

items.statement: ISMDPL portfolio: ~4.4 msf operational retail, ~2.2 msf completed offices, planned expansion 0.8 msf retail, 1.6 msf offices, two hotels ~700 keys at Bengaluru.
items.quote: Today, the portfolio comprises ~4.4 million square feet of operational retail space, ~2.2 million square feet of completed offices, a planned expansion of 0.8 million square feet of retail and 1.6 million square feet of offices, along with two hotels totaling approximately 700 keys at the Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore development.

items.statement: Residential gross sales >Rs 168 crore, collections Rs 99 crore in Q1 FY26; average sales price Rs 27,000/sq ft at Kessaku and One Bangalore West; price hikes well accepted.
items.quote: The price hike that we had undertaken in Kessaku and One Bangalore West has been well accepted by the market, and we recorded an average sales price of Rs. 27,000 a square feet for the sales done during Quarter 1.

items.statement: Balanced FSI potential ~2.71 msf across Bengaluru, Pune, Indore (land owned); subject to regulatory approvals and premium payments; capex not yet planned.
items.quote: After accounting for all the expansion plans and the ongoing projects across locations, we continue to have balanced FSI potential across all these developments. It's expected to be at about 2.71 million square feet cumulatively across three cities.

items.statement: Planned churn at MarketCity malls caused temporary trading occupancy dip (Bengaluru ~84% vs 98% leased); further staggered churn planned over coming year; expect occupancy to ramp up as fit-outs complete.
items.quote: At Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore churn is happening, it has come together, so that's why there is a big drop from where we were in December at 98% occupancy to today where we are at about 84% occupancy. And through the rest of the year, the occupancy will go up significantly from here.

items.statement: Infrastructure upgrades (flyover, underpass) near Phoenix Citadel Indore expected ready by 2026, to improve access and footfalls.
items.quote: The new flyover and underpass are expected to be ready by 2026. This not only improves access but also reduces the interim hardship that our mall visitors are currently facing because of the roadworks which have been ongoing.

items.statement: Management commits to sequential quarterly growth and mid-teens EBITDA margin range, but declines to give double-digit FY26 revenue guidance
items.quote: All I said is that we are committing to showing growth every quarter. And that is what we are focused on from an execution perspective that we want to be predictable, we want to be sustainable in terms of our margins, predictable in terms of our growth.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 wage hike impact quantified at $3 million; ESOP plan under consideration with margin impact timing uncertain
items.quote: So, we are looking at somewhere close to $3 million of wage hike impact, which is going to come in Q2.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.2%, down 40 bps QoQ due to sales/marketing investment and higher travel spend
items.quote: Our EBITDA this quarter stood at 15.2%, a drop of 40 basis points quarter-on-quarter. Decline was majorly due to: Investment in sales and marketing, and Increase in travel and other spends.

items.statement: Management targets mid-teens EBITDA margin range inclusive of wage hike and ESOP impacts
items.quote: But we remain committed to making sure that we are in the mid-teens margin range.

items.statement: Macro environment challenging with CIOs pausing net new spending; GenAI demand remains strong with 62% of CEOs identifying AI as defining future competition
items.quote: Overall, macro environment remains challenging with growth slowing in both U.S. and Europe, along with business capital expenditure showing only marginal improvement. We are seeing CIOs pausing on net new spending due to macroeconomic uncertainties.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 order bookings $172 million, up 11.7% YoY; average tenure increasing with more complex managed services engagements
items.quote: Added order book of $172 million in this quarter, which is 11.7% growth Y-o-Y. Average tenure of our order book is increasing with more complex and high-quality engagements, including managed services.

items.statement: Service lines revenue share 68.9%, up 170 bps QoQ and 380 bps YoY; Products & Platforms grew 10.1% QoQ, Cloud Infrastructure & Security 5.2%, Data Engineering & Analytics 2.5%, Enterprise Applications 1.3%
items.quote: The share of revenue from our service lines increased to 68.9% in Q1 FY '26, which is 170 basis points higher quarter-on-quarter and 380 basis points higher year-on-year.

items.statement: Top 5 clients grew ~5%, Top 20 grew ~7% QoQ; $20M+ accounts increased from 4 to 6 YoY; growth broad-based across top accounts
items.quote: No, it is more broad-based. In fact, if you noticed, the number of $20 million accounts have gone up from 4 to 6 same quarter last year was 4, this quarter, it's 6.

items.statement: Hedging strategy shifted to conservative balance sheet hedges only due to extreme FX volatility; outstanding hedges declined 75-80% YoY
items.quote: So, the market is, the FX is like extremely volatile, right? And to that extent, it makes sense to just be as conservative as you can, and that is what we are doing. So, we have moved from certain positions, and we are just focusing on I would say, balance sheet hedges.

items.statement: Experience Services marketing business faces downward budget pressure from AI-driven content generation; Indigo Slate ~$7-8M/quarter not critical but at risk
items.quote: Yes. We are worried about some of the impact that it might happen on particularly the marketing side of the Experience Services business because one of the areas where AI is disrupting significantly is in the marketing space because a lot of content generation is happening using AI.

items.statement: Second-order tariff impact could spread to BFSI and other sectors if US consumer weakens; consumer resilience key to limiting contagion
items.quote: And if there is a consumer weakness on the consumer side, then everything becomes fair game including Banking and financial services, credit card debt, mortgage default, everything becomes a fair game.

items.statement: AI talent developed internally via Ignite AI Academy; GenAI capability enrichment mandatory in all employee L&D plans; no significant AI talent cost inflation vs market
items.quote: AI, we are creating our AI talent ourselves. It is not that all this talent is available in the market. So, AI is such a new technology that we have to create talent from within.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs to normalize next quarter; third-party costs and headcount increases this quarter were one-time
items.quote: So subcon costs will basically come back in line with what it has been previously. There were third-party costs, which have got incurred this quarter, which will kind of get normalized.

items.statement: Avoids vendor consolidation deals as race to the bottom; focuses on innovative solutioning to create large deals rather than rebidding
items.quote: We don't go after existing large deals. We create large deals. So, for us, large deals is about being innovative and solutioning, not about bidding for things which have been bid for rebid and bid for 15 years in the past.

items.statement: Launched ZenseAI GenAI accelerator platform with connected intelligence, multi-modal search, enterprise-grade agentic AI models, responsible AI framework
items.quote: We launched ZenseAI, our GenAI accelerator platform. Our clients have been extremely appreciative of the key features of this platform, namely Connected intelligence, multi-modal search and enterprise-grade agentic AI models.

items.statement: Full-year credit cost guidance kept under 2% of total assets
items.quote: Overall, it will remain under 2% for us for the full year.

items.statement: Exit NIM target of 8.5-8.6% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are confident that we will reach to 8.5% net interest margin for the full financial year by the end of the year.

items.statement: NIM declined 14 bps QoQ to 8.11% due to negative carry from excess liquidity
items.quote: Our net interest margin was 8.11% as against 8.79% in Q1 FY'25 and 8.25% in Q4 FY'25.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost fell to 8.37% from 8.86% in Q4; deposit rates cut 40 bps in August
items.quote: The incremental cost of fund has come down substantially from March quarter which was 8.86% it has come down to 8.37% and we do expect this to further come down.

items.statement: AUM grew 16.6% YoY and 3.4% QoQ to Rs 2,72,249 crore
items.quote: Our asset under management as on 30th June 2025 registered a growth of 16.62% over Q1 FY'25 and of 3.44% sequentially. Our A UM stood at Rs. 2,72,249.01 crores

items.statement: Disbursements rose 13% YoY to Rs 41,817 crore
items.quote: We have registered a disbursement growth of 13. 01% year-on-year. Our disbursements in Q1 FY'26 this year aggregated Rs. 41,816.75 crores versus Rs. 37,001.65 crores in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Gross Stage-3 improved to 4.53% and net Stage-3 to 2.57%
items.quote: On our asset quality, gross Stage-3 in Q1 FY'26 stood at 4.53% and net stage 3 at 2.57%.

items.statement: Credit cost improved to 1.64% of total assets
items.quote: Our credit cost on total assets for Q1 FY'26 stood at 1.64% as against 1.87% for Q1 FY'25 and 2.07% for Q4 FY'25.

items.statement: Stage-2 increase attributed to early monsoon; management confident of roll-back without flowing to Stage-3
items.quote: This time the onset of monsoon was little early than they expected. Typically, monsoon arrives in the mid-June. This time it was in the last week of May in many parts of the country. So, there were some business disruptions here and there. That is the reason Stage-2 went up.

items.statement: MSME disbursement growth slowed QoQ due to seasonal demand; expected pickup in Q2-Q3
items.quote: First quarter is normally slow, but you will see the pickup in the next two quarters. We are still, on the course, for the guidance, to meet the guidance numbers.

items.statement: Used CV and used car financing driving growth; entry-level new car demand shifting to compact SUVs
items.quote: The demand for used cars is increasing. The entry-level car demand used to be mostly in the semi-urban and rural market. Now, we are seeing there is a shift to a higher vehicle, which is compact SUVs.

items.statement: Gold loan opportunity seen from informal-to-formal shift after RBI liberalisation
items.quote: We believe more business will flow in from informal sector to formal sector because there has been little the RBI new guidelines have been little liberal for small-ticket loans.

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q1; total branch count 3,220
items.quote: If you see last year also we added 165 branches this year also first quarter we added 5 branches.

items.statement: Excess liquidity covering 5 months of repayments; target to reduce to 3 months (Rs 18-19k cr) in 3-4 months
items.quote: Overall liquidity continues to be slightly on the higher side which is covering 5 mont hs of our liability repayment. We will work towards reducing this liquidity and this has some negative carry that will come down in next 4 to 5 months

items.statement: Cost of liabilities down 7 bps QoQ to 8.88%; leverage 4.15x; LCR 268.7%
items.quote: The cost of liabilities have come down by 7 basis points in the current quarter from 8.95% to 8.88% now and we do expect this to further come down. The leverage stands at 4.15 times versus 4.16 as of March end number. The liquidity coverage ratio is at 268.74% versus 286.12% as of March.

items.statement: Retail deposits grew 10% QoQ; deposit rate cut 40 bps in August to 7.5-7.6% incremental
items.quote: We have again reduced the rate from the first week of August by 40 basis point. So, effectively our cost for deposit interest rate comes to 7.6 now, which was around 8% plus 8.5 in the beginning of the financial year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio rose to 29.29% from 27.45% YoY
items.quote: Our cost to income ratio was 29.29% in Q1 FY'26 as against 27.45% recorded in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Write-offs Rs 448 crore and provisions Rs 838 crore in Q1
items.quote: For the current quarter it is Rs. 448 crores and provisions are Rs. 838 crores totalling to Rs. 1,286 crores.

items.statement: Fair value gain on mutual funds Rs 134.66 crore included in reported NII; no assignment income this quarter
items.quote: The net gain on the fair value changes was mainly on account of the profit that we earned on the mutual fund investments. For the current quarter, it is Rs. 134.66 crores. The similar figure for the previous quarter was Rs. 111.27 crores. And as far as the assignment income is concerned, since we have not done any assignment deals in the current quarter, no income was recognized.

items.statement: Management does not provide consolidated revenue or EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 or FY27
items.quote: We don't have any guidance. But like I said, overall, some of the variation -- like I think the Coding and Marking business is steady.

items.statement: Coding and marking gross margins dropped a couple of percent; price increase effective 1st August expected to improve margins from Q3
items.quote: a price increase, which we announced about a month or two ago. So that's with effect from 1st August. So practically speaking, it will take one to two months to roll it out because customers are good at negotiating and all our other type of stuf f. But what we should do is start seeing an effect from Q3 in terms of the coding and marking business margins

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA declined due to packaging business losses; track and trace near breakeven
items.quote: Essentially, the EBIT that has decreased at a consolidated level. It's mainly because we had certain losses in the packaging business. I think the track and trace, in fact, this quarter is close to breakeven.

items.statement: Track and trace business focused on two large pharma customers in top 10; rollout ongoing
items.quote: we are fully occupied with these two large customers. So, of course, in stages, only when they sign off, then the billing gets com plete and things happen. So it's definitely these are the two. I'd say, the two large customers, both in the top 10 easily of India, if not

items.statement: May invest ₹10-15 crores in pilot equipment for recyclable packaging material R&D and small-scale production
items.quote: In terms of CapEx, there may be because we are working on the recyclable material for the Packaging business. Although it's more of an R&D expense, we might buy ₹10 crores to ₹15 crores of some pilot type of equipment for like lab, our lab lines.

items.statement: Coding and marking capacity can scale from ₹400 crores to ₹600 crores revenue without significant CapEx or manpower
items.quote: In the Coding and Marking business, I think we can go from about ₹400 crores, what we're doing right now to at least ₹600 crores without adding any types of CapEx or any significant manpower.

items.statement: Standalone Q1 revenue mix: printers 11%, consumables 62%, spares 12%, services 14%
items.quote: For the Q1 of FY '25-'26, the breakup between the printers, consumables, spares and services is 11%, 62%, 12%, 14%.

items.statement: Coding and marking business targets 14-15% growth for next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think like our overall target is to continue growing the Coding and Marking business at, say, whatever growth we're used to doing in the past, something similar like maybe 14%, 15%. I think that's our target to keep growing at that rate for the next two, three years at least.

items.statement: No direct competitive pressure in V-Shapes mono-dose packaging due to patented technology; competing against sachets, thermoforms, other single-serve formats
items.quote: So there is no competitive pressure because as a patented technology. So we are competing against different technologies. So some people might use lik e sachets will probably be the biggest, I think, use of single -use packaging. Thermoform is another

items.statement: Purchase of stock-in-trade increased due to packaging division buying machines from CP Italy and materials from Europe for domestic sales
items.quote: In India in the stand-alone thing, we got a separate division called Packaging division, which purchases machines from CP Italy and sells it to the local domestic customers in India. So that is the reason why like in this quarter, we have sold two machines. So the purchase cost was there for these two machines.

items.statement: GST benefit for Guwahati plant ended 26 May; Q1 impact ~₹1.5-2 crores; annual benefit was ₹10-12 crores
items.quote: Yeah. So the Guwahati benefit is over. I think it was close to ₹10 crores, ₹12 crores a y ear, if I'm correct. So that is thing that -- already we could see like about maybe ₹1.5 crores of impact on Q1. So that was already there. ₹1.5 crores, ₹2 crores in Q1

items.statement: Consumables protected by RFID; printers only work with Control Print inks, inks not sold for other printers
items.quote: So we have a protection on our printers with our RFID technology. So in general, like you can't really use someone else's ink on our printers. And neither do we provide our inks for use o n other people's printers

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 revenue growth guidance of 15-20% excluding defence contribution
items.quote: We stand by our guidance, what we had given last time, 15% to 20% growth. This year also, we expect.

items.statement: Reaffirmed target to become a $1 billion company
items.quote: Yes sir, we still stand by it, and we'll do it.

items.statement: Finance cost guidance of INR90 crores and depreciation of INR60 crores for FY26
items.quote: The overall finance cost would be in the range of INR90 crores, and depreciation would be in the range of INR60 crores about, including all expansion.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin expected at 9.5-9.7% for FY26
items.quote: Sir, right now, in this quarter, we have done almost 9.74%. We hope the overall margin should be in the range of 9.5% to 9.7% in this current year.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube EBITDA margin expected at 15-16%
items.quote: It should be almost in the range of 15% to 16% EBITDA margin in this hydraulic tube.

items.statement: Defence products EBITDA margins expected to start from 25-35%
items.quote: But I hope, in all the defence products, EBITDA starts from 25% to 35%.

items.statement: Debottlenecking can increase infrastructure capacity from 1 lakh to 1.5 lakh tonnes
items.quote: Sir, right now, if you talk of infrastructure, the re is a debottlenecking, it can take it up to the current capacity, which is 1 lakh tonne. It can go to 150,000 tonnes because they are debottlenecking with the space

items.statement: Hydraulic tube plant at 50% utilization in Q1, targeting 70% for FY26
items.quote: Sir, in this quarter, we have achieved almost a 50% utilization. And in the coming quarters, we hope as this tariff war stabilizes, then it can go up to what we expect. In this year, we will achieve a capacity utilization of almost 70% in this financial year.

items.statement: Defence plant targeting 40-50% utilization in FY26, 90% in FY27
items.quote: So basically, in this financial year, we expect a 40% to 50% capacity utilization in FY '26.

items.statement: Defence plant revenue potential INR270-275 crores at full capacity
items.quote: The revenue, which we are expecting, it is just on the basis what the future will tell, but we hope it should be between -- when full capacity will be utilized, it should be almost INR270 crores to INR275 crores.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube plant revenue potential INR1,250-1,300 crores at 90% utilization
items.quote: When this -- it will go to 70% to 90% with our hydraulic tube business. Here, we have put up this plant for a turnover of almost INR500 crores. So before starting this, we were at INR750 crores. And when it goes to 90%, we hope a turnover we will get in this segment, it will be almost INR1,250 crores to INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: Domestic demand slowed in second half of Q1 due to money supply crunch and government fund flow issues
items.quote: Look, there was a slowdown in the later half of the quarter, slowdown in the Indian market and slowdown internationally also has happened. Why this has happened? We have yet to understand. There was money supply, crunch was there, government funds not flowing, government orders not flowing out.

items.quote: So I think our first intent would be to get back to those levels and I would wait for another quarter to give you some kind of a future path. But save that , I can give you one commitment, you will see quarter-on-quarter improvement from here on

items.statement: Remediation at Goa Plant-2 expected to be mostly complete by August 2025, with FDA inspection possible from September 2025.
items.quote: We expect to finish most of it by August this year, which is coming month. Some of the updates will continue to go to F DA for until December this year, b ut they keep getting updates from us and when are we ready to? I think from September any time, we should be able to reach out to FDA to ask them to come and audit us.

items.statement: Master manufacturing program Phase-1 rolled out in Q1 FY26; all plants expected operational by end of Q2 FY26, with full efficiency visible in Phase-2 from Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So by end of Q2 now, so come Q3, from day 1, we should have all plants up and going.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected to be around Rs. 50 crore incrementally, focused on completing ongoing projects at Goa Plant-2 and Warren Remedies API site.
items.quote: So I am not expecting anything more t han around Rs. 50 Cr incrementally to be put in CAPEX this year.

items.statement: R&D spend expected to be maintained at 5-5.5% of sales; 4-5 product filings planned for FY26.
items.quote: But by and large, we keep it at 5%. I think we should be able to maintain that 5%-5.5%.

items.statement: Debt repayment of Rs. 68 crore planned over remaining 9 months of FY26 after Rs. 21 crore repaid in Q1.
items.quote: In remaining 9 months, we will be repaying about Rs. 68 crores as per our current plan.

items.statement: Sterile product supply to US from Goa Plant-2 expected to show impact by Q3 FY26 after FDA allowed restart of 2 of 4 lines.
items.quote: So I would say by Q3, Q3 is a good quarter in which we should be able to see some impact coming i n from supply of sterile to US.

items.statement: European business expected to bounce back to regular supply levels by Q3 FY26 after supply challenges resolve by end of Q2.
items.quote: So by Q3, you will see Europe bounce back to its regular levels of supply.

items.statement: Warren Remedies OTC business expected to take a couple of years to reach EBITDA breakeven; Q1 FY26 was EBITDA positive.
items.quote: We would want to wait for a full couple of years before we see a breakeven happen at Warren Remed ies.

items.statement: Domestic formulation business grew 5% YoY and 14% QoQ in Q1 FY26; secondary sales per IQVIA grew 10% vs industry 8% with top 4 segments in double-digit growth.
items.quote: So when it come s to absolute secondar y, as we call them that is the primary impact sometimes weighs between Q4 and Q1. But at secondary level, there is a good 10% growth in the performance of products and almost all top 4 segments, Anti-infectives, Respiratory, GI, as we ll as Stomatologicals are in very healthy double digit growth.

items.statement: OTC business grew more than 46% QoQ in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: I am happy to share that the OTC business has shown great improvement and we have seen a growth of more than 46% over immediate preceding quarter this year.

items.statement: Emerging markets formulation revenue grew to Rs. 443 million from Rs. 298 million YoY, driven by brand building and sales structure revamp across French West Africa, LATAM, and Asia.
items.quote: And there has been a good growth in demand for our products on the ground. And therefore, we are seeing this kind of growth in semi -reg markets. The growth is uniformly seen in various territories across French West Africa, rest of Africa, LATAM and other Asia as well.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% in Q1 FY26 from 1% in Q4 FY25; consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.1% from negative in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA to net sales for the quarter is 3.9% compared to 13.1% for the same quarter last year. For the immediately preceding quarter, we were at 1%.

items.statement: Remediation costs continue at ~Rs. 4 crore per quarter for Goa Plant-2.
items.quote: Remediation continues. We continue to spend close to around Rs. 4 crores per quarter.

items.statement: International solid oral exports grew >26% QoQ in Q1 FY26 due to master manufacturing program Phase-1 rollout.
items.quote: our master manufacturing program which was almost near completion has seen a Phase-1 rollout in the 1st Quarter this year and this is seen in the increase of more than 26% in international business, solid oral exports which we have seen in this quarter.

items.statement: US formulation revenue declined to Rs. 283 million from Rs. 487 million YoY; Europe revenue declined to Rs. 635 million from Rs. 754 million YoY.
items.quote: Revenues from US business are at Rs. 283 million against Rs. 487 million. For Europe, for the quarter, we are at Rs. 635 million against Rs. 754 million

items.statement: Goa Plant-2: US FDA allowed manufacturing restart on 2 of 4 lines; European authorities approved sterile product supply from the plant.
items.quote: US FDA has allowed manufacturing to start from 2 out of 4 lines in the plant. Also, as of last evening, we heard the happy news that European au thorities have approved the plant for sterile product supply to Europe.

items.statement: Master manufacturing program: 3 of 4 plants fully operational in Phase-1; all 4 expected by end of Q2 FY26.
items.quote: out of the 4 plants we talked about last time, 3 are now completely on. But as part of Phase-1, the manufacturing has begun.

items.statement: Finance cost increased due to ~Rs. 5.5-6 crore MTM FX loss; underlying finance cost slightly higher due to borrowing exposure.
items.quote: As regards to finance cost, it includes certain FX loss on account of mark to market. That includes close to about Rs. 5.5-Rs. 6 crores.

items.statement: New products contribute ~4.5% of domestic topline; several new launches in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Also, new products continue to do well and they are at close to 4.5% of the topline. This quarter also, we have launched several new products.

items.statement: Prescriptions for 8 of top 9 brands growing in double digits; Cyclopam secondary sales grew 11.4% vs market <6%.
items.quote: Prescriptions also for 8 of the 9 top brands of the Company are in double -digit growth. So I am not reall y concerned about the hygiene of the branded business.

items.statement: European GMP approval received for sterile products from Goa Plant-2; US FDA warning letter remediation ongoing with inspection targeted by December 2025.
items.quote: European au thorities have approved the plant for sterile product supply to Europe. This speaks well of all the efforts we have taken at the plant for remediation and to meet with global standards of manufacturing.

items.statement: Consolidated debt at Rs. 951 crore as of June 30, 2025 (short-term Rs. 350 cr, long-term Rs. 600 cr), down Rs. 21 crore from March 2025.
items.quote: overall debt level at consolidation level, short term is Rs. 350 and long term is Rs. 600. Both put together Rs. 950 crores as of 30th June, 2025.

items.statement: Capital infusion planned for Warren Remedies (negative net worth Rs. 52 crore) over next 3 quarters; no infusion needed for FPP Holdings.
items.quote: Are we going to infuse capital in Warren Remedies as it has a negative net worth of Rs. 52 crores to strengthen its balance sheet in coming 3 quarters? Aditi Panandikar: Yes

items.statement: MR productivity average 3+ lakh per man; acute divisions 3.5-4 lakh; target to add 25,000 incremental productivity per man by year-end.
items.quote: I am confident by end of this year, we should be able to add at least 25,000 per man by way of incremental PHY.

items.statement: Brinzolamide and Combigan US launches from Goa Plant-2 delayed; evaluation possible only by Q4 FY26 due to complex suspension manufacturing.
items.quote: Quite honestly, it is better to look at probably Q4 this year as a time for when we can start evaluating the Ophthal business to the US and its performance.

items.statement: Domestic formulation secondary sales growth 10% vs IPM covered market 8% in Q1 FY26 per IQVIA.
items.quote: if you look at the IQV IA analysis of 1st Quarter performance, then for the industry, Q1, for the covered market, there has been a growth of 8 % and for Indoco Remedies, the growth is 10 %.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guided at 20-22% and PAT margin at 15-16%
items.quote: the guide sits at 20% to 22% on the EBITDA and 15% to 16% on the PAT

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA and PAT margins within guided range despite higher sales, R&D and employee costs
items.value: EBITDA Rs. 68 crore, PAT Rs. 51 crore
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT came in at Rs. 68 crore and Rs. 51 crore, respectively, with margins pretty much within the guided range

items.statement: Order book exceeds Rs. 1,450 crore strengthened by 16 new logos across key markets
items.quote: These wins have further strengthened our order book, which now exceeds Rs. 1,450 crore

items.statement: Added 16 new logos across key markets and expanded into Europe, Egypt and Africa
items.quote: This quarter saw a series of strategic wins, adding 16 new logos across key markets and facilitating our expansion into se veral new geographies, notably Europe, Egypt, and another place in Africa

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity ramp-up for TIG hardware over FY26-27 estimated at Rs. 40-50 crore total
items.quote: over FY26 - '27, you are talking of probably Rs. 40 crore to Rs. 50 crore

items.statement: Sales team expanded with step-jump additions in Europe (6 sales hires), North Asia and Africa
items.quote: we have added six sales guys in Europe along with the supporting pre-sales and other investments that will enable that team

items.statement: Sales expense jumped ~80% due to geographic expansion; R&D spend at 9.2-9.3% of revenue
items.quote: I think sales expense has gone up almost 80% or so

items.statement: Launching AI-native applications: new retail/SME loan origination, LMS, supply chain finance, trade finance with Fintra, transit and data center products
items.quote: We are launching a brand new retail LO, SME LO, the most cutting-edge AI-led origination system in the market today, we believe

items.statement: Banking segment grew 31% YoY to Rs. 192 crore; TIG grew 25% YoY to Rs. 145 crore
items.value: Banking Rs. 192 crore, TIG Rs. 145 crore
items.quote: banking segment delivered Rs. 192 crore, registering a strong 31% year-on-year growth. TIG posted a revenue of Rs. 145 crore, reflecting a solid 25% year-on-year increase

items.statement: Data center business is slightly less than one-third of TIG revenue for FY25
items.quote: slightly less than a third of the business is data center for TIG

items.statement: Transaction banking competes with 4-5 specialized players; enterprise AI stack targets financial institutions unlike C3.ai/Palantir
items.quote: there are four or five specialized players in the space, including like one more Indian one and then those are the ones we compete with

items.statement: R&D tax reliefs in jurisdictions like Singapore contribute to lower effective tax rate (~18-19% in Q1)
items.quote: one of the joys of being a R&D focused organization is you do tend to get the opportunity to claim some tax relief against R&D in like several places, especially, jurisdictions like Singapore

items.statement: Headcount increased due to acquisitions, annual increments, performance incentives and sales hiring in new geographies
items.quote: driven by a rise in headcount following recent acquisitions, as well as annual increments and performance incentives

items.statement: Fintra joined Aurionpro to build strategic trade finance blueprint
items.quote: this quarter was especially fruitful with Fintra joinin g Aurionpro to help build a critical part of our strategic blueprint for trade finance

items.statement: Revenue recognition skewed by project go-lives taking 12-14 months
items.quote: it usually takes 12-14 months for that to come in

items.statement: IP largely resides in Singapore and Dubai; R&D centers in Istanbul, London, Singapore, Vietnam
items.quote: A lot of our IP resides in Singapore, and a lot of our business gets done out of Singapore or Dubai

items.statement: Refreshed brand identity reflecting shift to product-first, innovation-driven global technology company
items.quote: This quarter, we also introduced our refreshed brand identity, which reflects Aurionpro Solutions shift into a product -first, innovation -driven, global technology

items.statement: Management targets mid-teen disbursement growth over the medium term and aims for non-Wheels business to reach 25% of mix by FY30.
items.quote: It is important for us to at least target a mid-teen growth, whether it's a disbursement growth, which will then lead to a book growth, which will lead into earnings growth, etc., etc.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 growth guidance not given; Q1 was muted but management expects tailwinds to drive growth in remaining quarters.
items.quote: I would be more keen to not give very immediate guidance. So, the midterm guidance, yes, the aspiration is to be at a mid-teen growth.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY26 is 1.3% to 1.7% of assets; GS2+GS3 target kept below 10%.
items.quote: we would like to operate in the 1.3 % to 1.7%. Last year, more than 1.3 % to 1.5%. But think of it like we would want the credit cost not to go more than 1.7%.

items.statement: NIMs believed to have bottomed out at 6.5%; fee income and incremental cost of funds improvements support margin expansion.
items.quote: I did comment last time that we do believe our NIMs have bottomed out at 6.5%. We do look at abilities to lever up on whether they are pricing capabilities or their cost of funds.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds trending down quarter-on-quarter; 3-year LCD cost at 7.10%-7.20% after repo rate cuts.
items.quote: So, if you look at, we kind of have, it should be in the range of a 7.10% to 7.20% kind of range, three years LCDs.

items.statement: Tractor disbursements grew 21% YoY, gaining market share; overall disbursements flat at 1% growth.
items.quote: The key highlight for the quarter was a standout growth in the tractor lending business. We saw a 21% disbursement growth. By virtue of the disbursement growth, we have been able to gain market share.

items.statement: SME disbursements declined due to org rejig into four zones; book grew 28% YoY.
items.quote: Our SME business did see a decline in disbursements. Nevertheless, the book grew at 28%.

items.statement: GS2+GS3 at 9.7% in Q1, same as Q1 last year; intra-quarter volatility lower than previous year (57 bps vs 123 bps increase).
items.quote: Our collection performance was quite steady. If you recollect, we have always said that our GS2 plus GS3, we target to be within the 10% range. Q1 came in at 9.7 %.

items.statement: Credit cost increased marginally due to 20 bps PCR coverage increase vs 340 bps release last year; underlying losses stable.
items.quote: Between Q4 and Q1 last year, we had close to 340 bps reduction in PCR cover, which would have given a release in provision. I mean, this year between Q4 of 25% in Q1 this year, we have seen a 20-bps kind of coverage increase.

items.statement: Collection efficiency improved ~100 bps vs Q1 FY24/FY25; segment-wise collection teams created to manage Q2 seasonality.
items.quote: considering Q1 collection efficiencies of the FY '24 and '25, we are about 100 bps up in Q1 of this year. So, the collection engines have worked reasonably well in this environment.

items.statement: Completed migration to cloud-based loan management system in June; all June disbursements on new LMS stack.
items.quote: we have completely Mahindra & migrated from our in-house tech stack, which is the loan management system. We did a complete cutover in the month of June. So, nearly all of June disbursements happened on the new cloud - based LMS stack

items.statement: No further capital raise planned; Tier 1 at 17.9%, debt-equity 4.75:1 post Rs3,000 cr rights issue; well capitalized for growth.
items.quote: We are, I think, very, very well capitalized. It would not be prudent for us, especially now. And we are 95%-plus secured businesses, right? So, we did want to equip ourselves well enough to equip ourselves for high growth.

items.statement: Rs46 cr dividend from MIBL (100% sub) included in Q1 PAT; expected to be recurring given MIBL's capital-light model and Rs540 cr cash surplus.
items.quote: This PAT includes the Rs.46 crores dividend payout from MIBL. This is not a one-off. We plan to have this as a recurring item going forward. Given the current future cash flows of MIBL.

items.statement: Employee count flat QoQ; apparent decline due to on-roll to off-roll shift; employee cost up 11% YoY.
items.quote: in Q1, we have kind of moved a certain kind of count of people from the on-roll to off-roll, and that's why I think employee count is looking lower in Q1. Otherwise, our overall employee count is flat quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Post-tax ROA at 1.6% for Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Overall, our post-tax ROA for the quarter was at 1.6.

items.statement: Banks aggressively pricing in vehicle finance; Mahindra Finance leverages 6,000+ dealer relationships and micro-market immersion as moat.
items.quote: Banks are being extremely competitive, vehicle as a category is getting intimated by mainstream banks. But we do have our moats in terms of, I did not mention we participated 6,000 dealerships. We are very relevant to that

items.statement: PSL assets from tractor growth used for securitization/on-lending to manage cost of funds.
items.quote: Our treasury teams have managed to leverage the priority sector book very well. Because of our increased tractor business, we will still have a lot of good PSL assets to offload either through on lending or through sectorization to keep the cost of funds at a decent level.

items.statement: Entry-level PV stress prolonged due to high vehicle prices and middle-income earning pressure; CV segment challenges in mining and price discovery.
items.quote: the entry-level car segment is seeing some stress for quite some period of time because of the buying of the, let's say, the middle-income households are seriously not, either the prices of the vehicles are too high or there is an earning pressure.

items.statement: Write-offs as % of opening/average assets stable despite 40% YoY absolute increase; managed within credit cost guidance.
items.quote: If you look at the write-off as a percentage of opening assets or the average assets, you will see that is largely in the stable zone, right?

items.statement: Aspires to achieve 20% EBITDA CAGR over the next two years, not formal guidance
items.quote: We're also seeing a strong momentum in our enterprise business, focusing on increasing wallet share, securing new clients and becoming the preferred partner in India's OTT space, supporting our goal of 20% EBITDA CAGR growth over the next two years

items.statement: Expects growth numbers to kick off from Q2 FY26 onwards
items.quote: Number two, the 20% CAGR growth, yes, we have a solid plan fro m this quarter, Q2 onwards. You will see the growth. You'll see the numbers kicking off from Q2 onwards

items.statement: AI-native platform deal signed with leading Southeast Asian telco for 3.5 years, subscription per user per month
items.quote: We have closed the deal for 3.5 years and starting from, I mean, this quarter onwards.

items.statement: MaaP platform deployed with two large Indonesian telcos (Telkomsel 52%, Indosat 25%), awaiting third operator Axiata
items.quote: We closed the deal with two telcos, which is Telkomsel and Indosat. Telkomsel represents around 52% and Indosat represents around 25%.

items.statement: ValueFirst India and Singapore acquisitions completed; global entities pending RBI approval, no timeline given
items.quote: We have completed the acquisition of ValueFirst India and ValueFirst Singapore. The other global companies of VF, while we intend to acquire, is pending RBI approval.

items.statement: Enterprise SMS volumes growing but price realisation lower due to competitive pricing pressure
items.quote: What we see from an enterprise SMS -- purely SMS perspective is that A, the volume continues to grow; B, we continue to win new RFPs and wallet share, as I said; and three, it's not reflecting on the revenue stream because of the price sensitivity, right?

items.statement: OTT channels (WhatsApp, RCS, Truecaller) driving growth; traffic shifting from SMS to OTT for better user experience
items.quote: WhatsApp continues to do very well. I think both WhatsApp, RCS, and TrueCaller, all three other channels from an OTT perspective is contributing for the growth.

items.statement: Targeting operating/gross margin of 25-26%; margins currently at multi-quarter low due to GTM and tech investments
items.quote: We have earlier called out that we will be happy in operating our operating margin or gross margin of 25% to 26%. But with the new ambition that we have set for ourselves, I think it has to slowly improve from here on to meet our EBITDA targets as well, right?

items.statement: Margin improvement to come from both top-line growth and efficiency gains from new deal revenues
items.quote: I would say it would be a combination of both the top line growth as well as efficiency-driven gross margin improvement and indirect costs.

items.statement: WhatsApp utility pricing per transaction has not decreased; effective price increased after 24-hour window removal
items.quote: Effectively, price has not come down. In fact, it has gone up, if you really see.

items.statement: Domestic SMS market remains price-sensitive with aggressive competition eroding realisation
items.quote: We have seen a lot of price aggressivene ss with our competition. Maybe some of those have settled, but there are still players, one or two, which are a little bit competitive, which has eroded our realisation versus the volume growth

items.statement: Omnichannel approach: SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, Truecaller, Email, Voice offered as bouquet; use cases moving to OTT for better experience
items.quote: When we go to the customer, we offer omnichannel experience. When I say omnichannel, it is SMS. It is all the OTT channels, that is RCS, WhatsApp, even TrueCaller, right? E-Mail, voice, everything has been it's a bouquet of services are offered to the customer.

items.statement: SBI deal renewed effective 1st April, fully baked into Q1 FY26 revenue and gross profit
items.quote: SBI deal, as I said, it's a continuity of our services, and we got the renewal of the RPF again this term. This is effective 1st April, so the volumes that we see is for the full quarter, both in terms of the gross profit and the revenue topline.

items.statement: Continuing to win new enterprise logos and increase wallet share in India domestic enterprise business
items.quote: we continue to win new logos. We continue to mine the accounts that we are in and continue to win market share in our existing business and overall wa llet share, if we have to call out from an India domestic enterprise business perspective

items.statement: Investing in Indonesia: recruiting people and planning to open office in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We are also planning to set up an office there in this quarter. So, we are investing in Indonesia in a big way, okay? We have recruited people, and we are planning to open the office there.

items.statement: AI-native platform to go live by first week or mid-August, generating revenue from Q2 FY26
items.quote: we believe that we will go live by first week or sometime mid-August, that will start generating revenue and profit from quarter two

items.statement: MaaP platform with Indonesian telcos to go live in coming weeks, revenue share from Q2 FY26
items.quote: Similarly, our MaaP platform, which we have deployed with the two large telcos outside India should go live soon in coming weeks. That should also start giving us a revenu e share from a market perspective

items.statement: Announced ₹175 crore buyback via tender route (window 29th July to 4th August); total shareholder returns near ₹1,000 crore over 5 years
items.quote: We also announced a ₹175 crores buyback, bringing our total shareholder return to nearly ₹1,000 crores over the past five years through dividends and buybacks, all while maintaining a zero-debt balance sheet.

items.statement: Open market buyback no longer permitted under regulations; tender route chosen
items.quote: Open market offer is no more there as part of the regula tions. And hence, we have gone ahead with the tender

items.statement: Anubhav Batra appointed as CFO designate; Abhishek Jain thanked for contributions
items.quote: I would like to welcome Anubhav as our new CFO and also would like to thank Abhishek Jain for his contribution. We wish him all the best.

items.statement: Platform revenue declined in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 despite SBI deal; management calls it a blip, no major customer losses
items.quote: I would say it was a blip and a small minor drop in the last two quarters. No major customer exits or no major business that has fall off.

items.statement: ILD revenue consistent at higher single-digit % of revenue, lower single-digit % of gross margin; no major near-term impact expected
items.quote: ILD revenue has been pretty consistent for last one, two quarters now. It is higher single-digit from a revenue contribution perspective and lower single-digit from a gross margin contribution perspective.

items.statement: AI-native platform claimed to have no direct competition; major customer announcement expected around 10th August
items.quote: I don't wa nt to hide that from this esteem customer. I want them to speak, this is going to be a major announcement, okay? So, you'll get to see the announcement coming from th e customer directly

items.statement: ValueFirst global acquisition pending RBI approval; company clarifying questions, no date committed
items.quote: The other global companies of VF, while we intend to acquire, is pending RBI approval. We are working with them and clarifying all the questions that they have.

items.statement: 20% EBITDA CAGR is an aspirational stretch target, not guidance; management under internal pressure to achieve
items.quote: And of course, just to clarify to all that, it's not a guidance, right? It is an aspiration that all of the management team has come together. And to be honest, we are putting pressure on ourselves because we are taking the stretch target to achieve this.

items.statement: Loan growth target for FY26 is 14% to 16%
items.quote: We are targeting around 14% to 16%. That is what the guidance we have given. So, we will continue with that 14% to 16% we should be able to achieve.

items.statement: NIM guidance to stay above 3%
items.quote: And our guidance is that we'll stay above 3% as far as the NIM s is concerned. And we'll ensure that our NIMs stay above 3

items.statement: DTA on business losses to be consumed by Q4 FY26; move to lower tax regime next year adding 9-10 bps to ROA
items.value: Rs. 65-70 crore tax payment; ~Rs. 900 crore benefit; 9-10 bps ROA upside
items.quote: we estimate that whatever the DTA on account of business losses, that we should be able to consume entirely by Q4. And in Q4, by taking a small hit of, I mean, actual payment of tax to the tax authorities of say, Rs. 65 crores-Rs. 70 crores roughly, w e should be able to move to the new tax regime and in our calculations, next year onwards, it should give us a positive side of roughly around Rs. 9

items.statement: NIM at 3.16% for Q1 FY26; conscious decision to avoid sub-6% corporate loans to protect margin
items.quote: NIM, that is net interest margin, which stands at 3.16 %. And cost to income ratio has also improved. Earlier, it was 57.71%. Now, it got reduced to 55.43%.

items.statement: SMA-0 reduced from Rs. 537 crore to Rs. 353 crore, already regularized; SMA-2 only 9 accounts totalling Rs. 69 crore
items.quote: On the SMA, I think it's a very minuscule amount that is there and the SMA-0, now already Rs. 353 crores. Already it is upgraded, it is regularized and we do not have any issues as far as the SMA-0, 1 and 2 is concerned in the credit this one.

items.statement: Trade finance platform closed ~Rs. 3,200 crore with turnover ~Rs. 18,000 crore; discounting only corporate-accepted bills at 60-90 day tenure
items.value: Rs. 3,200 crore portfolio, Rs. 18,000 crore turnover
items.quote: I think this time we have closed by around Rs. 3,200 crore and with a turnover of around Rs. 18,000 crores.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth reduced consciously due to pricing below 6%; RAM portfolio grew 15.71% (Retail 17.51%, Agri 12.70%, MSME 15.94%)
items.quote: It is a very conscious decision from our side that we do not want to lend at the rates what the corporates were demanding. So, this is also because our investment yield is almost 6.71%. There is no point in giving that 5.85%-5.80% just to show the topline.

items.statement: Corporate loan pipeline focused on data centres, logistics, select manufacturing, government-backed entities; LRDs also seeing repricing opportunities
items.quote: See, actually, mainly the areas where we are finding the scope is in the data center, logistics, and only one or two manufacturing sectors, not more than that. And much is on the government or government-backed entities, whether it is the NTPC or the IRDA, like that.

items.statement: Recruiting ~2,000 credit officers; induction expected in a month
items.quote: this time we have specifically gone for around 2,000 credit officers. That almost that indent is done and then people will get on boarded after a month or so.

items.statement: Signed shareholders agreement, trademark licensing and distribution agreements with Generali for life and non-life JVs; launch pending ROC name change approval
items.quote: we have already signed shareholders agreement, trademark licensing agreement and distribution agreement with Generali. And in the last week of this month, once the name change approval comes from the ROC, that we will be ready for launching this with the new name.

items.statement: MCLR cuts limited to 10-20 bps in Q2 vs 100 bps repo transmission on repo-linked loans; deposit rates not falling as fast
items.quote: 60-70 bps may not be. 10-15, 20 bps max. Again, it depends on the cost of deposits and how low the cost of deposits can go.

items.statement: NBFC lending at MCLR-based 9%-9.05%; bank not budging on rates despite competition
items.quote: NBFC, MCLR-based rates and we are getting 9%-9.05% kind of rates even now.

items.statement: Retiral benefit fund targeting self-sufficiency by Dec 2027; providing minimum required contributions quarterly
items.quote: we have taken a consistent stand that we want to make this fund self-sufficient by December 27. And so, whatever extra required over and above the calculation, we are providing it for.

items.statement: Airline account: favorable Singapore arbitration decision, execution in Delaware legal process ongoing
items.quote: Airline account, now there is a favorable decision from that Singapore arbitration that execution has to happen in Delaware. That is the thing that is happening. It is a legal process. It is taking some time for that.

items.statement: SARFAESI notices issued for extra property with Bank of Baroda; awaiting bids from 1-2 evaluating customers
items.quote: we have published that. That is on the public notice that we have published , SARFEASI notices. I think one or two customers are evalua ting, whatever the prospects and bids, we are just waiting for that.

items.statement: No revision in Agri/Gold loan targets despite RBI collateral guidelines for small loans; will continue existing plan

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY26 maintained at 5.5%-6% with second half run rate of 3%-3.5%
items.quote: we are saying that obviously, first half, the credit cost will be elevated and in second half, the run rate will be 3%-3.5%.

items.statement: Retail finance mix target of 12%-15% of AUM by FY28
items.quote: What we have guided is around by end of the year 2028, we should reach anywhere between 12%-15%.

items.statement: MFI book sustainable growth of 13%-15% with overall growth of 20%-25% including retail finance
items.quote: I think in a normal scenario, MFI book should grow in the early teens, maybe around 13%-15%. And along with retail, we projected that the overall growth should be 20% plus, 20%-25% kind of range.

items.statement: OPEX to AUM ratio expected to drop below 5% by end of FY26
items.quote: So, this OPEX, which is today around 5.1, it may stay at that level in Q2. And then Q3, Q4 as the growth picks up, we should see that ratio again dropping below 5.

items.statement: Karnataka additional credit cost guidance maintained at 1%-1.25% but subject to Q2-Q3 stabilization
items.quote: So, we would want to keep it there. But however, like I said, we will have to see how Q2 pans out and how we stabilize in Q3, right?

items.statement: PAR 15+ accretion rate improved to 0.46% in June 2025 from 1.34% in November 2024
items.quote: The PAR 15 plus acquisition rate stood at 0.46% in June '25 compared to 1.34% in November '24.

items.statement: Karnataka PAR 15+ accretion rate at 0.58% in June 2025 down from 2% peak in February 2025
items.quote: Karnataka is gradually inching towards stabilization with new PAR 15 plus accretion rates significantly being controlled at 0.58% for the month of June '25 from a peak of 2% in February 2025.

items.statement: Write-off of Rs.693 crore in Q1 FY26 including accelerated write-off of Rs.603 crore for 180+ dpd accounts
items.quote: In Q1 FY26, we undertook write-off of Rs.693 crore which included an accelerated write-off of Rs.603 crore related to 180 dpd plus non-paying accounts leading to an additional credit cost of Rs.193 crore for the quarter.

items.statement: Collection efficiency excluding arrears at 93.2% for Q1 FY26 and 93.5% for June 2025
items.quote: Our collection efficiency excluding arrears stood at 93.2% for Q1 FY'26 while being 93.5% for the month of June FY'25.

items.statement: PAR 90 at 3.29%, GNPA at 4.70%, Net NPA at 1.78% as of June 2025
items.quote: PAR 90 stood at 3.29%, GNPA of 4.70% and net NPA of 1.78%, both predominantly measured at 60 plus DPD.

items.statement: Stage-3 provision coverage at 63%, slightly lower due to Karnataka low-risk districts moving to Stage-3
items.quote: Stage-3 provisioning, today we are at roughly around 63%. It is slightly lower than the last quarter because the Karnataka book where majority of the districts are classified as low risk has flown forward to Stage-3.

items.statement: 40%-45% of early bucket PAR customers making partial payments
items.quote: So, less than 60 days PAR, partial paying customers at a company level, as well as Karnataka is roughly around 40%-45%.

items.statement: AUM-based market share increased by 70 bps in FY25 to 6.9% of microfinance industry
items.quote: We have strengthened our market position amid multiple headwinds, increasing our AUM -based market share by 70 basis points during FY '25 to reach 6.9% of the overall microfinance industry.

items.statement: Added 2.16 lakh borrowers in Q1 FY26 with 43% new-to-credit; 33% of borrower base unique to CA Grameen
items.quote: We added 2.16 lakh borrowers in Q1 FY '26 of which 43% were new -to-credit, maintai ning a consistent trend quarter -after-quarter. As a result, 33% or one -third of the borrower base is unique with CA Grameen as of June '25 compared to 26% in August '24.

items.statement: Retail finance portfolio share increased from 2.9% to 6.8% of AUM YoY
items.quote: Our retail finance portfolio, the strategic growth lever, witnessed significant increase in YO Y share from 2.9% to 6.8% at end of June 2025.

items.statement: 3-year loans share in GL book rose to 44.3% in Q1 FY26 from 33.3% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: At the same time, it is important to highlight the increasing share of 3-year loans in GL book, rising to 44.3% in Q1 FY'26 from 33.3% in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Borrowers with >3 pre-lenders reduced to 11.1% of GLP from 25.3% in August 2024
items.quote: Referring to slides 10 and 11, GLP of borrowers with greater than 3 pre-lenders stood at 11.1% in June 2025 versus 25.3% in August 2024.

items.statement: Borrowers with >Rs.2 lakh unsecured indebtedness reduced to 9.5% of GLP from 19.1% in August 2024
items.quote: GLP of borrowers with greater than 2 lakh unsecured indebtedness stood at 9.5% as of June 2025 compared to 19.1% in August 2024.

items.statement: Opened 54 branches in Q1 FY26; targeting ~200 branches for full year FY26
items.quote: On an average, we do around 200. This year also, we should do around 8% to 10%. So, roughly around 200 branches we should add this year. We've done 54 in Q1, and we will spread this out over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: NIM steady at 12.8% for Q1 FY26; cost of borrowings declined 8 bps to 9.7%
items.quote: NIM remains steady at 12.8% for Q1 FY'26. Cost-to-income ratio stood at 33.5% while PPOP stood at Rs. 656 crore in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowings declined 8 bps to 9.7% at end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: We observed a decline of 8 bps in our average cost of borrowings to 9.7% at the end of Q1 FY'26, having remained stable at 9.8% over previous 7 quarters.

items.statement: Raised Rs.2,570 crore in Q1 FY26 including maiden US$100M multi-currency syndicated social loan
items.quote: During Q1 FY'26, we raised Rs. 2,570 crore which included partial drawdowns from our maiden US $100 million multi-currency syndicated social loan comprising of Japanese Yen and US dollars denominated combined.

items.statement: Targeting 25%-30% foreign borrowing by FY28
items.quote: We remain confident of building on this momentum as we work towards our strategic objective of achieving 25 %-30% foreign borrowing by FY'28.

items.statement: Sanctions in hand of Rs.3,093 crore and Rs.6,500 crore in pipeline; funding currently only against microfinance book
items.quote: Additionally, we have sanctions in hand of Rs. 3,093 crore and another Rs. 6,500 crore worth of sanctions in pipeline.

items.statement: Employee base grew to 21,333 from 20,970; annualized attrition at 27.1% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our employee base grew from 20,970 employees in March ' 25 to 21,333 employees by the end of June ' 25 while maintaining lower annualized a ttrition rate of 27.1% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Higher attrition in Tamil Nadu seen as BFSI-wide pattern; maintaining higher bench strength
items.quote: With respect to attrition , over the last two quarters, we have been able to kind of stabilize headcount across all states. However, we do see slightly higher attrition in the state of Tamil Nadu, which is more or less I am seeing this as a pattern across BFSI, not necessarily microfinance.

items.statement: Customers per loan officer at ~320 currently; expected to revert to historical averages post accelerated write-offs
items.quote: Just to add to the point of customers per loan officer, currently it stands at around 320. And we have accelerated write off what we are taking, which is resulting in lower customer base. But we do expect that post -September when the accelerated write-off is completed, this number will revert back to our historical average.

items.statement: No lending rate increases in past few quarters; not contemplating near-term rate hikes
items.quote: So, we have not increased rates for the past few quarters. That media article was kind of quoting what is published on the website as well as comparing it with portfolio yield. So, on a QOQ basis, our average lending rates have not increased.

items.statement: MFI portfolio cap relaxation from 75% to 60% will lead to phased diversification across industry
items.quote: Similarly, with this higher room, I think a lot players will step in to experiment into adjacent asset classes, could be mortgage, some of them could be other asset classes that they are confident about. But I think this will grow in a phased manner.

items.statement: Karnataka PAR 15 accretion still above normal; expecting further drop by end of Q2, stabilization view by Q3
items.quote: But we are hoping that by end of Q2, we should see further drop in new PAR accretion in Karnataka. And we will have to kind of watch Q3 to see where this will settle d down.

items.quote: We would now like to place before you the guidance for the year. items.statement: Gross loan book grew 11% YoY and 4% QoQ to INR33,287 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1, our gross loan book delivered a growth of 11% Y-o-Y and 4% Q-o-Q, reaching INR33,287 crores.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 24% YoY to INR6,539 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The disbursements in the quarter grew to INR6,539 crores, registering a strong growth of 24% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Secured portfolio share rose from 31% to 46% YoY
items.quote: The rising share of our secured portfolio from 31% to 46% Y-o-Y underscores the calibrated strategy to diversify our product suite and enhance portfolio quality.

items.statement: Group loan disbursements in Q1 were 2% higher than Q4 despite MFIN Guardrails 2.0 adoption
items.quote: While we had anticipated a slower disbursement, we observed that demand scenario improved and Q1 disbursement in group loan was 2% higher than Q4.

items.statement: Added ~1.1 lakh new micro banking customers and graduated ~34,000 group loan customers to individual loans in Q1
items.quote: We added approximately 1.1 lakh new customers in micro banking during Q1, while ensuring healthy borrower profiles. items.statement: PSL requirement for SFBs reduced from 75% to 60%, giving flexibility to calibrate portfolio mix
items.quote: Recently regulatory changes were introduced, reducing the Priority Sector Lending requirements for small finance banks from 75% to 60%. This move marks a significant positive shift and gives the bank enhanced flexibility to calibrate its portfolio mix.

items.statement: NIM expected to be ~7.9% in Q2-Q3 and stabilize at 7.8% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We expect our NIM to be closer to 7.9% in Q2, Q3 and stabilizing at 7.8% by the time Q4 comes.

items.statement: Peak FD rates cut by 65 bps, SA rates recalibrated up to 100 bps; cost of funds already down 21 bps QoQ, further 30 bps reduction expected
items.quote: what we have done is peak FD rates have been cut by 65 basis points and savings account rate calibration has also been done in a few buckets up to 100 basis points as well. We see further reduction coming to the exte nt of 30 basis points based on our plan

items.statement: X-Bucket collection efficiency at 99.34% in June'25, expect 99.5%+ by Q3 FY26
items.quote: X-Bucket collection efficiency of the micro banking book remains strong at 99.34% for June '25, reflecting repayment discipline. We are witnessing improvements in collec tions environment and expect to touch normalized levels of 99.5% plus by

items.statement: Slippages peaked in 9 of 10 states in Q4, Karnataka peaked in Q1; expect improving trend
items.quote: Our slippages in micro banking had peaked in 9 out of 10 states in Q4, and we foresee Karnataka peaking in Q1. Slippages are expected to show an improving trend going forward.

items.statement: Accelerated provisions of INR23 crore taken in Q1; unutilized floating provision of INR21 crore as of June'25
items.value: INR23 crores accelerated, INR21 crores unutilized floating
items.quote: As was the case in Q4 and Q3 of FY24-25, this improved scenario did not necessitate sale of NPAs to ARC in Q1. Bank continued the prudent approach of taking accelerated provisions of approximately INR23 crores in Q1 and additionally holds unutilized floating provision of INR21 crores as of June '25.

items.statement: Housing portfolio (affordable housing + micro mortgages) grew 53% YoY to ~INR8,000 crore
items.quote: Our housing portfolio comprising affordable housing and micro mortgage loans has delivered impressive growth of 53% Y-o-Y in loan book, reaching approximately INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: Micro mortgages grew 227% YoY and 24% QoQ to ~INR900 crore
items.quote: Micro mortgages, a higher yielding, lower ticket product continues to contributes roughly INR900 crores to the portfolio, registering a strong growth of 227% Y-o-Y and 24% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: MSME loan book grew 59% YoY to INR2,253 crore; working capital & supply chain finance now 24% of MSME book
items.quote: MSME business continued to witness an impressive loan book growth of 59% Y-o-Y, reaching INR2,253 crores. Working capital and supply chain finance now account for over 24% of our MSME book, reflecting the growing traction in our business banking segment.
