items.quote: look at bulk TD, we are now sourcing at 7.69% and average tenure is around 1 year. Rajiv Mehta: Okay, 1 year. Hitendra Jha: And retail, we are now sourcing at 8.09% Q1, which, as Mr. Nautiyal said, going forward, it will be come down

items.statement: Plan to open ~25 branches in FY26 and ~400 branches over next 4 years
items.quote: This year, we are planning to open around 25 branches. And over the next 4 years, we may open around 400 branches. That is the overall plan.

items.statement: Umesh Arora joined as Head of Emerging Businesses overseeing Housing, MSME, Agri banking
items.quote: Before I conclude, I would like to introduce Mr. Umesh Arora, who has joined as our Head of Emerging Businesses. He holds a rich experience of over 25 years and has held senior leadership roles in retail lending, credit and asset businesses across reputed banks like Axis Bank, IDBI Bank, Standard Chartered Bank and Utkarsh Small Finance Bank. He would be overseeing the departments of Housing, MSME

items.statement: GNPA expected to be contained below 2.5% going forward; credit cost normalized by Q4 FY26
items.quote: So you can say that the GNPA would be contained below 2.5% as we go forward.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance 2.3-2.4% of avg gross loan book for FY26; steady-state unsecured 2-2.25%, secured 0.7-0.8%
items.quote: credit cost to be in the range of 2.3% to 2.4% of average gross loan book. ROE to be 10% to 12% and ROA to be around 1.2% to 1.4%.

items.statement: PCR projected at 75-77% range during FY26; INR21 crore unutilized floating provisions not counted in PCR
items.quote: So we would be hovering in the range of 75% to 77% during the course of the year. That is what the projections are telling us. We still would have INR21 crores of unutilized provisions that we are not using for computation of PCR.

items.statement: Karnataka microfinance stress: PAR 7.4% in IL (up from 6.8%), issues in Belgaum, Davangere, Tumakuru, Ramanagar due to ordinance; Bengaluru metro performing well
items.quote: We have excellent portfolio quality in Bangalore and urban market, as I mentioned. We see still some kind of issue in certain districts like Belgaum, Davangere, Tumakuru and Ramanagar, which contributes close to 10% of our estate portfolio and which is majorly impacted due to ordinance issue. Otherwise, state portfolio is doing excellent.

items.statement: Individual loan yield ~100 bps higher than group loan yield
items.quote: And as far the yield is concerned, IL yield is close to 100 basis points higher than GL.

items.statement: CGFMU cover at INR649 crore; will continue quarter-on-quarter based on portfolio situation
items.quote: Yes, we have started doing CGFMU from the Q4, and we continued in Q1 as well. And we intend to continue this. This gives a very good coverage, and we will continue to do as part of the portfolio coverage going forward as well.

items.statement: Expects to maintain annual CAGR of close to 15%
items.quote: By consistently executing strategic projects and optimizing efficiency, we are well in position to maintain our annual CAGR of close to 15%.

items.statement: Incurred Rs 7,003 crores capex, 70% of total planned; Rs 4,900 crores capitalized
items.quote: As Q1 FY '26, we have incurred up to Rs. 7,003 crores in capital expenditure, representing 70% of our total planned CAPEX. Of this, close to Rs. 4,900 crores have been capitalized.

items.statement: Carbon steel capex operational by FY26; stainless steel and aluminum by FY27
items.quote: As stated during our call, most of our carbon steel CAPEX is expected to become operational by FY '26, with the stainless steel and aluminum projects on track for commissioning in the year FY '27.

items.statement: Remaining Rs 3,485 crores capex to be spent over next two years from internal accruals
items.quote: In this quarter, we spent Rs. 419 crores, and the remaining Rs. 3,485 crores shall be spent over the next two years from our internal accrual and from cash generated from our operations.

items.statement: Pig iron plant utilization at 104% in Q1 FY26; color coated unit at close to 70%
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, the pig iron plant recorded a utilization rate of 104% while color coated unit reached close to 70%, indicating a healthy ramp-up and positive momentum.

items.statement: Pig iron facility currently operating at more than 120% rating, producing 2,700 tons vs guaranteed 2,100 tons
items.quote: And today, I am very happy to say that we are operating the pig iron facility at more than 120% rating presently. And this is something, none of the company in India is operating the capacity of the pig iron at this capacity.

items.statement: First 90 MW captive power plant in Odisha commissioned; second 90 MW in Bengal expected by end August or early September
items.quote: We have commissioned the first 90 megawatts of Odisha, and the second 90 megawatts of Bengal plant is under the final stage of commissioning, we expect that by end of August or early September we should be able to commission that as well.

items.statement: Stainless steel wire plant operating at 30-35% capacity; expects to sell 10,000 tons in FY26 and ramp to 20,000 tons next year
items.quote: In the stainless-steel wire, we just commissioned the plant and presently, we are operating at close to 30% - 35%. items.statement: Color coating capacity to double from ~200,000 tons to 450,000-500,000 tons by end FY26 with galvalume line 2 commissioning
items.quote: This year, we have the flat product, this color-coated business and HR and all what we are doing right now, we are more than doubling. So, from close to 200,000 tons approximately what we should be able to do this year, we are ramping up to close to 450,000 to 500,000 tons. So, by end of this year we will be commissioning this project.

items.statement: Blast furnace expected to produce close to 800,000 tons in FY26 at 120% utilization
items.quote: We will be able to produce at 120% like the capacity of the blast furnace what we have installed, and I am sharing we will be able to do close to 800,000 tons this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 operating EBITDA margin at 13.12%, up from previous quarter due to new pig iron and color-coated products
items.quote: And operating EBITDA margin in Quarter 1 of the current financial year was 13.12%. This margin, mainly increased over the previous quarter, is on the back of our performance of a newly introduced product, pig iron and color-coated steel.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to sustain between 11-13% for FY26, no downside seen
items.quote: We are working between 11%, 12%, 13 % EBITDA. So, I think the days -- I do not see anything will go further down. We expect that we should be able to do decent. It's Shyam Metalics & very difficult to project anything on the margin side, but yes. I do not see anything on the downside hence further for this year

items.statement: Captive power generation cost at Rs 2-2.5 per kWh using waste heat and byproducts, reducing grid imports
items.quote: So, most of our power plants are based on the fuel rejects and waste heat gases and all. So, our cost of generation is close to Rs. 2 to Rs. 2.5 a KWH. So, it is going to enhance the bottom line because the cost is going to be more competitive.

items.statement: Finished steel accounts for 76% of total revenue in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The sales mix constitutes a high percentage of volume from finished steel, which accounts for 76% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Aluminum foil demand improving with margins; transition phase of 3-4 months before better numbers reflect
items.quote: See, definitely there is a good spurt in the demand in the aluminum foil and the margins are definitely improving, but people are carrying over with their own inventories on the sales side as well as on the buy side. Generally, all these things take some transition phases in the level of three, four months. We will start seeing more and more better numbers in the time to come.

items.statement: Stainless steel wire exports started; customer approvals progressing well with world-class compliance
items.quote: We are overcoming all the challenges of stability, and we also have started the export market, started exporting the material. So, this year we will be stabilizing our market, and I expect that we should be able to sell close to 10,000 tons of wire this year.

items.statement: Pig iron facility operating at 4.5 rating vs industry standard 3.5; fuel consumption very competitive vs peers
items.quote: If you see, generally, the blast furnace is operating at 3.5 rate. Like, I will just give you an example like, today we have set up a 600 cubic meter blast furnace. And for a 600 cubic meter blast furnace, the optimum capacity what is guaranteed generally is close to 2,100 tons. But constantly, we are producing 2,700 tons today, which is close to 4.5 rating.

items.statement: Government policy announcements on railway, roadways, civil aviation, gas pipeline, affordable housing and budgetary allocation to drive steel demand
items.quote: We expect with a reasonable strong demand recovery on the back of recent policy announcements made by the government towards railway, roadways, civil aviation, gas pipeline, towards affordable housing and the incremental budgetary allocation to this sector is likely to drive the demand for both long steel and as well as in stainless-steel.

items.quote: See, this is a monsoon time and these three months are generally challenging months, starting from July, August, September. items.statement: Aluminum business expected to grow >250% in next couple of years; focusing on niche high-return products like battery foil, automotive components

items.quote: For '25, '26, we have given a guidance of upward of 25%. So, it will be very premature to give any guidance for '27, '28.

items.statement: Electrolyte Salt segment revenue expected at INR15-20 crore in FY26
items.quote: More or less, yes. Anywhere between INR15 crores to INR20 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex plan of INR110 crore for new block at existing site for agro intermediates
items.quote: We have a new block coming up. So that is to accommodate the missing parts which we require to achieve the full volumes that the customer wants for the new agro intermediates

items.quote: So until May, it was not fully occupied, but now I would say most of the capacities are occupied and we have started becoming selective in terms of what we want to make and what we want to avoid.

items.quote: The second approved product is now being manufactured at plant level, and we are on track to dispatch the material within the current quarter. In a significant development, another customer engaged in manufacturing batteries for hybrid vehicles has also approved our material and placed their first small-scale commercial order for extended

items.statement: SDA demand revival: China negligible, US/Europe picking up, stronger demand visible in Q2-Q3
items.quote: Still the Chinese demand is nearly negligible, whereas the U.S. and the Europe demands have actually picked up. And it is gradually still picking up and we see stronger demand coming in Q2 and Q3.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 14.8% (+287 bps YoY) due to 4.1% COGS decrease partly offset by 1.2% other expense increase
items.quote: EBITDA margin increased by 287 bps year-on-year basis to 14.8% in Q1 FY '25 due to decrease in COGS by 4.1%, but partly offset by increase in other expenses by 1.2% Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Margin expansion expected through FY26 driven by mix shift to SDA and exports (71% vs 61% prior quarter)
items.quote: This shift has started to happen. So, the numbers start becoming more healthy. And this we will see going forward as well in the Q2 that the shift towards more of SDA and healthier sales happening from Q2 will have even better numbers in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Exports 71% of revenue in Q1 FY26 (INR830 mn); major markets Japan, USA, Germany, Malaysia, Switzerland, South Korea, China
items.quote: During Q1 FY '26, exports stood at INR830 million, contributing 71% of the revenue. The major countries include Japan, USA, Germany, Malaysia, Switzerland, South Korea and China.

items.statement: CFO Ashok Bothra departing to pursue another opportunity
items.quote: Our CFO, Mr. Ashok Bothra, has decided to relocate himself and pursue another opportunity. It indeed has been a pleasure to work with him. We will surely miss him, and we wish him the very best for his future endeavours.

items.statement: US reciprocal tariff uncertainty; most products currently not subject but abrupt changes possible
items.quote: The global geopolitical landscape remains fragile and also there exists a lot of uncertainties pertaining to U.S. reciprocal tariffs. As of today, most of the products which we sell into the U.S. markets are not subject to reciprocal tariffs, but we continue to remain cautious owing to possible abrupt changes that can happen in the system.

items.statement: Contribution margin reached 60% in Q1 FY26, up from 50% a year ago; management guides for high-50s steady state.
items.quote: Last year, in the same quarter, we were at 50%, so significant improvement there. We have set high 50s, so we want to just leave some room for quarter on quarter aberrations.

items.statement: Management targets 15-20% EBITDA margin over the next two to three years.
items.quote: We do think that what we had said earlier about 15% to 20% EBITDA Margin over the next two, three years is still the number to drive towards.

items.statement: Payment services business operated at breakeven in Q1 FY26; management expects it to become a large profit driver when UPI MDR returns.
items.quote: I do believe payment is a profitable business. Like you're seeing, without UPI, MDR, we are talking profits. And I do believe the payment channel is profitable and has operating leverage.

items.statement: DLG-based disbursements have declined very significantly; partner AUM under DLG is down over 40%.
items.quote: I can tell you that that number is down, even that AUM number is down over 40%. So you can imagine that the new disbursements are significantly lower under DLG than before DLG.

items.statement: Both personal and merchant loan disbursals and revenue grew sequentially; mix remains roughly the same as last quarter.
items.quote: Both personal loan and merchant loan grew last quarter, both in terms of revenue and disbursals and also the mix is roughly the same as it was last quarter.

items.statement: No significant recovery yet in personal loans; growth is linear and sequential.
items.quote: No, not significant recovery. It is linear.

items.statement: POS devices accepting credit cards have increased; RuPay credit cards on UPI now generate MDR-bearing revenue.
items.quote: Yes. Actually, you pointed out the correct thing. The net payment margin is going to grow because of credit card, EMI, and let's say, loyalty point or any other high-margin processing payment instrument.

items.statement: Subscription prices for POS devices were increased (e.g., from Rs 100 to Rs 129) with no merchant churn due to superior product quality.
items.quote: So, sometimes if you were charging Rs 100, we are charging Rs 129 now. And we are able to do it because the customer loves it. And the stability and robustness gives a premium to it.

items.statement: Capex and refurbishment efficiency have improved significantly, supporting lower subscription revenue per device focus on lifetime value.
items.quote: As a part of our overall subscription revenue per device, because we have become extremely efficient on capex and refurbishment, we are not looking to drive up subscription revenue per merchant necessarily.

items.statement: Madhur Deora stepping down from board after ~2.5-3 years to focus on business initiatives; General Counsel nominated as executive director.
items.quote: I've been on the board for about two and a half, three years, and there was never the intention that this should be a permanent thing. We wanted one executive director on the board, so I did a term, and now our General Counsel is being nominated for this.

items.statement: Financial Services Revenue was Rs 561 crore in Q1 FY26; lower QoQ due to reduced DLG but merchant disbursements grew strongly.
items.quote: If you read Financial Services Revenue Rs 561 Crores, it is overall, if you see quarter on quarter, and the number is, because of DLG not being there, this number is lesser.

items.statement: Lenders have voluntarily foregone DLG requirements due to strong portfolio performance and regulatory clarifications.
items.quote: It is the same lenders who have decided to forego DLG-based math because they see the book performing great for their references.

items.statement: BNPL and personal loan resumption depends solely on recovery in sub-Rs 50,000 personal credit market; no wallet dependency.
items.quote: It was rather the small credit issue that exists in the market, less than Rs 50,000 credit due to that, and that is the only single KPI that materially matters to the lenders.

items.statement: Collection costs are down significantly QoQ and YoY due to lower personal loan AUM and shift to distribution-only model.
items.quote: Our collection costs are down quite a lot, on a sequential basis and also on a year on year basis, because especially in personal loan, our partner AUM, which is under the collection model, is down quite a lot.

items.statement: POS pricing increased from Rs 100 to Rs 129 with no churn due to product superiority
items.quote: So, sometimes if you were charging Rs 100, we are charging Rs 129 now. And we are able to do it because the customer loves it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve significantly from current ~4% by end of financial year
items.quote: We do see significant improvements in EBITDA margin between now and the end of the year. We're currently at about 4 percent, but that is like 4 percent just in the first quarter that you have hit profitability.

items.statement: Payment market has 4-5x growth potential from current levels driven by UPI expansion and merchant base growth
items.quote: So we continue to see that payment has 4-5x growth left in this country from today.

items.statement: App homepage now payments-heavy; non-payment upsells deprioritized to drive retention and engagement
items.quote: The app homepage, for example, is very, very much payments heavy. And a lot of the things which might have been distracting users or it might have been cross-sell, upsell have been sort of deprioritized.

items.statement: Merchant lending with partners is a star performer with enormous tailwinds and conservative risk management
items.quote: Merchant lending has been fantastic with our partners and really been a star. And we run that business very conservatively. But it just has enormous tailwinds.

items.statement: Net device deployments lower due to pickups of inactive devices; gross deployments higher but conservative accounting writes off devices >12 months with no transactions
items.quote: We may have deployed higher devices at a gross level, minus the devices picked up. So while the absolute deployments are larger, we are reporting only the net.

items.statement: Company has been AI-first across all customer products and internal processes for last 1.5 years
items.quote: Every customer product and every internal process should be AI first. And that's something which we're not seeing as sort of a thing that we're going to start to do. That has been the posture of the company internally for the last one and a half years.

items.statement: POS hardware and software stack considered far superior to Chinese copy competitors enabling premium pricing
items.quote: Our hardware, software, stack, et cetera, work out incredibly better. And that gives our product a premium level in the market.

items.statement: No visibility on MDR for large merchants; business not based on regulatory hopes but on current profitable operations
items.quote: we are as aware as you are. So no extra comment or input that we discover. So we will go by what happens and get informed. We are not basing our business on one hope of the future

items.statement: Personal loan recovery expected in 2-4 quarters per partner conversations; company waiting for cycle recovery rather than pushing growth
items.quote: Our partners tell us it's maybe two, three, four quarters away, right? And ultimately, it's their decision when they want to lend more.

items.statement: EMI product differentiated by 5-party subvention model, card offers for small merchants, and brand advertising integration on consumer app
items.quote: One of the biggest differentiation in our product versus many others who were in the market when we entered, is that we have at least five parties that can subvention the cost of financing.

items.statement: Soundbox charged over 2 years, EDC over 3 years; becoming more conservative on device useful life accounting
items.quote: If you know we charge the soundbox in two years and the EDC in three years. Now we wrote off a lot of these devices which were more than 12 months old and we didn't see transactions.

items.statement: Refurbishment hubs in India enable dramatic cost efficiency vs competitors; manufactured devices locally for capital efficiency
items.quote: We do dramatically more refurbishments than anybody else even adjusted for relative scale because we manufactured these devices in India, refurbishment hubs are in India and so on right.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 28-31% expected to continue at least at current levels in future quarters
items.quote: We do think in future quarters that number should be at least that much, if not higher.

items.statement: Revenue per financial services customer doubled despite flat customer count due to merchant lending strength
items.quote: Our revenue has doubled despite this number remaining slightly flat. Which I think is sort of positive. On the other hand, I do understand that that is not as helpful a metric for modeling as we may have initially expected it to be. Because our revenue per financial services customer in a sense has doubled.

items.statement: POS provider model with banks/brands started as very small part of business; not considered as attractive as direct merchant model
items.quote: We have also started as a very small part of our business, partnering with banks and brands on what we call this POS provider model. But that we don't think is as attractive as a model.

items.statement: POS provider model doing significantly less than 10,000 but more than 5,000 units per month
items.quote: In a month, we should do significantly less than 10,000, but a little more than 5,000.

items.statement: Reverse price elasticity observed: higher prices work because product stability and robustness commands premium
items.quote: By paying large, because our products are far superior than competition in the market, everybody else is a Chinese copy; our hardware, software, stack, et cetera, work out incredibly better. And that gives our product a premium level in the market.

items.statement: Enterprise POS opportunity large but deeper penetration via payment gateway model and device spectrum (QR, Soundbox, Card Soundbox, Android machines) seen as larger opportunity
items.quote: However, we think that a larger part of that opportunity is probably in taking these card machines a bit deeper. And for that, you need to have the payment gateway model that we have.

items.statement: Credit card on UPI not progressing at previously guided 5% of GMV pace; Rs 50,000 ticket loan overhang cited as factor
items.quote: It is rather the Rs 50,000 ticket loan kind of thing that is overhanging on it.

items.statement: Non-UPI GMV contribution declining; RuPay credit card and EMI will grow but not faster than UPI due to limited card base
items.quote: Faster is the wrong word because of the very reason that there is still a finite number of people who have RuPay Credit Card and that number is not very large, because the common people are using more and more UPI.

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; focus on profitable growth and internal efficiency
items.quote: We are rather committed to continue to drive profitable business even today.

items.statement: Management confident of exceeding 18-19% USD revenue growth guidance for FY26
items.quote: So, at this point in time, we are very confident of going past the 18%, 19% number. In fact, I was just having a debate with Raj before this call whether we should put up 20% at this time.

items.statement: Financial Services vertical grew 48.4% YoY and 21.3% QoQ; expected to exceed 40% growth in FY26
items.quote: We are fairly upbeat about the gro wth momentum in Financial Services. You will all know that last year, Financial Services grew by about 60% on a Y - o-Y basis. We would ideally want to replicate a similar performance this year. But at this point in time, we're fairly confident that the business could deliver a growth in excess of 40

items.statement: Consumer goods showing early revival signs with new wins and CIO/CTO traction
items.quote: There are also some early signs of revival in consumer goods. I don't want to specify numbers here at this time because it's still a little of early days. However, we did have new wins in this quarter.

items.statement: Strong order book provides confidence for 18-19% growth; robust pipeline
items.quote: In terms of current order book, we have a fairly strong order book, which gives us reasonable confidence to deliver the 18% to 19% growth that we've been talking about. In terms of the pipeline, again, the pipeline continues to be fairly robust and healthy.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 21.4% reported, 22.2% adjusted; wage hikes impacted margins by ~3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins, for this particular quarter came in at about 21.4% , this is on a reported basis. And on an adjusted basis, excluding the transaction-related costs for the Decision Point acquisition came in at about 22.2%.

items.statement: Expect to recover wage hike margin impact over next couple of quarters through pyramid restructuring, onsite/offshore mix, utilization
items.quote: And therefore, we will look at all other levers. This could be pyramid restructuring , it could be looking at the on-site/offshore mix as well as looking at utilization, all of these are levers that we typically look at to sort of bring back the margins to normative levels or historical levels.

items.statement: Building Databricks Center of Excellence with identified leader; expanding GTM and sales team (1 joined, 2 more offers made)
items.quote: We are also in the process of expanding the GTM and sales team on the Databricks side. One of the peop le has already joined us. There are 2 more roles. We have made a few offers, and we expect to close them fairly quickly

items.statement: GenAI/Agentic AI Center of Excellence staffed with 10 people (5 internal, 5 external hires) plus PhD interns; $6M confirmed work, $8M pipeline
items.quote: At this point in time, for the current year, we already have $6 million of work confirmed on GenAI and agentic AI, and there is another $8 million of work that is in the pipeline that we are actively engaged, and we expect to close.

items.statement: Chief Client Officer Krishnan Venkata departing after 17 years; his teams now report directly to CEO
items.quote: Our Chief Client Officer, Krishnan Venkata, who had been with us for 17 years, he decided that to take a break and pursue opportunities elsewhere. His last date wi th LatentView will be the 8th of September

items.statement: Attrition at 23%, considered manageable; seasonal uptick post bonus payout
items.quote: In fact, we are pleasantly happy to note that this year, that number is, I would say, while it's at 23%, it's not gone up significantly in comparison to immediately preceding quarter.

items.statement: Rationalizing intercompany loans to overseas subsidiaries; new transfer pricing structure on cost-plus basis
items.quote: And going forward, the one update that I would like to give to all the analysts is that we are looking to rationalize some of the loans that have been given to our group companies.

items.statement: Wage hikes effective April 1st higher than normal, mainly on variable/performance pay; external consultant engaged for comp benchmarking
items.quote: You would all note that we had indicated that we plan to roll out wage hikes effective 1st of April and the wage hikes that were sort of given in this year, I would say, was slightly higher than normal, not on so much on the fixed compensation side, but more on the performance and the variable pay side.

items.statement: Won 7 new accounts in Q1; 3 with high growth potential (could reach $5M in 12-18 months); 2 new FS accounts added in last 6 months showing strong growth
items.quote: So first off, you would have seen that we won 7 new accounts this quarter. More than the fact that we had 7 additions to our logos, I'm really happy about the quality of the new client deals that we are bringing on board.

items.statement: Recognized by Magazine as top player in GenAI/Agentic AI PeMa Quadrant
items.quote: This quarter also saw u s getting recognized by Magazine as one of the top players in the GenAI and the agentic AI space as part of their PeMa Quadrant, and we are really proud about that outcome

items.statement: Focus on integrated transformation in consumer goods combining R&D, supply chain, and revenue growth management capabilities
items.quote: We are starting to see the emergence of conversations where these capabilities can be integrated into one holistic kind of an approach, driving true digital transformation for them.

items.statement: Doubling down on SAP data migration capabilities following Databricks-SAP partnership announcement
items.quote: And finally, at this point in time, we are also doubling down on building competency around SAP data migration. You would all know that Databricks has announced a solid partnership with SAP.

items.statement: Organic business grew 2.8% in USD terms (1.6% in INR due to rupee appreciation); core tech flat due to one-off project endings
items.quote: But the other point that I did forget to mention, by the way, in dollar terms, the underlying business grew by about 2.8%, whereas in rupee terms, and that's the numbers that you guys have access to right now, the underlying business grew by only about 1.6%.

items.statement: Q2 expected to catch up Q1 dip and stay on track for 18-19% full year guidance
items.quote: So the second quarter numbers will not only be on track for the 18%, 19% that we have guided. In fact, it will also catch up with the slight dip that you have seen in the first quarter.

items.statement: Decision Point acquisition completed 1 year ago; Q1 revenue INR 22.2 crores; expect to significantly accelerate Decision Point business
items.quote: This, by the way, concludes 1 year since we acquired Decision Point and of course, going forward, the goal will be to significantly accelerate that business.

items.statement: Decision Point growth expected to outstrip organic business due to small base and positive momentum in CPG
items.quote: I would expect that the growth will, in fact, outstrip the organic business because they are coming off a small base, if you remember, and they also had a dip in quarter 4.

items.statement: Forex gains from intercompany loans (INR 6 crores in Q1) will not continue as loans are rationalized; steady-state EPS expected
items.quote: And going forward, you may not see this level of forex gain or losses. And therefore, you will see steady state, I would say, EPS numbers going forward.

items.statement: Elected to move from old tax regime (29%) to new tax regime (25%) for India business; one-time deferred tax benefit
items.quote: We also had the benefit of an election to move from the old tax regime to the new tax regime in this particular quarter, the tax rate that the business will pay going forward from some 29%, this is for the India business from 29% to 25%.

items.statement: Rupee appreciation against dollar reduced INR revenue growth vs USD growth (2.8% USD vs 1.6% INR)
items.quote: So there is a currency impact in this particular quarter where the rupee appreciated against the dollar. So, the growth in the core business is definitely higher than the 0.3% that we see.

items.statement: Utilization at 82%, offshore ratio at 83%; building buffers for GenAI and Databricks CoE demand
items.quote: So, I think that utilization, we will watch it carefully, but we also want to make sure that we are not shortchanging on the supply front, right, and the availability of skilled people.

items.statement: Initial engagements convert to longer-term managed services contracts ~70% of the time
items.quote: In general, we are able to convert initial engagements, whether they are in a staff augment model or whether they are in a fixed fee, fixed scope model into longer-term managed services contracts in about 70% of the time.

items.statement: Hiring criteria: curiosity, self-starters, technical/algorithmic/domain expertise, consultative problem-solving; impact measured via voice of customer surveys
items.quote: We look for people who have an intense amount of curiosity because this is a very dynamic and evolving space. And unless people bring that kind of curiosity, it is very e asy to kind of stay close to just what you already know

items.statement: Targets ~26% CAGR to reach $200M revenue by FY28; expects to exceed 20% growth before end of current quarter
items.quote: The 3-year $200 million target calls for approximately a 26% CAGR. And as we just alluded to, I think at this point in time, there is a good deal of confidence that we should be able to go past the 20% kind of a number, even before the end of this

items.statement: Full-year consolidated margins targeted at 23-24% despite wage hikes and strategic investments
items.quote: See, like we mentioned, we want to keep the consolidated margins on a full year basis in that 23% to 24% sort of range. And then we are fairly confident that the impact of the wage hikes notwithstanding, we should be able to bring back the sort of margins to that level on a full year basis.

items.statement: Transaction-related costs to phase out by March 2026
items.quote: So to answer your first question, the transaction-related costs, I think that will sort of play out for the next 3 quarters. And therefore, you will see this getting fully phased out by March of '26, right?

items.statement: Other income expected to normalize to INR 17-18 crores per quarter going forward
items.quote: Yes, the other income should be going forward, in the range of INR 17 crores to INR 18 crores. Give or take, of course, that number could go up or go down depending on the yield that the treasury generates, but it should largely be in the range of INR 17 crores to INR 18 crores.

items.statement: Strong Databricks migration pipeline visible; expects significant uptick in data engineering opportunities over next 12-18 months
items.quote: In fact, only on Friday, I was reviewing the pipeline, right, that we have visibility into in terms of what Databricks is chasing and there is a whole host of migration opportuni ties that are in

items.statement: CPG business ex-Decision Point expected to return to growth trajectory on full-year basis based on current order book and pipeline
items.quote: But I would say on a full year basis, our CPG business [ex] of Decision Point, again, will be back on a growth trajectory. This is based on the order book and the pipeline that we are currently carrying.

items.statement: Macro headwinds persisting for 18 months; clients cautious on large production-scale GenAI engagements but data engineering demand expected to accelerate when uncertainty lifts
items.quote: At this point in time, I would say that while that interest and excitement is fairly significant, they are still being a little cautious in terms of signing up for the larger production scale engagements. And that is what should change once the move gets better in terms of the uncertainty in the macroeconomic environment.

items.statement: Technology vertical flat due to delayed follow-on deal signings; confident of returning to growth trajectory next quarter
items.quote: For technology, we are very confident that for the next quarter, we will sort of be back on the growth trajectory. And this quarter, while it was a flattish quarter, was largely because of delayed signing, follow-on work on the back of one-off projects that we had executed in the last quarter.

items.statement: BFSI growth driven by fintech and payments; larger banking relationships (European bank, large US consumer bank) expected to ramp in next couple of years
items.quote: The growth that we are seeing is more on the fintech and payments and that type of area, because that is where we have been stronger even in the past, though we worked with a fewer set of accounts.

items.statement: GenAI work mix of POCs/pilots and production engagements; building horizontal Center of Excellence with existing expert talent
items.quote: It's a combination. Obviously, GenAI, agentic AI being the new kid on the block, right, in terms of the buzz and the excitement. There will be a bunch of POCs, pilots and experimentation type of projects that are happening. But we are seeing instances where it's already moving into production with a longer-term kind of involvement.

items.statement: Added 7 new clients in quarter; 0.6% of 2.8% dollar growth from new clients, rest from existing logos
items.quote: See, the overall number of new clients that were added during the current quarter, I would say, was about 7 in total. In terms of the split of the growth, in terms of what came from existing clients versus new clients. So like I mentioned, right, in dollar terms for this quarter, we grew by about 2.8%. Of that 2.8%, I would say about 0.6% came from new clients that we added in the current quarter

items.statement: Europe traction in Financial Services and Consumer Goods; now 6+ clients across both sectors; relocated Decision Point key person to London
items.quote: We are seeing traction both in the Financial Services space and in the consumer goods space. I mean if you remember, a few quarters, a couple of quarters back, we had already started talking about that we want to double down only on these 2 industries in Eu rope. And at this point in time, I think we have upwards of half a dozen clients that we are working with in these 2 sectors put together

items.statement: BFSI competitors include IT services players with analytics solutions and pure-play data analytics firms; differentiated by innovative GenAI solutions
items.quote: I think the competitors will be fairly broad spectrum. I mean you can have anybody even the IT services players, right, if they have strong analytics solutions that they bring to the table. There are other pure-play data analytics companies as well, which do work in the Financial Services space.

items.statement: Planning investments in Databricks partnership and AI Center of Excellence; may impact margins short-term but targeting exponential revenue
items.quote: We are, at this point in time, planning for investments on the Databricks side as well as the AI, CoE side, right? I think while we have made some investments already, we are in the process of formulating one, setting up the team and also formulating the plan for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Completed 70% Decision Point acquisition payments; acquired additional 10% in current quarter; balance 20% payment due June next year linked to revenue and floor EBITDA performance
items.quote: In fact, in the current quarter, we have made the acquisition of another 10% in Decision Point. So, with this, in terms of payout, what will be payable, and this will happen around June of next year, is the payment for the balance 20%.

items.statement: Dr. Anindya Ghose joined as Independent Director; Board discussions focused on GenAI and agentic AI strategy
items.quote: You will all recall that Dr. Anindya Ghose has joined us recently as one of our Independent Director. In fact, he is here with us today and tomorrow, and we are going to be having some discussions specifically focused on the topic around GenAI and agentic AI.

items.statement: Sales cycles remain long with no let-up; growth dependent on pipeline conversion and macro improvement in specific areas
items.quote: In general, the sales cycles have been long right through this last 18 months and longer. And I don't feel let up on the sales cycles themselves. But given that some of these conversations were kicked up 12 months back, 18 months back, we are starting to s ee some of them coming through at this time

items.statement: Databricks targeting 60% CAGR; industry consensus estimates GenAI/agentic AI growth at 35-45% over next 5 years
items.quote: And everybody is talking about anywhere from 35% to 45%.

items.statement: Managed services model to continue; may see higher percentage of fixed-fee fixed-scope projects for architecturally mature clients
items.quote: I think managed services models will continue to be in vogue. I don't think they're going to get replaced by one-off fixed fee, fixed scope projects only. But there will, of course, be maybe a higher percentage of fixed fee, fixed scope projects that start happening.

items.statement: Intending to pare down investments in Europe subsidiaries due to transfer pricing changes; will reduce forex gains/losses volatility
items.quote: Our intention is to pare down or substantially trim the level of investments in Europe because of some of the transfer pricing changes that we have made. And therefore, we don't need that level of investment or debt to be sitting in the books of the subsidiaries.

items.statement: Formal alumni engagement program launched covering 3,500+ former employees; ex-clients and alumni returning as source of new business
items.quote: We are also extending this exercise to over 3,500 alumni that we have, who have passed through the portals of LatentView and who are currently working, right, in other organizations.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR144.8 crores as of June 30, 2025, including the INR137 crore EP-5 order
items.quote: Our order book as of June 30th, 2025, stood at approximately INR144.8 crores.

items.statement: Secured INR137 crore contract for mini-UAVs in fifth emergency procurement cycle after rigorous technical evaluation
items.quote: We are proud to share with the audience that as a part of this cycle, ideaForge secured INR137 crores contract for its mini-UAVs.

items.statement: L1 pipeline of INR400 crores expected to close within FY26 and FY27, with more additions expected
items.quote: Typically, the expectation is for it to close within this and the coming financial year.

items.statement: EP-6 emergency procurement round imminent with INR40,000 crores allocated, INR9,000 crores for Indian Army
items.quote: The government had already allocated INR40,000 crores to replenish and modernize the armed forces with cutting-edge solutions, out of which INR9,000 crores have been allocated to the Indian Army.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 61.7% in Q1 FY26 from 35.9% in Q4 FY25 due to mix of deliveries and service orders
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR7.89 crores compared to INR7.29 crores in the previous quarter, with a gross margin of 61.7% in this quarter and 35.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: ZOLT and YETI platforms on track for development; Q6 V3 and SWITCH V2 undergoing final evaluations before pilot production
items.quote: Our next generation of quadcopter and hybrid fixed-wing VTOL platforms, Q6 V3 and SWITCH V2 are undergoing final evaluations before moving to pilot production.

items.statement: ISR and CI-CT applications are top priority acquisition areas for Indian Army; command-level procurement will add to demand
items.quote: Intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance (ISR) and counterinsurgency and counterterrorism (CI-CT) applications are now the top priority acquisition areas for the India Army.

items.statement: Early Adopter Program in US with successful demonstrations to Homeland Security and DoD; structural movement in Africa for border security; European market opening due to NATO budget expansion
items.quote: In the United States, we have made significant inroads with our Early Adopter Program with multiple customers, and we have concluded successfully demonstrations with U.S. Homeland Security and the Department of Defence.

items.statement: Drone-as-a-Service showing green shoots in mining and infrastructure; contributes via product sales and direct services but smaller revenue share near-term
items.quote: Drone-as-a-Service is currently in a lot of scale-up mode. It's showing up in 2 ways. In some cases, there are partners in service contracts, where we win product contracts on the back of that.

items.statement: Expect improvement in working capital cycle from milestone-based payments and advances in EP contracts
items.quote: Definitely, as we continue to participate in some of these EP opportunities and all where we will get an opportunity to have bifurcated milestone-based payments. There will be advances also as part of these contracts.

items.statement: Self-sufficient cash reserves and debt facilities in place for execution of orders this year
items.quote: We can assure that we have self-sufficient numbers runway in terms of cash reserves as well as debt facilities in place for execution of any orders that get built in this year.

items.statement: No fresh fundraise being looked at presently
items.quote: Nothing is presently being looked at.

items.statement: EW-resilience capabilities validated in Army field evaluations; 700,000+ flights on systems provide reliability advantage; patents and IP create differentiation
items.quote: Our customers have done over 700,000 flights on our systems. And all of that experience goes into building the reliability onto the platforms, and that is carried over to not just our existing products, but also our future product developments.

items.statement: INR1 lakh crore RDI fund announced for deep-tech including drones; PLI 2.0 for drone industry expected
items.quote: The announcement of the INR1 lakh crores research, development and innovation (RDI) fund for companies working on cutting-edge technologies, including drones, is a strong policy signal that deep-tech is a strategic priority for the country.

items.statement: EP-5 order delivery timeline typically 12 months with 3-4 parcel supplies; accelerating delivery where possible
items.quote: Typically, any emergency procurement order comes with a 12-month timeline for delivery. And of course, in our case, we will -- we are accelerating the delivery to the best extent possible.

items.statement: NETRA 5 in final stages of industrialization; ZOLT and YETI technology demonstrators being built for Make-2 opportunities
items.quote: Also, NETRA 5 is in the final stages of the industrialization process. All these platforms have garnered interest during the Aero India 2025 from visitors all over the world.

items.statement: Key provider for Svamitva scheme mapping 660,000 villages; geospatial capabilities include LiDAR, multispectral, hyperspectral, oblique camera
items.quote: In fact, for the Svamitva scheme where the government of India is mapping all the 660,000-odd villages in the country using drones, we are proud to say that we are a key provider of the drone technology for that opportunity.

items.statement: Revenue recognition based on delivery chunks with advance payments; EBITDA loss narrowed to INR15.4 crores from INR17.41 crores sequentially
items.quote: EBITDA stood at negative INR15.4 crores compared to negative INR17.41 crores in quarter 4 FY '25.

items.statement: Revenue and profitability timeline depends on order book closure timing in Q3/Q4; EP-6 RFPs still in making, cannot quantify opportunities yet
items.quote: Lot will depend on what order book and timeline we close in which it's Q3 or Q4 and that will determine our deliverables as well as realization of the revenue as well for the year.

items.statement: Management expects strong growth and margin trajectory through FY26 with healthy demand visibility and capacity in place
items.quote: We expect the business to maintain strong growth and margin trajectory through FY '26, and we remain focused on discipline execution, innovation -led partnerships, and long-term value creation.

items.statement: Unit-3 Mahad capex increased from Rs 250 crore to Rs 300 crore; Rs 100 crore incurred, balance Rs 200 crore by FY27
items.quote: As a consequence of this high level of versatility and automation th at is being built into the Unit -3 Mahad, we envisage that the earlier planned CAPEX of Rs. 250 crores for Unit-3 shall increase to about Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex incurred was Rs 280 million
items.quote: In terms of CAPEX, during Q1, we approximately incurred an expenditure of 280 million.

items.statement: Unit-2 Phase 2 expansion fully operational; Unit-3 Mahad construction on schedule for H2 FY26 commissioning
items.quote: we completed phase 2 expansion in unit 2, which is now fully operational. Progress continues at Unit-3 Mahad, where the construction is on schedule for H2 FY'26 commissioning.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 60% for PI/CMI block at Unit-2; overall company utilization around 75%
items.quote: Currently, we are at 60% capacity utilization, and we believe we have the capability to capture any further uptick in demand should that happen in the near future.

items.statement: Plan to add 1,000 KL capacity over next 2-3 years via new large land parcel developed in three phases
items.quote: In the next two to three years, maintaining the same growth momentum, we plan to add another 1,000 KL capacity to keep in step with our aspiration, to keep in step with our medium-term goals, and to keep in step with the business commitments which have been backed by client lock-ins.

items.statement: Strong order visibility for cardiovascular intermediate and new contrast media molecules; 20 RFPs tracked with 6 in late Phase III/commercial
items.quote: Today at R&D, we are tracking about 20 new opportunities with high client interest and visibility. About 30% of these, which is approximately six, are in late phase III or commercial phase.

items.statement: Q1 gross margin 48.5% down 6.5% QoQ due to inventory drawdown (4.4%) and product mix (2.1%); normalized run-rate 53%
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 48.5%, down by 6.5% from 55% in Q4. I will explain the movement. If you notice in the P&L, there is a reduction in the finished goods and WIP to the tune of 750 million in Q1 as against an increase of 100 million in Q4 '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 34.1% in Q1 FY26, down 7% QoQ but up 173% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was at Rs. 1.2 billion or 34.1 of the sale, which is 7% sequentially declining, yet a 173% increase over Q1 last year.

items.statement: Healthy demand visibility across key customers; structural tailwinds from supply chain de-risking and complex API adoption
items.quote: Demand visibility across key customers is healthy. Capacity is now in place and product pipelines are expanding. In particular, we see structural tailwinds from de-risking of supply chains by global innovators, increasing adoption of complex APIs and NCE intermediates, growing traction in contrast media, especially with new molecules under validation.

items.statement: PI/API grew 8.2% QoQ, sweeteners 17.4% QoQ, contrast media dipped 3.9% QoQ due to phasing
items.quote: PI and API grew by 8.2% quarter -on-quarter, and we were able to sustain the momentum. Artificial sweetener grew 17.4% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting a recovery from muted historical perfor mance. Contrast media saw a 3.9% quarter -over-quarter dip, mainly due to phasing.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory reduced by Rs 75 crore QoQ due to customer dispatch schedules; inventory days down 131 days
items.quote: If you notice in the P&L, there is a reduction in the finished goods and WIP to the tune of 750 million in Q1 as against an increase of 100 million in Q4 '25.

items.statement: Cash and treasury instruments at Rs 2.7 billion; positive operating cash flows
items.quote: From a balance sheet perspective, we hold 2.7 billion in cash and treasury instrument and we continue to generate positive operating cash flows aligned with internal expectations.

items.statement: Fund raise plans at drawing room stage; shareholder resolution taken, options being evaluated
items.quote: We are still in the drawing room stage. We are yet to finalize anything. As and when we conclude on this, we will actually communicate. Right now, we have just taken a shareholder resolution and we are still evaluating the options.

items.statement: Company-level asset turnover north of 4x on net block; target 2.5-3x on gross block over next 5 years
items.quote: Overall, at a company level, because our capacities are fungible, let's not go product category -wise or business segment-wise. But at a company level, I think we have clocked one of the best in the industry north of four.

items.statement: 70% of energy consumption from wind and solar; carbon footprint consistently reducing
items.quote: We contribute about 70% of our overall energy consumption from wind and solar.

items.statement: Surrendered 8-acre land parcel in Gujarat (red category) to pursue larger land acquisition for future expansion
items.quote: Actually, our application has been for a much, much larger parcel. But today in the red category, Gujarat does not have too much of land. So, we got about 8 acres. We took that, but then we felt that that was subscale because now we have spotted and in the process of finalizing a much, much larger piece of land.

items.statement: No forward guidance given on gross margin or segment growth; quarter not good indicator for CDMO business
items.quote: We don't give guidance on the future. So, based on the current portfolio mix, it's going to be 53 and we will be in a position to sustain similar levels in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Cardiovascular intermediate scaling under long-term contracts with innovator; end molecule performing well in US, Europe, ROW
items.quote: The cardiovascular intermediate that we have in this block with the innovator has seen a huge uptick as compared to Q uarter 1 FY'25 and has shown consistent growth over the last several quarters as the end molecule is doing well in US, Europe, and ROW markets.

items.statement: New iodinated intermediate (ABA HCl) commercial in Q2; gadolinium-based products planned in Q1; backward integration for CMI KSM at Unit-3 Mahad
items.quote: In contrast media itself from an H2 perspective, there's this iodinated AB HCL that we spoke about. And there is the backward integration that we are doing. So, these are the two material launches.

items.statement: Focus on chronic segment CDMO; building blocks and peptide fragments for innovators and global CDMOs; not participating in generic space
items.quote: We don't wish to participate in the generic space. As far as your reading of our environmental clearance is concerned, while the advanced intermediate that we make for Bempedoic is just two steps away from the final API. But then many a times we give a laundry list of products because going back to the EC for amendments of the product list is not very convenient nor efficient.

items.statement: R&D team has specialized peptide synthesis capabilities; 45 peptide fragments developed with high client conviction
items.quote: We have a couple of scientists who are extremely good in this type of synthesis. As I mentioned, we are not in the catalogue business. As we speak, we are not venturing now. We already have about 45 peptide fragments which are already ready.

items.statement: Target 20% asset growth with secured mix moving to 72-73% by H1 and 80% eventually; unsecured to stay at 20%
items.quote: I really want to reiterate that the guidance given on 20% asset growth, we are certainly on track to meet that in the shape that we have always talked of, which is moving secured to 80%, while we would like unsecured to remain at 20%.

items.statement: Deposit growth target 20% with CASA at 20% share; cost of deposits to improve from Q2
items.quote: We do expect to certainly meet our 20% target on deposit growth with CASA at 20% and we would see the cost of deposit pricing getting positively impacted from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilise around 7.2-7.3% for FY26 including Q1 6.9%
items.quote: So we see around 7.2%-7.3% being the NIM, including the 1st Quarter 6.9%.

items.statement: Plan to open 70 branches in FY26: 30 new and 40 relocations; 8 added in Q1
items.quote: We plan to open 70 branches this year. We are conscious on cost, so 30 of these will be new branches and the bala nce 40 will be relocations of existing branches

items.statement: Secured assets headcount hiring largely done; only nominal additions in used car and 150-200 in gold
items.quote: We will see nominal cost growth in secured only when we are hiring in used car and marginal increase of about 150-200 people in gold.

items.statement: Customer yield steady at 16.5%; NIM compressed to 6.9% due to investment book churn and unsecured book decline
items.quote: The yield of the book continues to be 16.5%. However, NIMs are lower because a portion of our book, which we have sold at OMO, were at higher yield, our investment book, and the yield has come down.

items.statement: NIM expected to cross 7% decisively in Q2 as cost of deposits falls and unsecured book recovers
items.quote: As we go into Q2, we will see a drop in cost of deposits and cost of funding that should add to this number. And of course, with unsecured, gaining back the 2.5% loss of portfolio that should also make the NIM better and we should, if all goes well, certainly cr oss the 7% in a very decisive way

items.statement: Secured advances grew 3% in Q1; expected 12-13% growth by H1; unsecured declined 2.5% in Q1, seen flat to slightly up in Q2
items.quote: The total s ecured advances now show that in Q1 we have done 3%. This should show up to 12% -13% minimum when we finish this quarter

items.statement: Affordable Housing and Micro LAP book at Rs 12,000 crore; two-wheeler and gold loans performing well
items.quote: Our Affordable Housing, Micro LAP book is at Rs. 12,000 crore. If you take our secured book, we did have exit on ODFD roughly about Rs. 600 odd crore. If you take secured growth, excluding this ODFD, we are at 6%.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.8%, Net NPA 0.9%; secured PCR 69.1%, unsecured PCR 89.7%; 90% of provisions for unsecured
items.quote: Our gross NPA at 2.8%, net NPA remains at 0.9% with PCR, which is at 69.1% for the secured, which is on the higher side. But as you do accelerated provision, there are little choices left. You have to provision secured because secured is the biggest portion of our balance sheet. So naturally, when you really want to keep gross NPA, net NPA below 1%, you have no choice but to increase more secured

items.statement: MFI B0 collections: April 96.4%, May 98.9%, June 98.8%; July disbursements highest of the year
items.quote: So Shailesh, I will give you April B0 MFI collections around 96.4%. May was about 98.9% and June is 98.8% or 98.7%. So if you just see the April 3% odd drop in the B0 that has kind of been a challenge, which is why we say the significant drop of NPA will only happe n in Q3

items.statement: Deposit rate cut 50 bps from 8.25% to 7.75%; term deposit pricing declining; CASA growth expected double-digit by H1
items.quote: Exactly, it is 8.25% in March is now at 7.75%. So we have done a 50 basis point cut. We do expect to certainly meet our 20% target on deposit growth with CASA at 20% and we would see the cost of deposit pricing getting positively impacted from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Employee cost up 26.4% YoY and 7.3% QoQ due to prior hiring for collections and secured business plus annual appraisal; other opex flat
items.quote: Yes. So I think it is a fair question on cost, which is why Manish when we started the first slide itself, I said, our cost is going to be plateaued here or nominal increase in secured side because we are kind of fully loaded for the year. Yes, the first cost increase on the people side is the hiring we did in Q4 for collections and Q3 for collections last year. So they are flowing through into ou

items.statement: LCR at 171%, down from ~250% a year ago; liquidity comfortable; long-term borrowings from SIDBI, NABARD, NHB continue in small amounts
items.quote: For folks who have noticed it earlier on the deposit page, our LCR is at 171%. We did speak in the last few investor calls that we would like to normalize our LCR below 200% as the liquidity position impr oves. We are doing so

items.statement: Universal Bank licence application filed 9 June; active engagement with RBI; no adverse feedback; criteria largely BAU (NPA, net worth, capital adequacy)
items.quote: There is very active engagement. There is nothing that we have heard the problem. As you know, they have given a hurdle of who can apply. We have met the hurdle we have applied. We put a 5-year plan. There is active engagement and there is nothing which tells us now that there is anything different than what we knew 2 months back.

items.statement: Launched ASBA, Solitaire Savings Account for women, and iVanii digital soundbox app for merchants in Q1
items.quote: First quarter, we have seen 3 product focuses from us, which you can see on the right-hand side. One is our ASBA launch, second is a S olitaire Savings Account for women, and third is a digital offering called iVanii, which essentially is a soun d box for all the merchants and traders that they can use on their

items.statement: Cross-sell deepening: CASA, pre-approved business loans, gold penetration all rising per customer
items.quote: And as you can see very clearly from page 10 that whether it is CASA or pre-approved business loans or gold penetration, on every single parameter, there is more and more absorption of multiple products by customers across the bank.

items.statement: Two-wheeler expansion paced by city rollout (120 of 185 cities); 15-20% of book to existing customers; second-gen scorecard in use
items.quote: We operate roughly in 185 cities as a bank. And when we launched two-wheeler, we began with the first 30 cities, then we took it to 60 cities. I think the last I remember, we have put a stop around 120. We have not even reached the 180 cities that we are available in.

items.statement: NBFC lending book Rs 1,987 crore (6-7% of total) at ~12% yield; zero delinquency in 7 years; tactical use of surplus liquidity
items.quote: So first NBFC roughly around Rs. 1987 crore is like 6%-7% of our total book. Second NBFC has been not a single day delinquent, forget NPA in the last 7 years. So we are very mindful. If you watch our 1st Quarter last year also, see 1st Quarter is normally slow growth of assets and we tend to pick up the NBFC lending in the 1st Quarter, 2nd quarter, and then we slow down Q3, Q4, certainly because o

items.statement: Repo-linked book only 6%; 94% fixed rate; third-gen scorecard for Affordable Housing and Micro LAP going live next month
items.quote: The very marginal portion is repo-linked because we do give the customer at the end of 39 months to choose whether they want to continue fixed or they want to do a repo-linked. So 6% is repo-linked.

items.statement: MFI stress longer than expected; staying conservative on underwriting; accelerated provisions Rs 150 cr in Q1 (total Rs 450 cr) to keep net NPA below 1%
items.quote: We have increased our accelerated provision to Rs. 150 crore. This ensures that both gross NPA remains below 3%, net NPA remains below 1%, and we are well capitalized.

items.statement: BC book down 30% to Rs 1,500 crore; three BCs had NPA issues, one stabilised, two more by Q2; extra growth guardrails on BCs
items.quote: BC book has run down much faster than our book. As you can see, their book was around Rs. 2,500 crore is down to Rs. 1,500 crore. So Shailesh, t hey have dropped 30%, we dropped 10%. So their book has dropped much faster. And which is why they are, so that is one of the main reasons of gross NPA increase

items.statement: Long-term financing from SIDBI, NABARD, NHB in small amounts; ALM benefit from deposit tenure; no urgent borrowing need given high liquidity
items.quote: We continue getting long-term financing from SIDBI, NABARD, and NHB and we do take small amounts because, as you know, we are very liquid, so we don't really need to take too much borrowings any longer, though, given the cost of deposit and the length of deposit, which helps our ALM, we do take small amounts every now and then.

items.statement: Hired ~1,400 in secured business last year (Micro Housing, Affordable Housing, two-wheeler, supply chain); focus now on productivity
items.quote: we had invested in increasing our headcount in secured business last year, mainly in Micro Housing, Affordable Housing where we had added roughly about 1,400 people fresh last year. We had hired supply chain people, we had increased some more on the two-wheeler side. So the focus on the entire hiring that we did last year is on improving their

items.statement: PSLC income accounting changed to amortisation over 4 quarters; Rs 50 cr sale in Q1 yields ~Rs 18 cr per quarter in Q2-Q4
items.quote: There has been a change in accounting policy, normally on a PSLC, when we sell, we, till last year, were using the entire income in the 1st Quarter. From this year onwards, we are amortizing it into 4 quarters. So, there is another Rs. 50 odd crores of PSLC sale, which will come in quarter 2, quarter 3, quarter 4, roughly about Rs. 18 crore each.

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth expected at 21%-23% vs medium-term 24%-26%
items.quote: Due to heightened competitive activity, pricing on the acquisition, higher portfolio attrition and benign real estate market, AUM growth assessment for FY ‘26 is expected to be in the range of 21%-23%.

items.statement: FY26 OPEX to NTI expected flat at 20%-21% corridor
items.quote: OPEX to NTI is expected to be flat in the corridor of 20 %-21% in FY ‘26 in line with what we delivered last year.

items.statement: FY26 NII expected stable in line with FY25; NIM/NTI may moderate 15-20 bps
items.quote: NII is expected to remain stable and in line with FY ’25, while NIM or NTI may moderate by 15 -20 bps.

items.statement: FY26 ROA expected 2%-2.2%; ROE 11%-12% due to equity overhang
items.quote: ROA is expected to remain range bound at 2 %-2.2%, which is in line with our medium-term guidance and with ROE moderation of 11%-12% which is resulting from equity overhang of a capital raise done in FY ‘25.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross spread flat at 1.8% sequentially; NIM at 4%
items.quote: Gross spread for the quarter was flat at 1.8% on sequential basis with reduction in portfolio yield, which got offset with reduction in cost of funds. Net interest margin stood at 4% and that too was in line with Q4 FY ’25.

items.statement: Portfolio yield down 20 bps QoQ and 30 bps YoY to 9.5%; COF down 20 bps to 7.7%
items.quote: Portfolio yield reduced by 20 bps on sequential basis and 30 bps on Y-o-Y basis and stood at 9.5% in Q1 FY ‘26. While COF also witnessed reduction of 20 bps on sequential as well as Y-o-Y basis to 7.7% in Q1 FY ‘26.

items.statement: NIM compression of 5-10 bps expected for FY26 due to lower investment and assignment income
items.quote: Yes, it will moderate to 10 basis points roughly, 5 to 10 basis points.

items.statement: Product mix: HL 55.8%, LRD 20.4%, DF 11.9%, LAP 10.5%
items.quote: Portfolio mix continues to remain well diversified with HL mix of 55.8%, LAP of 10.5%, lease rental discounting at 20.4%, and DF at 11.9%.

items.statement: Home loans grew 21%, LAP 30%, LRD 29%, developer financing 32% YoY
items.quote: At product level, home loans grew by 21%, LAP by 30%, lease rental discounting by 29% and developer financing by 32%.

items.statement: Real estate market moderation and intense competitive pricing led to higher attrition
items.quote: Overall, Q1 was a balanced quarter with AUM growth of 24%, which was driven by moderation in real estate market , coupled with intense competitive pricing , resulting into higher attrition.

items.statement: Industry home loan disbursal growth virtually flat last 2-3 quarters per Bureau data
items.quote: Even when you look at the Bureau data for home loan disbursals in the last 2-3 quarters versus earlier, there is virtually no disbursal growth.

items.statement: Retail disbursements grew 12% YoY in Q1 despite industry flatness
items.quote: For Q1 versus last Q1 we would have a 12% disbursal growth as far as home loans are concerned.

items.statement: Lowest home loan rate offered at 7.49%; competition at 7.3%-7.35% from PSU banks
items.quote: The lowest range in the market today would be starting at 7.3.%, 7.35%, which is largely all public sector banks, going up to for the real prime customer, up to 7.75 %, 7.8%.

items.statement: LAP incremental yield ~100 bps above home loan; HL incremental yield 8.76% in Q1
items.quote: It will be roughly in the range of 9.7 to 9.9.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 21 bps QoQ to 7.7% due to lower incremental borrowing rates and repo transmission
items.quote: Cost of funds on sequential basis saw reduction of 21 bps and stood at 7.7% in Q1 FY ’26 versus 7.9% in Q4 FY ’25. This was owing to incremental borrowings at lower rate , coupled with repo rate transmission benefit on existing borrowing.

items.statement: Borrowing mix: money market 53%, bank borrowings 37%, NHB refinance 10%
items.quote: Borrowing mix remained well diversified between various instruments , where money market stood at 53%, bank borrowings at 37% and NHB refinance at 10%.

items.statement: NCD mix up 5% sequentially; bank borrowing down 4.5%; NHB down 0.4%
items.quote: NCD mix had inched up 5% sequentially, corresponding reduction in bank borrowing by 4.5% and NHB refinance by 0.40%.

items.statement: Annualized credit cost 16 bps in Q1 FY26 vs 17 bps normalized in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Annualized credit cost stood at 16 bps in Q1 FY ’26, against 5 bps in Q1 FY ‘25. However, if we exclude overlay release of Rs. 25 crores in Q1 FY ‘25, normalized credit cost would have been at 17 bps in Q1 FY ‘25. So, 16 bps in Q1 FY ‘26 versus 17 bps normalized in Q1 FY ‘25.

items.statement: Home loan GNPA 0.36% (+2 bps); LAP GNPA 0.61% (-4 bps)
items.quote: Marginal increment of 2 bps in home loans at 0.36% in Q1 FY ’26, while improvement of 4 bps in LAP at 0.61%.

items.statement: PBC ratio 61.71% vs regulatory 60% requirement
items.quote: PBC ratio, which is a principal business criteria for being an HFC as defined by the Reserve Bank of India was at 61.71%, higher than the regulatory requirement of 60%.

items.statement: RBI increased risk weight on top-up loans to 125%; no specific regulatory pressure on BHFL
items.quote: Reserve Bank of India had earlier guided all companies, all NBFCs, HFCs, banks to be cautious about top-up, and that is where they have increased the risk weight on the top-up loans from 100% to 125%. Apart from that we have not heard any other chatter recently or definitely not had any specific conversation with any regulator or supervisor, which is NHB in this case.

items.statement: Digital traction: e-agreement penetration 93%, digital onboarding 88% in June 2025
items.quote: Company’s digital initiatives continue to get traction with e-agreement penetration now at 93%, and improved penetration in digital customer onboarding journey now at 88% in June ‘25.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of north of 15% for FY26 maintained despite 5% growth in Q1
items.quote: we said for the whole year, we are anticipating to manage growth North of 15% in terms of revenue. I think that guidance still remains despite the fact that first quarter, we have grown only 5%

items.statement: Target to double business in 3-4 years and 2.5-3x in 5 years at 15%+ CAGR
items.quote: between 3- to 4-year type of scenario, you can definitely double the size of the business. If you look at 5 years, y ou have a chance to make it 2.5, 3x

items.statement: Piping segment to grow 15-17%, irrigation 12-14%, plastic sheet 8-10%, solar pumps substantial growth under KUSUM
items.quote: We see piping segment to grow quite a lot, maintain 15%, 17% growth. Definitely. We see irrigation to also maintain a 12% to 14% growth

items.statement: Overall EBITDA target 13-15% for FY26, Hi-Tech 15-17%, Plastics 12-14%, Agro Processing 12-13%
items.quote: overall idea would be to stay between 13% to 15%. I think 15% EBITDA on consol business combined, I think, would be a good level

items.statement: Hi-Tech Agri EBITDA improved from 15.2% to 16.6% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Hi-Tech business, we have been able to improve our EBITDA from about 15.2% to 16.6%.

items.statement: Agro Processing EBITDA improved by 1.6% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: in agro processing, EBITDA has improved by another 1.6%.

items.statement: Exports grew 40% from INR88 crores to INR130 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Overall, exp orts grew in this current quarter from the same period from INR88 crores to INR130 crores. So almost registering 40% growth has come in the exports

items.statement: Solar pump sales crossed INR50 crores in Q1 FY26 vs less than INR2 crores same period last year
items.quote: We crossed INR50 crores sales in the current quarter. So as against same period last year, it was hardly less than INR2 crores.

items.statement: Government project receivables of INR500-700 crores expected to be recovered by mid-FY26
items.quote: by mid-'26, we should receive most of old government receivables, and that is INR500 crores to INR700 crores

items.statement: Total project receivables ~INR750 crores, INR350 crores expected before March 2026
items.quote: overall amount on the project side is about INR750 crores approximately. And out of that, I think about at least INR350 crores should happen before March '26

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex INR44 crores vs depreciation INR68 crores; full year capex to remain in line with depreciation
items.quote: this quarter, capex - - overall maintenance plus growth capex was about INR44 crores, while depreciation was INR68 crores. For the rest of the year, maintenance capex would b e in line with what we have done in earlier years

items.statement: Existing capacity sufficient for 2-3 years growth in pipe and drip without serious capex
items.quote: normal pipe or drip, I think we can grow next 2 to 3 years without any serious capex, only maintenance capex we will do

items.statement: Plastic piping demand hit by early monsoon starting mid-May, lost 20-25 days of season
items.quote: volume because early monsoon starting from mid-May, we lost almost 20, 25 days of the season. So that was the reason of the reduction in the plastics volume

items.statement: Drip irrigation, solar pumps, tissue culture, plastic sheet exports showing strong demand
items.quote: Drip irrigation overall has done well. Pipe was down. Food was even. That is how I will say, different business segments have played out in total

items.statement: Resin prices deflationary but arrested over last 2-3 weeks, expected stable to firm for rest of year
items.quote: of deflationary pricing on commodities, whether plastics or food, at least on plastic side it seems to have been arrested over the last two, three weeks and indications based on certain scenario planning is that things would be stable to firm going forward

items.statement: Onion and mango prices at 5-7 year lows in Q1, impacting food processing revenue but may improve margins going forward
items.quote: Mangoes, I think we saw the lowest price in the last 5 to 7 years in this season. Now that also impacts your sales, right, because yo u're selling at lower price because the raw material has gone down so much

items.statement: Receivables and inventory increased in Q1 but 50% of incremental receivables recovered in July; DSOs to improve by March 2026
items.quote: Already in month of July, almost 50% of increment in the receivable, which we had in the June quarter has be en recovered in last four weeks. So I think it's a temporary short-term phenomenon

items.statement: Gross debt stable at INR3,590 crores; net debt up slightly due to working capital; INR250 crores long-term debt repayment due in next 9 months
items.quote: another INR250 crores of long-term debt is due for the repayment, which we should be a ble to do through internal accruals

items.statement: INR150 crores equity infusion from warrants (1/3 promoters, 2/3 institutions); no outstanding warrants; may raise more for working capital if needed
items.quote: This was also a quarter where we got the funds comi ng in towards the equity for the warrants, which we had issued earlier, almost to the tune of INR150 crores

items.statement: Food processing subsidiary IPO possible in FY27 at INR3,000-4,000 crores valuation vs INR600-700 crores investment
items.quote: depending on, again, preparation, the market underlying perfo rmance, sometimes in '26, there is a good possibility that you would see value monetization of that business
