items.quote: You've seen a sharp increase in our fixed price revenue. So that is one of the big contributors for this.

items.statement: No imminent weak spots seen in BFS, Insurance, TMT; macro uncertainties remain
items.quote: As we stand today, the answer is no, we don't see any of those weak spots. And I think our approach to dealing with any headwinds has been just sell our way out of that by actually creating deals using the propositions and differentiation.

items.statement: Bulk of Logistics client impact behind; recovery expected gradually through year
items.quote: We believe the impact from these is largely behind us, and we expect this vertical to gradually recover through the remainder of the year.

items.statement: EPS Rs 23.2, up 8.5% YoY; sequential impact from higher ETR due to minimum tax expenses in subsidiaries
items.quote: Our EPS of Rs 23.2 represents an 8.5% YoY growth. Sequentially, there was an impact from higher ETR due to certain ‘Minimum tax expenses ’ in certain subsidiaries, which we believe will normalize through the remainder of

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of 7%+ on average for the full year
items.quote: definitely, for -- as spoken earlier our margin guidance will be in the range of 7% plus on average for the whole year.

items.statement: Long-term target of 15%+ revenue CAGR and 20%+ profitability growth by 2030 with EBITDA margins above 8% and ROCE >20%
items.value: 15%+ revenue CAGR, 20%+ profit growth, EBITDA >8%, ROCE >20%
items.quote: We are aggressively scaling our net production capabilities, while expanding adjacent non -ferrous verticals, targeting over 15% value growth, revenue CAGR and profitability growth of 20% plus . These gains will be accompanied by meaningful margin expansion with a focus on achieving EBITDA margins above 8% and ROCE greater than 20%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex of INR 8 cr; additional INR 42 cr planned for remaining 9 months of FY26 (excl. Phase 1 capitalization of ~INR 75 cr)
items.quote: POCL invested INR 8 crores in Capex during Q1 FY '26 and plans to invest an additional of INR 42 crores over the remaining nine months of FY '26 .

items.statement: Phase 1 of 36,000 tpa lead capacity at Thervoykandigai commissioned in Q1 FY26 at 40-45% utilization; expected to reach ~70% in upcoming quarters
items.quote: Commercial production of Phase 1 of 36,000 metric tons per annum commenced in Q1 FY '26 with the plant operating at approximately 40% to 45% capacity utilization during the quarter . This is expected to increase to around 70% in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Phase 2 of 36,000 tpa lead capacity scheduled for commissioning in H2 FY26 with est. capex ~INR 20 cr
items.quote: Phase 2 of expansion is scheduled for commissioning in the second half of FY '26 with an estimated capital expenditure of approximately INR20 crores.

items.statement: Existing lead smelting capacity running at 90%+ utilization; overall existing plant utilization ~70%
items.quote: So the existing plants are running at in excess of about close to 70% . As far as the smelting capacity, smelting capacities are running at 90% plus and overall at 70%.

items.statement: Copper capacity currently ~6,000 tpa, targeting 90%+ utilization in FY26; expansion to ~12,000 tpa by end FY26, targeting 90%+ utilization in FY27
items.quote: The copper capacity end of '26 will be about 12,000 tons . Currently, we are operating at approximately 6,000 tons, which is in the process of expansion as well.

items.statement: Clear order visibility for specialized lead alloys via annual contracts signed from Q1 FY26
items.quote: See, we sign annual contracts . And starting this first quarter, we have signed the annual contract for these alloys as well, and we have a very clear visibility through the year for these alloys .

items.statement: Lead-acid battery demand growing ~3% globally and ~6% in India; expected to stay relevant for 8-10 years
items.quote: as of now, the growth in terms of the lead acid battery segment is still in excess of 3% globally and in India, still at about 6% .

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin >7% (record), PAT margin 4.6%; driven by operational efficiencies (1-1.5% margin impact) and higher VAP share (0.5-1% impact)
items.quote: EBITDA margins exceeding the 7% mark represent a significant milestone in POCL journey towards long -term sustainable value creation . This increase is due to increased sale of value-added products and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Lead EBITDA/ton jumped 48% YoY to INR 16,898; sustainable run-rate guided at 7%+ blended margin
items.quote: EBITDA per ton of lead increased significantly by 48% to INR 16,898 per tonne on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Lead VAP share rose to 71% in Q1 FY26 vs 50% YoY and 58% QoQ; target 60%+ for full year
items.quote: The percentage of value -added products in lead segment stands at 71% compared to 50% and 58% on a Year-on-Year and Q-on-Q basis.

items.statement: Copper margins currently 4-4.5%, expected to improve with forward-integrated value-added products
items.quote: currently, I mean, as what we are doing right now about 4% to 4.5% levels of margin is what we are looking at, which will be enhanced as we add some forward integrated value-added products.

items.statement: Fully hedged back-to-back model; lead price changes have negligible impact on EBITDA margins
items.quote: in terms of our margins, we run a completely hedged model . So in terms of percentage, the impact is hardly any impact because our raw material versus our sales are completely hedged.

items.statement: Lead scrap sourcing: ~80% imported, ~20% domestic in Q1 FY26; procurement diversified across continents (each 15-20%), Africa <5%
items.quote: At present for import, it is 80%, 20% is domestic we are buying.

items.statement: Plastics segment moving to own premises from leased; rent saving ~INR 17 lakh/month (INR 2 cr/yr) to turn EBIT positive from next quarter
items.quote: The rent we want to stop it . Already, we have given vacation notice . So probably from the next quarter onwards, that substantial amount of rent will be saved and we move to our own premises automatically that segment will come to the positive .

items.statement: Cash ~INR 52 cr (incl. QIP & warrant proceeds); gross debt ~INR 122 cr as of 30 Jun; net debt <INR 100 cr
items.value: Cash INR 52 cr, Gross debt INR 122 cr, Net debt <INR 100 cr
items.quote: So the cash at bank as of today is about INR 52 crores. This comprises of both the QIP money, which is pending to be utilized as well as the warrant proceeds, which we have received during this quarter. The overall debt in our books of accounts, as of 30th June is about INR 122 crores. So net debt is less than INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Battery Waste Management Rules (BWMR) enforced; penalization pending; reverse charge mechanism notified but low threshold limits limit impact; GST rate reduction to 5% under discussion
items.quote: So BWMR is being enforced . And the only part now that is -- I mean, the notifications are out, the only part that is left is the penalization part of it, which is -- right now, the industry stakeholders are opposing that because, of course, they do not want to get into the penalization part.

items.statement: Informal sector share reduced from 20-30% to ~60% formalized over time; further shift expected over 2-3 years as RCM/GST changes reduce informal incentives
items.quote: Already that percentage has gone up from 20%, 30% to now it is moved to 60% -- informal sector is reduced now. It has moved to the formal sector . So over the period of time, that will be reduced further.

items.statement: Export revenue split: Lead ~65% of sales (INR 328 cr in Q1), Copper 7% export; Geography: Southeast Asia 75-78%, Middle East balance, Europe <5%
items.quote: Europe is marginally -- Europe is below 5% . Southeast Asia would contribute to about 75% to 78% and the balance would be a part of it to the Middle East and other parts.

items.statement: Specialized lead alloys sold to international customers under annual contracts; NDA prevents product/customer disclosure
items.quote: Yes. These are mainly international customers.

items.statement: No acquisition plans; proprietary lead recycling technology superior to unorganized players; organic expansion preferred
items.quote: we are not looking at these small acquisitions of other companies because right now, the kind of technology that we have installed in our plant is one of its kind in India, and I'll say probably one of its kind globally also with our new lead operations.

items.statement: No near-term risk from customers building in-house lead recycling; global trend shows large battery makers have had internal recycling for over a decade
items.quote: I mean we do not see a risk because if you look at the global trend that has been there and many of the large battery makers have their own internal battery recycling capacities, even to a lot of customers that we are currently supplying as well have their internal battery recycling capacities for over a decade.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated: Revenue +35% YoY, EBITDA +78% YoY, PAT +94% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, also POCL reported a strong financial performance . Revenue from operations, EBITDA and PAT increased by 35%, 78%, and 94%, respectively, Year-on-Year basis.

items.statement: Lead production +17% YoY to 24,167 MT; Lead sales +9% YoY to 22,530 MT; Copper production 1,107 MT; Plastics 808 MT
items.quote: The production in sales of lead has increased significantly by 17% and 9% to 24,167 metric tons and 22,530 metric tons on a year -on-year basis .

items.statement: Lithium-ion recycling: evaluating chemistries (NMC, LFP, LMFP) with tech partners; no concrete plan/capex yet; decision in few months
items.quote: we are currently in discussion with many of our technological partners in terms of identifying the chemistry because there is -- this industry is quite fast moving.

items.statement: Aluminium segment: revenue expected from Q2 FY26; products linked to existing portfolio; slight delay vs earlier timeline
items.quote: Yes, it is in progress and we will have some numbers on the aluminium segment in this second quarter and the work is in progress for the same as updated earlier. There is a slight delay on that, but in the second quarter you will start seeing the numbers.

items.statement: Revenue target of $2 billion by end of FY27, implying 19-20% CAGR
items.quote: We remain committed to our goal of reaching 2 billion dollars by end of FY27.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to remain in 22.5% to 23.5% range for the year
items.quote: We expect our overall effective tax rate for the year to remain in the range of 22.5% to 23.5% going forward.

items.statement: Margin improvement target of 200-300 bps by FY27 from FY25 exit level
items.quote: We have mentioned in the past that it needs to be improved by 200 -300 basis point by the time we reach FY27.

items.statement: Macro environment cautious with slower decision-making; pipeline healthy but not quantified
items.quote: The environment has been cautious. Decision making has been slow. If the environment becomes a little bit better and not just for us, for everyone, I think things will be easier.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical impacted by tariff uncertainty and federal funding cuts (DOGE), driving vendor consolidation and offshoring
items.quote: People looking at alternative plans, people looking at even supply chain movements and so on and so forth. So, there is definitely stress because of the tariff part and we will see where it resolves.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBIT margin at 15.5%, down 10 bps QoQ; ESOP cost lower by 230 bps, offset by earn-out reversal absence (60 bps), onsite retention and delayed ramp-ups (100 bps), higher amortization (40 bps), and adverse currency (40 bps)
items.quote: All these put together resulted in a net decrease of 10 basis points in our EBIT margin sequentially.

items.statement: Wage hike postponed by a quarter due to uncertain business scenario
items.quote: In view of the current uncertain business scenario, we have decided to postpone our wage hike by a quarter.

items.statement: ESOP cost reduction to remain flat for next couple of quarters before further decline
items.quote: That reduction has already happened. Now, this will continue to remain flat for the next couple of quarters before you'll see further reduction.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 TCV at $520.8M with new bookings TCV of $337.0M; ACV at $385.3M with new bookings ACV of $211.8M
items.quote: The Total Contract Value (TCV) for the quarter stood at USD 520.8 million, with TCV of new bookings coming in at USD 337.0 million.

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio moderated to 1.3-1.4x from historical 1.5-1.6x; executable order book tracked internally
items.quote: What you don't see and what we measure ourselves is the executable order book.

items.statement: Top 5 customers grew 22.8% YoY, top 10 20.2%, top 20 23.1%, top 50 22.7%, top 100 22.4% in USD terms
items.quote: This quarter, we witnessed healthy year-on-year growth in US dollar terms among our various client buckets, with the top 5 customers' revenue growing by 22.8%, top 10 by 20.2%, top 20 by 23.1%, top 50 by 22.7%, and top 100 by 22.4%.

items.statement: Billed DSO improved to 56 days (-2 QoQ), unbilled DSO to 20 days (-3 QoQ); operating cash flow to PAT at 98.6%
items.quote: In this quarter, billed DSO came in at 56 days, an improvement of 2 days compared to the last quarter while unbilled DSO came in at 20 days, an improvement of 3 days compared to the last quarter. Our operating cash flow to PAT for Q1 FY26 stands at 98.6%.

items.statement: RoCE (ex-cash) improved to 43.8% from 38.7% YoY (+510 bps)
items.quote: Return on Capital Employed (RoCE), excluding cash from capital employed for Q1 FY26 came in at 43.8% versus 38.7%, an improvement of 510 basis points from the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Headcount at 25,314, up 746 QoQ and 1,821 YoY; trailing 12-month attrition at 13.9% vs 11.9% YoY
items.quote: At the end of Q1 FY26, our total headcount stood at Rs. 25,314, an increase of 1821 resources from Q1 of previous fiscal year and 746 quarter on quarter. Trailing 12-month attrition, this quarter came in at 13.9% compared to 11.9% in Q1 last year.

items.statement: Launched SASVA 3.0 with 55+ patents (up from 35); platform used for engineering productivity, tech modernization, and agentic AI across verticals
items.quote: The innovations in SASVA are powered and backed by 55-plus patents across data intelligence, AI infrastructure, productivity, autonomous agents and security, up from 35 in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy focused on tuck-in capability-led deals; scaled acquisition only if good asset in Europe to reach 15% revenue share in 2-3 years
items.quote: Most of these would be capability-led, smaller acquisitions. The only place where we would do a scaled acquisition would be if we get some good asset in Europe.

items.statement: Forward contracts outstanding at $440M at average rate of Rs. 86.90/USD; FX gain of Rs. 188.7M this quarter vs loss of Rs. 154.3M last quarter
items.quote: Forward contracts outstanding as of June 30, 2025 were 440 million US Dollars at an average rate of Rs. 86.90 per dollar.

items.statement: Total cash and investments improved to Rs. 307.8 crore on better collections
items.quote: On the back of better collections, our total cash and investment saw an improvement this quarter and stood at Rs.307.8 million as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: No forward-looking guidance given; growth dependent on macro improvement and pipeline conversion
items.quote: We don't give forward-looking guidance, so I'm not going to give you a number per se. All I can say is, if you look at the overall growth, it was 3.9% in USD terms.

items.statement: Margin trajectory includes continued investments; some cost normalization benefits may be reinvested rather than flow to margin
items.quote: On the way as we grow our company, we have to also make investments. So, some portion of that will get back into investments.

items.statement: 15th IPO anniversary celebrated with NSE closing bell ringing on July 24, 2025
items.quote: This quarter, we are proud to be ringing the closing bell at the National Stock Exchange tomorrow, that is July 24th.

items.statement: Targeting 12-15% net area addition annually with 1-2% closures, expecting at least 65 net new stores in FY26
items.quote: Our guidance remains unchanged. We are targeting 12% to 15% net area addition annually, with 1% to 2% closures, which will be normal closures in any year. This year, we should see a net addition, therefore, of around at least 65 new stores.

items.statement: Expecting healthy consistent same-store sales growth and at least 13-14% additional square feet area in FY26
items.quote: consistent growth rate from the same-store, and we should be doing that as we hav e been performing in the past quarters. We should also open up stores. There is big pipeline, which is getting built in by the team. There's a lot of store identification that has been done. So, we are on the path to open at least 13% to 14% of our square feet area -- additional square feet area in this year

items.statement: Consumer sentiment positive but not bullish; expecting growth during festival season with strong undercurrent
items.quote: Customer sentiment in in Bharat market, looks okay. I would not call it as a very high customer sentiment in terms of consumption. But yes, it's positive. It's not too bullish as of now because the period and the seasonalities are such. But we expect it to grow during festival. This is definitely something we are seeing the undercurrent is very strong.

items.statement: Expecting better Q2 as festivals preponed; Durga Puja 7-10 days earlier should improve September
items.quote: July seemed a little slow, but it should immediately come back in August and September, when the festival starts coming in right from Raksha Bandhan. So we are expecting a better Q2 because the festival will move in a little bit. The Pujo, the Durga Puja season is a little preponed of 7 to 8 or 10 days. We should expect a little better September month or the second half of the September month.

items.statement: Gross margin ex-LimeRoad improved 60 bps to 34.8%; total gross margin up 10 bps to 35.3%; focusing on rupee gross margin over percentage
items.quote: Our gross margins, excluding LimeRoad, improved by 60 bps to 34.8% on the back of better full price sell-throughs and liquidation of old inventory, which released provisions. Total gross margins, however, improved marginally by 10 bps to 35.3% due to the 48% decline in LimeRoad's revenue contribution, which flows entirely into the gross margin line.

items.statement: EBITDA margin ex-LimeRoad 14.9% (+80 bps YoY); total EBITDA margin 14.3% (+170 bps YoY); LimeRoad losses reduced 56%
items.quote: Excluding LimeRoad, we delivered an EBITDA margin of 14.9%, which is 80 bps higher year-on-year, driven by operational efficiencies. Including LimeRoad, where the EBITDA losses reduced by 56% year-on-year, our total EBITDA grew by 27% and margin improved by 170 bps to 14.3%.

items.statement: Conservative on percentage EBITDA margin guidance; focusing on rupee margins and higher full-price sell-through rather than percentage margins
items.quote: We are definitely -- right now, as you rightly said in the beginning, quarter 1 has not really been a very good start in terms of the SSG. While we are hoping that quarter 2, quarter 3, we should get better results. But at the same time, we are also trying to rework our product strategy and our margin strategy, and we are looking at higher rupee margins rather than percentage margins.

items.statement: YTD capex INR 30 crores primarily for new store openings and refurbishments
items.quote: YTD capex stood at INR 30 crores, primarily towards new store openings and refurbishments. We continue to invest in expanding the store base and refurbishing existing older stores, and the results are visible through sustained footfall and sales momentum.

items.statement: Targeting 12-15% net area addition annually; on track for expansion cycle with big pipeline built
items.quote: We are on the path to open at least 13% to 14% of our square feet area -- additional square feet area in this year. So that is what we are on to and we are on target. We are on track as far as our expansion cycle is concerned.

items.statement: Total apparel ASPs grew 1% (V-Mart +2%, Unlimited -3% due to value-led shift); Unlimited ASPs to converge toward V-Mart over time
items.quote: The total apparel ASPs grew by 1% with 2% growth in V-Mart, and a conscious decline of 3% in Unlimited due to the ongoing shift towards more value-led offerings.

items.statement: V-Mart prices 15-20% lower than urban value retailers like Style Union and Yousta on average
items.quote: We definitely are a little more mass retailer. And our price point of similar items should be at least 15% to 20% lower. That's our goal. That's our expectation.

items.statement: Seeing competitor aggressiveness from national (Zudio) and regional (V2) players; organized retail share growing
items.quote: We definitely have seen a lot of competitor aggressiveness coming in from all the sites, right, from the national competitors, like Zudio's and others and from the regional competitors, or even the larger regional competitor like V2 growing aggressively. So, there's been a lot of store openings.

items.statement: Quick commerce impact limited to ~20% of locations with muted growth/degrowth in some towns; not significant for V-Mart
items.quote: Exactly, I would not call out that for 80% of the locations. But yes, maybe 20% of the locations, I could see some discussions happening. There is some muted growth or degrowth as well in certain towns where we are seeing an aggressive penetration of these quick commerce.

items.statement: Working capital utilization back to INR 35 crores; expect average INR 90-100 crores for full year; inventory 93 days (5% improvement)
items.quote: On the liquidity side, working capital utilization, which had temporarily spiked in quarter 4 is now back to INR35 crores, while this may go up in quarter 2 due to seasonal stocking, but we expect it to remain within a comfortable range of average around INR90 crores to INR100 crores for the entire year.

items.statement: Inventory INR 818 crores at 93 days (5% YoY improvement); aged inventory provision down from 1.7% to 0.7%
items.quote: We closed the quarter with inventory of INR 818 crores, translating to 93 days, which is a 5% improvement over last year. Per store inventory increased marginally, but remained healthy. The provision for aged inventory came down significantly from 1.7% last year to 0.7% this year this quarter, reflecting better inventory health

items.statement: No long-term debt; free cash flow INR 109 crores in Q1; well positioned to fund growth through internal accruals
items.quote: We generated INR 109 crores in free cash flow this quarter, largely due to efficient inventory management. There is no long-term debt as we have always maintained, and we are well positioned to fund future growth through internal accruals.

items.statement: Normalized same-store sales growth 5% in Q1 (both V-Mart and Unlimited contributing equally); North states strong, East region challenged near Bangladesh border
items.quote: Adjusting for the preponement of Eid, which fell in quarter 4 this year instead of quarter 1 like last year, the normalized SSG came at 5% with both V-Mart and Unlimited contributing equally. From our regional standpoint, the North states of Rajasthan, Uttarakhand performed much better, while the Eastern region continued to face some amount of cha llenges, particularly around the Bangladesh border

items.statement: Expecting higher single-digit same-store sales growth over next 3-4 quarters; building merchandise plan on last 4 quarters' numbers
items.quote: Very difficult to give you a number-driven answer -- but yes, we are positive. We are definitely building our business plan, our planning, our sourcing, our buying plan from the number that we had displayed in the last 4 quarters. So, we definitely believe there should be a little higher single-digit same-store sales growth that we should be expecting in the next 3, 4 quarters.

items.statement: Good customer repeat rates and NPS scores; positive feedback from employees; governance principles strong
items.quote: We've got very good customer repeat rates. We've got very good feedback from our customers in the NPS scores. So, we have seen good consistent feedback from employees. So, we believe our governance principles are good.

items.statement: US tariff policies shaking export market; seeing risk in relying on large vendors; spreading vendor base
items.quote: The exports also seems to get opened up market -- the tariff policies of U.S. have really shaked the market. So, we saw some risk coming in, which I also highlighted in the last call to last call and last call. So, we don't want to really bank too much on key vendors and top vendors.

items.statement: Bangladesh border disruption impacting Eastern region footfall; major disruption started 3-6 months ago
items.quote: there is an impact that we can see in our business one because also there's a large consumption, which also happens from Bangladesh, and that's one consumer set, which has stopped coming completely. So, in the eas tern part of India, especially, we see a lot of those consumers also are an active consumer to some of -- a lot of our stores. So, we've seen some drastic downfall in their footfall and

items.statement: Omni/digital business integrating well; costs reducing, efficiencies improving; tracking breakeven not just revenue growth
items.quote: Other than t hat, I think we definitely have a clear strategy for our online digital business that digital business is becoming more omni. That is definitely -- the omni piece is getting integrated well. The costs are being reduced. The efficiencies are being generated . There is more that we are trying to generate with less. We don't believe in just tracking the revenue growth. We are tracking th

items.statement: Debt reduction target of INR 60 crores for FY26 now looks unlikely given Q1 performance
items.quote: That is definitely our intent. Given the way the first quarter has happened at this point, that looks unlikely. I would to definitely call it out.

items.statement: Current debt level stands at INR 306 crores as of Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, current debt level is INR 306 crores.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was negative INR 5 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: It was negative around INR 5 crores.

items.statement: Budgeted spend on new initiatives for FY26 is INR 75 crores
items.quote: So, when we started the year, we had budgeted around at INR 75 crores, which is higher than what we had spent last year because we knew that the big four broadcasters will come in.

items.statement: Accelerated inventory charge-offs of INR 35 crores per quarter expected to continue through FY26, totaling ~INR 140 crores
items.quote: So, if I have to just extrapolate that, it would be around in the region of INR 140 crores of accelerated amount that we will be taking in this financial year.

items.statement: Traditional media revenues declined 26% YoY in Q1 FY26 due to Free Dish broadcaster entry and FMCG ad softness
items.quote: Traditional media revenues for the quarter stood at around INR 72 crores, which declined by 26% year-on-year.

items.statement: Digital media revenues grew 18% YoY to INR 67 crores in Q1 FY26 driven by YouTube, ShemarooMe and Syndication
items.quote: Digital media revenues for the first quarter stood at around INR 67 crores, growing by 18% year-on-year.

items.statement: Advertising monies redistributed 15-25% across channels due to Free Dish viewership shifts from new broadcaster entry
items.quote: So basically, there has been a redistribution of viewership. So as a result, what has happened is, the overall ad spend in Free Dish platform s have not come down, but the advertising monies have also got redistributed according to the viewership changes. So that is what has happened. I mean, it depends on which channel has got hit so much and so on and so forth. But largely, at an overall level,

items.statement: ShemarooMe Gujarati released six new titles in Q1 FY26 including movies, web series and plays
items.quote: ShemarooMe Gujarati released six new titles during this quarter, featuring a diverse mix of movies, web series, and plays.

items.statement: YouTube flagship channel Shemaroo Filmi Gaane crossed 72.5 million subscribers; portfolio garnered over 10 billion views in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On YouTube, our flagship channel Shemaroo Filmi Gaane crossed a significant milestone of 72.5 million subscribe Across our entire portfolio of channels, the company garnered more than 10 billion views during the quarter, underscoring the sustained strength of our digital engagement with the audiences.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain under pressure due to ongoing accelerated inventory charge-offs started six quarters ago
items.quote: However, margins are expected to remain under pressure due to the ongoing accelerated inventory charge -offs, a strategic initiative we began six quarters ago.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic about seasonal pickup in advertising spend in upcoming quarter supported by festive season and digital viewership momentum
items.quote: We rema in cautiously optimistic about a seasonal pickup in advertising spend in the upcoming quarter, supported by the festive season and strong viewership momentum in our digital platform.

items.statement: Inventory reduced from INR 568 crores to INR 528 crores in Q1 FY26, a reduction of INR 40 crores net of additions
items.quote: To give you just the numbers, we closed March '25 at INR 568 crores of inventory. June, we stand at INR 528 crores. So, about INR 40 crores reduction in the inventory and which includes net of further additions, etc.

items.statement: Rationalizing costs for select channels, repositioning others, and reinforcing investment strategy across content portfolio
items.quote: These include rationalizing costs for select channels, repositioning others to better align with audience preferences, and reinforcing our investment strategy across the content portfolio.

items.statement: Entry of four major broadcasters on Free Dish caused viewership redistribution without expanding total Free Dish viewership
items.quote: The impact is largely around what has happened, with the entry of the four new broadcasters, the viewership numbers have not increased. It is not that new viewers have come to the Free Dish platform. So what has happened is, overall, GRCs in the Free Dish platforms have got redistributed.

items.statement: Syndication business is lumpy with deals in pipeline expected to materialize over next three quarters
items.quote: But there are a lot of deals in pipeline, so it will happen sometime over the future in the next three quarte rs So that is something which will get

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; focus on strengthening balance sheet through operational efficiencies and cash flow management
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain focused on strengthening our balance sheet, driving operational efficiencies, and positioning the company to unlock substantial long-term value.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to remain between 55% to 60% in coming quarters
items.quote: Now you can say as the contribution from CDMO business increases, we expect the gross margins will remain between 55% to 60%. That's what we expect in the coming quarters.

items.statement: ARV revenue guidance maintained at INR2,500 crores plus or minus INR200 crores for full year
items.value: INR2,500 crores plus or minus INR200 crores
items.quote: When it comes to ARV, we are telling we'll be around INR2,500 crores plus or minus INR200 crores. We have visibility there.

items.statement: CDMO revenue contribution has potential to touch 50% in near to medium term
items.quote: Currently, the CDMO contributes over 30% of our revenue. We expect it will continue to grow. In the near to medium term future, we expect it has the potential to touch 50%. That's our guesstimate.

items.statement: INR5,000 crores capex planned over next 5 years in Vizag, funded primarily through internal accruals
items.quote: As we indicated before, we are going to invest INR5,000 crores in the next 5-year time. I think internal cash flows will be sufficient to take care of it.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex investment of INR265 crores
items.quote: On the capex front, we invested close to INR265 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Microbial fermentation Phase 1 Greenfield project at Vizag with 400 kiloliter capacity expected online by end of 2026
items.quote: The plan is to create over 400 kiloliter capacity in Phase 1, which is expected to go online by the end of 2026.

items.statement: Gene therapy and antibody-drug conjugate GMP facility at Shameerpet moved to Hyderabad Genome Valley with 6,000 square meter facility

items.statement: Virtually term-loan free; ~INR 200 cr working capital debt; targeting debt/EBITDA <1x and debt/equity <1x even with expansion

So in terms of debt to EBITDA, we will be comfortably below 1 and we will always try to achieve this number

items.statement: Among few domestic SS flat product makers (Jindal Stainless, Shyam Metalics, 2 others); differentiated by thinner gauges (0.26mm), faster delivery (5-6 days), non-wash galvanizing tech
items.quote: We will be the first in India to make 0.26 mm of stainless steel coils with integration and supply it to the market.

items.statement: SS coil pricing at ~1% discount to market leader; captive power (16MW WHRB + 9MW AFBC) and raw material proximity (coal/iron ore within 200-250km) support cost advantage

items.quote: Capacity utilization of pre-galvanized and stainless steel coils division has improved significantly.

items.statement: Monsoon seasonality impacts Q2 demand; management targeting flattish Q2 volumes vs Q1
items.quote: Definitely there will be an impact of monsoon because we get seasonality, in particular monsoon seasonality is there in our demand.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 440 cr used for debt repayment, working capital, expansion, general corporate purposes

items.statement: All projects on track for timelines, safety, quality, budget

items.quote: So, to answer to €300 million, which we had projected and how is it going to ramp up? Well, as you know, it all depends on the vehicle that is launched already.

items.quote: On non-operating income side, we had supported the group companies in specific projects, which was charged out to them based on the transfer pricing policies of the group.

Also, as higher tariffs have been imposed on some of the key t yre exporting countries, India is well positioned to increase its export share.

items.statement: Orion plant closures in Europe and North America (estimated 250,000-300,000 tons) create opportunity for PCBL as supply-demand gap grows
items.quote: Our sense is that it could be somewhere around 250,000-300,000 tons.

items.statement: Carbon Black EBITDA per metric ton at INR17,791 in Q1 FY26; margins similar across domestic and international markets

items.statement: Aquapharm Q1 FY26 sales volume 26,523 MT (9% YoY growth)

items.statement: Carbon Black feedstock cost gap vs Chinese competitors narrowed to ~USD 130/ton

items.statement: Aquapharm freight cost impact ~INR6 crores in Q1 due to geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: The impact of freight cost is around INR6 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: New Specialty Black line in Mundra to include ink and coating grades

items.statement: Global carbon black capacity additions ~300,000-400,000 tons/year historically, primarily in Asia/India
items.quote: every year about 300,000-400,000 tons of new capacity get added.

items.quote: Recently, we have been granted a process patent by the U.S. Patent Office on our proprietary method of developing nanomaterials designed for next-generation energy storage technologies.

items.statement: PCBL targeting international market growth; Europe and U.S. key geographies subject to tariff situation; logistics cost higher for U.S.

items.statement: Management focusing on working capital management improvement to strengthen financial performance amid uncertainty

items.quote: Top 5 would contribute maybe around 7% or 8%. We have a very wide base of customers. So there's no one customer taking more than 1.5%, 2%.

items.statement: Yarn expansion expected revenue INR450 crores at full capacity
items.quote: So INR235 crore CapEx will all give you a revenue of around INR450 crores.

items.statement: Management targets employee cost at 10-12% of revenue on a yearly basis.
items.quote: See, our target is, if I can talk about the range, it would be between 10-12% on a yearly basis. That is what we are targeting as of now.

items.statement: Management expects finance cost to reduce by 5-6% going forward, dependent on cash generation and global rate cuts.
items.quote: So, if I talk about a range, we will reduce it by maybe 5-6% more going forward. But that will take time, and that will depend on the cash generation to which we are committed.

items.statement: Management aims to reach ~70% capacity utilization to achieve 18-20% EBITDA margin, as demonstrated 2-3 years ago.
items.quote: One part we have guided in the past is that as we move this back towards around 70% utilization, we are confident of getting to that 18-20% EBITDA margin, and we have demonstrated that in the past about 2 -3 years ago.

items.statement: Global optical fiber demand projected to grow ~2% YoY in 2025 after two years of decline, led by North America (~11.6% CAGR) and Europe.
items.quote: According to CRU, global optical fiber demand is poised for a turnaround in 2025 with a projected close to 2% year on year growth after two years of continuous decline.

items.statement: China Mobile tender of 98.8M fiber km and Unicom 68.5M fiber km signal aggressive network expansion, supporting demand recovery.
items.quote: The latest China Mobile tender also highlights a robust fiber demand in China, surpassing expectations, with close to 98 point 8 million fiber kilometers announced, well above the CRU research estimate of 80-85 million.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 order intake was Rs 1,529 crore, nearly 3x YoY and QoQ, including a 3-year European telecom contract and strong North American inflows.
items.quote: In Q1FY26 we clocked Rs.1529 crores in order intake, nearly 3x from Rs.566 crores in Q1FY25 and Rs. 588 crores in Q4FY25.

items.statement: Open order book rose to Rs 4,888 crore in Q1 FY26 from Rs 4,378 crore in Q4 FY25; Rs 722 crore slated for Q2 execution.
items.quote: Our open order book rose to Rs. 4,888 crore in Q1 FY26 up from Rs. 4,378 crore in Q 4FY25 reflecting strong order inflow and market confidence. Of this, Rs.722 crore of order book is slated for execution in Q2 with balance Rs.4166 crore scheduled for FY26 and beyond.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 13.7% (Rs 140 crore) from prior year, driven by US geography mix and cost optimization.
items.quote: Our profitability has also improved meaningfully as EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.140 crore, with margins expanding to 13.7% . This marks a significant year-on-year improvement and underscores the progress we have made on operational efficiency and cost optimization.

items.statement: Optical networking business Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin was 14.3% (Rs 137 crore), reflecting significant improvement from previous year.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarters Rs.137 crores with a margin of 14.3% reflecting a significant improvement from the previous year.

items.statement: US tariff impact partly offset by customers; margin improvement continues despite tariff headwinds.
items.quote: There has been an impact of tariff, definitely, but that has been partly offset by customers there. The US is a market wherein it is quicker in terms of absorption of any cost which is going there. So, there is a slight impact. We cannot tell you the number as of now, but that looks promising.

items.statement: US factory utilization improving quarter on quarter and will continue to improve through the year; above 25-30% level.
items.quote: in the US . I n terms of utilization of that factory that is improving quarter on quarter and certainly will continue to improve through the course of this year

items.statement: Completed capacity expansion over last 3-4 years; no new major capex indicated, focus on sweating existing assets.
items.quote: We have the capacities we have invested in the capacities over the last 3-4 years, and that is just on the cable side.

items.statement: Enterprise and data center business contributed 23% of revenue in Q1 FY26; new STS data center portfolio and multi-core fiber launched.
items.quote: 23% of our revenue came from a growing enterprise and data center business in the past quarter.

items.statement: Optical connectivity attach rate stable at 23%; target to improve with recent product launches and market recovery.
items.quote: While our optical connectivity attach rate remains stable at 23% with recent product launches and market recovery signs in focused markets, we expect to improve these metrics further.

items.statement: STL Digital added 4 marquee clients in Q1, total 30 global customers; signed multi-year contracts with two Middle East healthcare providers.
items.quote: In Q 1 we added four more marquee clients, taking our total to 30 global customers, and we signed multi -year contracts with two leading healthcare providers in the Middle East.

items.statement: Revenue diversification: Europe 49%, Americas 31% in Q1 FY26; strong order inflows from top-tier North American and European telecom operators.
items.quote: Europe led our performance with a 49% contribution in Q1 while the America s strengthened to 31% , reflecting robust growth.

items.statement: Global market share in OFC (ex-China) improved to 7% from 6% in Q1 FY25 per CRU data.
items.quote: As per CRU data our market share has improved year on year in the global OFC market outside China, to 7% from 6% in Q1FY25.

items.statement: UK FTA neutral to positive; STL already a leader in UK market selling duty-free from India.
items.quote: From STL perspective, we were already serving the UK market, quite actively from India. We are probably one of the leaders in the UK market with our cable and connectivity portfolio. This does not change anything for us in that sense.

items.statement: US-China tariff dynamics and potential India-US tariffs (est. 10-20%) create opportunity for India-based manufacturing; STL's US factory well-positioned for 'Made in America' requirements.
items.quote: if you look at the recent announcements, the expectation is that it is somewhere between 10-20% is what we are seeing in the domain, if you look at Indonesia or other countries. Our guess is as good as yours in terms of where this finally lies. But we are very proud that we have proactively set up this factory and expanded that factory in the US.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 1,300 crore, debt-to-equity 0.64x, net debt/EBITDA 2.3x; target to bring net debt/EBITDA below 2x.
items.quote: In line with our expectations, net debt stands at Rs. 1300 crore with debt-to-equity ratio of 0.64x and net debt to EBITDA at 2.3x . We are focused on bringing this below 2x going forward.

items.statement: STL Networks demerger approved; listing expected by end of August 2025.
items.quote: We are currently progressing towards listing its shares with necessary regulatory approvals. We expect this listing by the end of August.

items.statement: Employee cost increased 10% QoQ to Rs 156 crore due to investment in leadership for data center and international markets; target 10-12% of revenue yearly.
items.quote: this increase reflects our investment in building strong leadership across high growth areas like data center and international markets. With this launch recently, we had to have a team fully set up and aligned to demonstrate revenue growth as well.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III execution visibility low; MAF submitted with some winners, volumes uncertain for another quarter.
items.quote: So, probably another quarter or so will be able to give you a better update as the execution for these projects starts kicking off.

items.statement: Multi-core fiber and quantum key distribution commercialization early stage; will take time despite strong interest from hyperscalers and government.
items.quote: We are very early in the market here. There is strong interest from hyperscalers and other telecom operators, but the commercialization will take some time.

items.quote: We have given deposits in the range of 8% to 10%. It is now 9.26%.

items.statement: Advance growth guidance 10-12% for FY26; actual Q1 YoY 11.50%
items.quote: Advance, we have given guidance of 10% to 12%. It is in the range of 11.50%.

items.statement: CASA ratio guidance around 40% for FY26; Q1 domestic CASA 38.97%
items.quote: CASA, we have given guidance of around 40%, but our endeavor will be to maintain that 40%.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance <3% for FY26; Q1 at 3.01%, may go to 2.5%
items.quote: Our gross NPA guidance of less than 3%, we will deﬁnitely achieve, I mean, maybe we can go even up to 2.5

items.statement: Net NPA guidance 0.1-0.7% for FY26; Q1 at 0.18%
items.quote: Net NPA, same range, 0.1%, 0.7%, 0.65%.

items.statement: NIM guidance 3.15-3.30% for FY26; Q1 domestic NIM 3.23%
items.quote: NIM, we have given guidance of 3.15% to 3.30%. We are at 3.23%.

items.quote: ROA, we have given guidance of 1.20%, but we have been able to maintain at 1.34%.

items.quote: recovery from NCLT, we have given guidance of Rs. 800 crores. But in this quarter, itself, we have been able to recover Rs. 451 crores from one NCLT account.

items.statement: AUC recovery guidance Rs 2,000 cr for FY26; Q1 recovered Rs 815 cr
items.quote: we have also given guidance of AUC of Rs. 2,000 crores, but we have been able to recover around Rs. 815 crores already in this quarter itself

items.quote: we have given guidance of between Rs. 5,500 crores to Rs. 6,500 crores. We have been able to recover Rs. 2,059 crores in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Domestic NIM fell 13 bps QoQ to 3.35% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Domestic NIM has come down from 3.48% to 3.35%. That means there is a decline of 13bps.

items.quote: Cost of deposit there is marginal increase from 5.10% to 5.14% because repricing of deposits is yet to happen, part of that will start from this quarter.

items.statement: Expect further margin reduction in Q2 FY26 but full-year NIM guidance 3.15-3.30% intact
items.quote: Yes, yes there will be, there will be some margin reduction further.

items.quote: quantum of margin decline will reduce from this quarter onwards because bulk will also start repricing, and we have also gone for revision of rate in retail term deposit.

items.quote: Gross NPA has come down from 3.77% to 3.01% on YoY basis, that means a 76bps reduction and QoQ basis, 8 bps reduction. Net NPA has come down on a YoY basis from 0.39% to 0.18%, 21bps reduction and on QoQ basis, 1 bps reduction from 0.19% to 0.18%.

items.statement: Slippage ratio 0.94% in Q1 FY26 vs 1.09% in Q4 FY25 and 1.50% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Slippage ratio, in last June it was 1.50%, now it is 0.94%. For the quarter ended March, it was 1.09%.

items.quote: SMA -2, which was more than Rs. 5 crores, which was Rs. 4,586 crores as of June-end, 30th June. Now it is only Rs. 815 crores.

items.statement: PCR 98.20%; credit cost 0.28% in Q1 FY26 vs 0.81% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: PCR ratio is 98.20%. Credit costs have come down substantially from 0.81 % to 0.28%

items.statement: Total sanctions Rs 88,000 cr in Q1 FY26 vs Rs 60,000 cr in Q1 FY25; corporate sanctions Rs 27,000 cr in Q1 vs Rs 18,000 cr in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In last year, it was Rs. 60,000 crores, now this year, so far, it is Rs. 88,000 crores in the first quarter itself, we have been able to achieve.

items.statement: RAM grew 15.93% YoY, 3.52% QoQ to Rs 3.63 tn; retail 16.52% YoY, agri 16.4% YoY, MSME 14.45% YoY
items.quote: RAM has grown by 15.93% YoY and QoQ, it is 3.52% and reached to Rs. 3.63 trillion. Retail has grown by 16.52% YoY and 3.83%, QoQ and reached Rs. 1.24 trillion. items.statement: Corporate credit marginally degrew 1.41% QoQ but grew 1.77% YoY; private capex demand still weak
items.quote: Corporate credit has grown; on QoQ basis, it has marginally degrown by 1.41%. However, YoY, there is 1.77% growth.

items.statement: Hiring ~3,000 freshers in FY26 including specialized roles in cybersecurity, IT, risk, forex
items.quote: Manpower, also, we are around 3,000 fresh hiring will happen in this year. So out of that part will be in a specialized sector, like we are also going for cybersecurity, IT sector, risk management, Forex officer.

items.statement: Bulk deposits Rs 1.45 lakh cr (50% maturing within 1 yr); retail term deposits Rs 2.5 lakh cr with Rs 86,000 cr repricing in 3-6 months
items.quote: my retail term deposit is around Rs. 2,50,288 crores. So out of that, Rs.86,000 crore is repricing in the next three months to six months.

items.statement: External benchmark linked loans 40.46% of book; 1-year MCLR linked 41%; EBLR transmission immediate, MCLR transmission lagged
items.quote: my MCLR book is 52% and, external benchmark linked is 40.46% and within MCLR, 1-year MCLR-linked is 41%.

items.statement: Private banks aggressive in MSME and export-oriented units; corporate lending mostly PSU banks
items.quote: certain segments like MSME, we are seeing good competition from the private sector banks and certain export-oriented units, there also we are seeing very high competition

items.statement: CASA ratio challenge to maintain ~40% due to govt JIT adoption and savings shifting to alternatives
items.quote: CASA moving up will be really a challenge on two counts. One, government is also adopting JIT in many states. And this pace of increasing JIT will further increase only. And number two, if you see where people are shifting their saving to other alternates also.

items.statement: Further 50 bps rate cuts could require NIM strategy rework beyond 3.15-3.30% guidance
items.quote: if as you are saying another 50 happens, then of course then we will have to think about our NIM strategy. So, how we can protect at least whatever guidance we have given. We will have to rework that.

items.statement: Target gross addition of 1,000 rooms by March 2026
items.quote: Overall, I do believe our goal of gross addition of 1,000 rooms by March-end, which is March 26, I think we stand firm on that, and I think there is a very good pipeline of resorts which will be back-ended towards the second half of the year.

items.statement: Current inventory base of 5,800 keys with five ongoing Greenfield and Brownfield projects
items.quote: Our current inventory base is about 5,800 keys. And I think as I mentioned the pipeline for the future is very, very strong.

items.statement: Pipeline visibility of 65% to 70% for doubling inventory journey
items.quote: If I take all of that, I think today's visibility is probably between 65% to 70% of that journey.

items.statement: Industry ADR up 7% YoY in May with high occupancy levels despite geopolitical impact
items.quote: If I look at the metric of ADR, for example, in May, it was up 7% YoY compared to last year, I think there was some seasonal softening, but overall, I think the occupancy levels continue to be very high.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded to 39%, PAT margin expanded 680 bps
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR161 crores, up 42% and our EBITDA margin expanded to 39%. PAT was at INR76 crores, up 69% YoY, and our PAT margin expanded by almost 680 bps.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 22%, consolidated PAT up 18% YoY despite INR28 crore forex impact
items.quote: Our consolidated income was INR740 crores, up 8% YoY, and our EBITDA was INR161 crores, which was an improvement of about 16% versus Q1 of FY'25. Our EBITDA margin stood at 22%.

items.statement: Resort occupancy at 85%-plus despite highest ever inventory addition last year
items.quote: Despite that, I think we have got an occupancy level of about 85%-plus. And I must add that this is on the back of added inventory. I think we added our highest ever inventory in the last financial year.

items.statement: Average Upgrade Revenue (AUR) at INR8.3 lakhs, up 69% YoY
items.quote: We added about 1,524 members at an overall level. Our AUR is at INR8.3 lakhs, up 69% YoY.

items.statement: Digital and referral channels now 65% of total member additions
items.quote: Member additions through the digital route and referrals, I think continue to grow; now it is 65% of total member additions, while upgrades have been stable at about INR56 crores.

items.statement: Shorter tenure products (5-year) 42%-47% of mix, blended tenure 12-13 years
items.quote: If I look at what we define as shorter tenure products, they are about anywhere between, I would say given the quarter between 42% and 47% overall. But the blended mix will probably take us to between 12 and 13 years, right?

items.statement: Focus on selective customer acquisition and right product-market fit, 48 focused destinations
items.quote: The third thing we did was, as we did this, we reduced our spread geographically, which meant that today we have, I think, about 48 focused destinations, and I think it was a much larger number.

items.statement: Standalone cash position improved to INR1,576 crores as on June 30, 2025
items.quote: Our cash position also improved to INR1,576 crores as on 30th June 2025.

items.statement: HCRO occupancy improved 10% to ~55% in Q1, Finland hotel average ~45% for April-May
items.quote: I know that occupancy went up 10% to about 55% or so is the number I have.

items.statement: Government investing INR20,000 crores in 50 destinations with state partners
items.quote: I think there is INR20,000 crores investment in developing 50 destinations with state partners. All of these are helping set the base for this industry on a longer-term basis.

items.statement: F&B price hike implemented, rental income and experiences driving resort revenue growth
items.quote: So, I think from our perspective, I think both of these will continue to drive. So, I think in the resorts, the journey here is driving the experiences piece much more sharper.

items.statement: Employee expenses flat while serving more guests, sales and marketing costs optimized
items.quote: So, if you look at the bridge, I think what we have been able to do well is look at leverage on our employee expenses, right? So, we are serving more on the same employee expenses base, right?

items.statement: HCRO turnaround depends on Finnish economy recovery and Russia-Ukraine geopolitical resolution
items.quote: So, from our perspective, see, it is difficult to put a timeline because it depends on largely extraneous factors. So, if you look at, as I said, the economy is expected to recover through the course of the year. On the geopolitical situation, the Russia-Ukraine situation, I think that is something to wait-and-watch.

items.statement: Sustainability: biodiversity assessment at 4 new resorts, solar at 41% of demand, 15 MW cumulative
items.quote: I think we have completed biodiversity assessment at four new resorts, increased solar installation to 41% of total demand and an overall cumulative installation of 15 MW.

items.statement: Tech transformation underway: contactless check-in piloted at 2 resorts, service quality focus
items.quote: For example, we are piloting a contactless check-in process in two of our resorts. We are also looking at quality of service at the resort level and how do we actually anticipate member needs much better.

items.statement: No plans to sell HCRO, strategic options only later, focus on operational efficiency
items.quote: So, as I have said in previous calls, I think at this point in time, I think the focus is on operating the business at an efficiency level. I think the strategic options we will only think later is what I would say.

items.statement: Views Airbnb/SaffronStays as potential partners not competitors, different traveler segments
items.quote: And the last thing I would do is, I think I do think these have probably potential partnership opportunities rather than competitive situation. And that is the current state of mind in terms of looking at all of these options.

items.statement: Member additions unlikely to accelerate until sales transformation journey completes in few quarters
items.quote: So, in my mind, I think the member addition will probably not accelerate till we reach a point in time where we are completing this journey, and that also is something which I think will take a few more quarters.

items.statement: Incremental inventory growth to be capital-light, owned share to drop from ~45% to 25-30%
items.quote: And I think incrementally, as we go forward, I see that swinging to maybe only 30% owned or even less than that owned.

items.statement: Resort revenue INR114 crores with double-digit growth
items.quote: I think even this quarter we have reported double-digit growth in resort revenue and delivered about INR114 crores of revenue from the resorts.

items.statement: No debt or funding needs mentioned for India business, HCRO requires no incremental cash
items.quote: We don't anticipate any funding needs for that business at this point, and even that continues to be stable.

items.statement: Credit cost guided at 2-2.05% for FY26
items.quote: I'm saying at an overall level, we should come at a credit cost of about 2%, 2.05%. This is broadly what we had guided earlier as well.

items.statement: NIM expected to restore to ~5.8% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: So, we feel that by Q4, margins should broadly restore back to what we posted last quarter and only caveat there is there could be, still some rate cuts, which could sort of kick in.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 65% for FY27
items.quote: And we have already guided on cost -to-income ratio of 65%, which we are targeting for FY '27, but still hope and belief is that we should try to come in

items.statement: Opex growth guided at 11-12% near term
items.quote: So operating expenses, we will continue to sort of moderate, and it should stay in the range of about 11% to 12% that kind of growth in the near term as well.

items.statement: NIM moderated 24 bps QoQ to 5.71% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The net interest margin on AUM for the quarter moderated by 24 basis points to 5.71%.

items.statement: Cost of funds declined 9 bps QoQ to 6.42%
items.quote: Connected point, the cost of funds for the quarter was at 6.42%, and this declined by about 9 bps during the quarter.

items.statement: Peak FD rate cut from 7.9% to 6.75% (115 bps reduction)
items.quote: We were earlier paying 7.9%, at the peak, when the money was tight, I think during March or something. And now we brought down to 6.75% as the peak rate, which is almost a reduction of 115 basis points.

items.statement: GNPA rose to 1.97%, NNPA to 0.55% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Gross NPA of the bank increased marginally from 1.87% in March to 1.97% in June. Net NPA correspondingly increased from 0.53% in March to 0.55% for June quarter.

items.quote: In absolute terms, MFI, SMA pool was at INR315 crores at June '25, and this has declined by 59% post peaking out in December quarter. We have also seen an improvement in collection efficiency for MFI during the quarter, which stood at 99.0% as against 98.1% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Ex-MFI gross slippage ratio 3.54% in Q1, marginally above 4-quarter average of 3.35%
items.quote: Gross slippage ratio during the quarter, excluding microfinance stood at 3.54%, which was marginally higher than 3.35% witnessed on an average in last 4 quarters put together.

items.statement: Customer deposits crossed INR2.57 lakh cr, up 26% YoY; retail deposits crossed INR2 lakh cr
items.quote: Our customer deposits, in fact, crossed the INR2.5 lakh crores milestone and was at INR2.57 lakh crores at June. Similarly, retail deposits crossed INR2 lakh crores mark. The growth in customer deposits was very strong at 26% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved sequentially to 48%; CASA deposits grew 30% YoY
items.quote: If we talk about the CASA ratio, that also improved sequentially and touched 48% at June. The CASA deposits in value terms grew strongly at about 30% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Credit-to-deposit ratio improved to 93.4% from 98.1% YoY; incremental CD ratio 75.8%
items.quote: We continue to bring down the credit-to-deposit ratio that is now down to 93.4% at June '25. This was at 98.1% in June of last year. In fact, incremental CD ratio for last 1 year is at 75.8%.

items.statement: Added 14 branches in Q1, total branch count now 1,016
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 14 more branches, and that takes the branch count to now 1,016.

items.statement: Repaid INR2,600 cr high-cost legacy borrowings; residual stock INR2,200 cr maturing this year
items.quote: We also repaid high-cost legacy borrowings of INR2,600-odd crores in the current quarter. Happy to report that the residual stock is just now INR2,200 crores and majority will mature in this year itself.

items.statement: Credit card spends grew 35% YoY; 3.8 million cards issued
items.quote: We have now issued 3.8 million credit cards. The spends on the credit cards were quite healthy, and it grew by about 35% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Core operating profit (ex-trading) improved 7.8% QoQ to INR1,744 cr
items.quote: Core operating profit, excluding trading gains, improved by 7.8% sequentially to INR1,744 crores.

items.statement: Repo rate pass-through: Feb/April cuts partly in Q1, June cut largely in Q2
items.quote: So, let me further clarify. Generally, say, a repo is changed on a particular month, there is a cycle. So, if a customer's loan will get reset once in 3 months. So, it depends on when his last change happened. So that's how the transmission will happen through the quarter.

items.statement: No material asset quality shock expected; 50 bps credit cost increase ruled out
items.quote: Do we think any product of the bank would take us that zone? The answer is no. Do we expect our H2 to be in a credit cost average book? In fact, we think could be better than H1.

items.statement: Growth driven by business finance (INR22k cr), vehicle loans (INR5.2k cr), mortgages (INR8.4k cr)
items.quote: So, if you take a full 1-year Y-o-Y, you could see that INR22,000 crores has come from business finance, which is basically wholesale banking loans, business banking, working capital, CV/CE, etcetera, etcetera. So that's INR22,000 crores. And then INR5,200 crores is coming from vehicle loans growth and INR8,400 crores is coming from mortgages growth.

items.statement: MFI book to bottom out around INR7,500 cr; will grow in line with industry thereafter
items.quote: our own thinking is that probably it will bottom out at about INR7,500-odd crores. It's currently about INR8,500 crores. Sudhanshu Jain: Yes. V. Vaidyanathan: Yes, like there. And then from there on, wherever industry grows, we'll probably keep in line with

items.quote: Non-interest income for the period stood at Rs . 447 crores, down from Rs . 509 crores in the previous quarter. Recoveries from written off accounts amounted to Rs. 78 crores, compared to Rs. 182 crores in the prior quarter.
